90161e64dafc87b58878cb8afff11e94e90d4179.title: Compact summary closure
90161e64dafc87b58878cb8afff11e94e90d4179.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning level.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathcal M\) be the class of full-data probability laws satisfying the uniformly conditioned model with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), let
\[
\mathscr S=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\},
\]
and let \(\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\) be its closure in the finite-dimensional summary space. For summaries \(s,q\), write
\[
d_S(s,q)
=
\|s.M_0-q.M_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|s.M_1-q.M_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|s.N_0-q.N_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|s.N_1-q.N_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\Bigl(\sum_i (s.m_X(i)-q.m_X(i))^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
Then there exists \(B\in\mathbb R\) such that \(d_S(s,0)\le B\) for every \(s\in\mathscr S\). Moreover, \(\mathcal K\) is compact, and \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal M\) is nonempty.

1ac39a4a36c7328e9ec66fe651438008b5ae5b97.title: Total Borel repair
1ac39a4a36c7328e9ec66fe651438008b5ae5b97.body:
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), \(k\le d_z\), and \(n\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed constants.)} \(L\ge 1\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\item \textbf{(Calibration.)} \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and \(C_0\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Empirical summary.)} The empirical-summary map \(\widehat S_n\) in \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}\) is Borel measurable.
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathcal K\) be the \(d_S\)-closure of the admissible summary image. Then there exists repair data \(R\) of the form described in \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\), with Borel selector \(\Pi\), continuous extension \(\overline F\), and associated estimator \(\widehat\nu_n=\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\) on \(\mathcal K\), such that \(\widehat\nu_n\) is Borel measurable. If \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), then for every sample the repaired estimator is the unit point mass \(\delta_0\). Moreover, for every sample the retained summary-inversion set
\[
\begin{cases}
\{\delta_0\}, & \mathcal K=\varnothing,\\
\{\nu:\exists q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le 2r_{n,\alpha}\ \text{and}\ \nu=\overline F(q)\}, & \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(r_{n,\alpha}\) is the simultaneous concentration radius, is nonempty.

8e737440d2904c7404761d471e80fe1f25b97fbd.title: Gap-free modulus extension
8e737440d2904c7404761d471e80fe1f25b97fbd.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent dimension.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Set
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal M\) be the collection of probability laws satisfying the uniformly conditioned model with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), let \(S(P)\) denote the observable summary of \(P\), and let
\[
\mathcal K=\overline{\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\}}.
\]
For summaries \(s,q\), write
\[
d_S(s,q)=
\|M_0(s)-M_0(q)\|+\|M_1(s)-M_1(q)\|
+\|N_0(s)-N_0(q)\|+\|N_1(s)-N_1(q)\|
+\left(\sum_i (m_X(s)_i-m_X(q)_i)^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Then there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\), depending on
\((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), such that, for every \(P,Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
W_1(\nu_P,\nu_Q)\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(S(P),S(Q)),
\]
where \(\nu_P\) is the quotient \(k\)-atomic latent-effect probability law of \(P\) on
\([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\). Moreover, there is a continuous and Borel measurable map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
such that, for all \(q,q'\in\mathcal K\),
\[
W_1(\overline F(q),\overline F(q'))\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q'),
\]
and, for every \(Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
\overline F(S(Q))=\nu_Q.
\]
This extension is unique among continuous maps \(G:\mathcal K\to
\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) that satisfy the same \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\)-Lipschitz bound and agree with \(Q\mapsto \nu_Q\) on every admissible summary \(S(Q)\).

a276c50bc09651097d7ae142fe1b3ea909b67e9e.title: Observed VMW margins
a276c50bc09651097d7ae142fe1b3ea909b67e9e.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P\) be a full-data law for \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) as defined in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).
\end{itemize}
Then all of the following hold. For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0,
\]
and, writing \(M_t(P)\) for the observed conditional \(ZX^\top\) moment in arm \(t\),
\[
M_t(P)
=
A_t\,
\operatorname{diag}\!\left\{P(U=u,T=t)/P(T=t):u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\right\}
B^\top .
\]
Moreover, for every orthonormal signal basis \(V\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) spanning the signal space of \(S(P)\),
\[
\sigma_k\!\left(M_t(P)V\right)=\sigma_k\!\left(M_t(P)\right),
\qquad
\pi_0\sigma_0^2\le \sigma_k\!\left(M_t(P)V\right).
\]
The stacked observed proxy moment also satisfies
\[
\pi_0\sigma_0^2
\le
\sigma_k\!\left(
\begin{bmatrix}
M_0(P)\\
M_1(P)
\end{bmatrix}
\right).
\]
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\|M_t(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,
\qquad
\|N_t(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,
\]
and the target-proxy mean satisfies
\[
\|m_X(P)\|_2\le L.
\]
Finally, with \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and each \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
|Y(t)|\le L_\tau/2
\quad\text{almost surely under }P\text{ conditional on }U=u,
\qquad
|\mu_{tu}|\le L_\tau/2,
\qquad
|\tau_u|\le L_\tau .
\]
The same law \(P\) belongs to the published VMW parameter class represented by the published scope handle.

2f18a84e47a044b29c0951b937c97c1b473ef673.title: Ordered weight upper bound
2f18a84e47a044b29c0951b937c97c1b473ef673.body:
Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope and margins.)} \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant
\[
C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0
\]
such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), one can choose a measurable nearest-summary repair construction on the \(d_S\)-closure \(\mathcal K\), with its continuous extension \(\overline F\) and nearest selector \(\Pi\), and the associated ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:labeled-weight-estimator}\) satisfies the following bound.  For every gap scale \(g\) with
\[
0<g\le \frac14,
\]
uniformly over every full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M(g)\),
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
  \left\|\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1
\right]
\le
C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]

13ba4bda131e540f6cbf9d724a0255ec8115c5db.title: Honest root-n confidence
13ba4bda131e540f6cbf9d724a0255ec8115c5db.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\) and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), there are constants \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) and \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}>0\) for which the following holds. With
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
the constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is the prescribed structured-lattice constant
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
={}&\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\bigl(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f\bigr)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}\,L}{\sigma_0}
+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}}.
\end{gathered}
\]
For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\), summary-space repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\), and a prescribed structured lattice in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set}\), such that for every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set}\), formed using \(C_0\), \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and \(\widehat\lambda_n\), satisfy the following assertions.

For every sample, both sets are nonempty, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) admits its constrained finite-transport representation around \(\widehat\lambda_n\):
\[
\nu\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\nu\in\mathcal P_{\le k,\pi_0}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\ \text{and there exists a transport plan from \(\nu\) to \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with cost at most \(R_{n,\alpha}\)}.
\]
For every full-data law \(P\) satisfying the model conditions in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\nu_P\in \mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For every sample,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le
4C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le
2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

df7827a91bd50a838cbfdc73003534e342252761.title: Collision-uniform root-n rate
df7827a91bd50a838cbfdc73003534e342252761.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Set
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
Then there is a constant \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), there exist two total Borel estimators
\[
\widehat\lambda_n,\widehat\nu_n:
(\{1,\ldots,n\}\to O_{d_x,d_z})\to
\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
with the following properties.  The estimator \(\widehat\nu_n\) is the nearest-summary repaired estimator \(\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\) supplied by \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\).  The estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is represented by a finite structured-lattice list together with a first-minimizer rule: the list consists exactly once of every well-formed structured lattice point at radius \(L_\tau\), is ordered by the lattice lexicographic order, and \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the effect law of the first listed minimizer of the structured-lattice criterion with penalty scale \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) evaluated at \(\widehat S_n\).

For every \(0<\eta<1/2\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\max\left[
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P),
W_1(\widehat\nu_n,\nu_P)
\right]
>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}
\le \eta .
\]
Moreover, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\{N_{t,n}=0\}\le (1-k\pi_0)^n .
\]

4d4dc00002158af2f14204f7efaf027590d5d165.title: Same-class quotient minimax
4d4dc00002158af2f14204f7efaf027590d5d165.body:
For the submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), let
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0=80\sqrt 2 .
\]
There exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\) with \(0<c<C\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\),
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
  W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal M\) is the uniformly conditioned causal VMW model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with the displayed parameter values, \(\nu_P\) is the quotient latent-effect probability law induced by \(P\), and the infimum ranges over measurable estimators \(\widetilde\nu_n\) from \(n\) observed proxy records to quotient laws supported in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\).

21bb1b27b6a09c3966b18de8e090795ab87eeda0.title: Two-class witness validity
21bb1b27b6a09c3966b18de8e090795ab87eeda0.body:
For every perturbation \(\varepsilon\) with
\[
0\le \varepsilon \le \frac18,
\]
the explicit two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\), with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), belongs to \(\mathcal M\). Moreover,
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Treatment masses.)}
\[
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=0)=\frac{12}{25},
\qquad
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=1)=\frac{13}{25}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Proxy determinants.)}
\[
\det(B)=\frac35,
\qquad
\det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=\frac25.
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed proxy moments.)}
\[
\det(M_0(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=\frac{3}{50},
\qquad
\det(M_1(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))
=\frac25\cdot\frac35\cdot\frac{36}{169}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Latent masses.)}
\[
p_0=\frac25,
\qquad
p_1=\frac35.
\]
\item \textbf{(Quotient law.)}
\[
\nu_{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}}
=
\frac25\,\delta_{1/4-\varepsilon}
+
\frac35\,\delta_{1/4+\varepsilon}.
\]
\end{itemize}
At \(\varepsilon=0\), the target-proxy matrix \(B\) and both reference-proxy matrices \(A_0,A_1\) are nonsingular, the quotient law is
\[
\nu_{P_{0}^{\mathrm{wit}}}=\delta_{1/4},
\]
and the two latent masses remain unequal.

9f7921fa311d43f8f6d61faff27deb2e4e234223.title: Borel nearest-point selector
9f7921fa311d43f8f6d61faff27deb2e4e234223.body:
Let \(d\in\mathbb N\), let \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), and let
\(d_S:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty feasible set.)} \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty.
\item \textbf{(Compactness.)} \(\mathcal K\) is compact.
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} The map \((s,q)\mapsto d_S(s,q)\) is continuous.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a Borel measurable map \(\Pi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) such that, for every \(s\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K
\quad\text{and}\quad
\forall q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(s,\Pi(s))\le d_S(s,q).
\]

99149662b984453c392cc1c10c480ac3ad42d285.title: Cluster adaptive report
99149662b984453c392cc1c10c480ac3ad42d285.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Atom floor.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), the following statement holds.  Let
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},\qquad
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\]
and define
\[
\begin{gathered}
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}\,L L_\tau}{\sigma_0},\qquad
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\\
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}\,L L_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
     +\frac{2\sqrt{k}\,L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}\,L c_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}\,L c_V,\qquad
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\\
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
\end{gathered}
\]
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\,
\left(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f\right)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\}.
\]
This constant satisfies \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}>0\).  For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) supported on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\), summary-repair data \(R\), and an exhaustive lexicographically ordered structured-lattice candidate list such that \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the first minimizer of \(J_n\) over that list and has atom floor \(\pi_0\).

For every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), set
\[
r_{n,\alpha}=C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}},
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}\right),
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\pi_0}.
\]
For every full-data law \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and every sample used to form the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\) in \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}\),
\[
W_1\!\left(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
\left\{
d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}
\right\}.
\]
Moreover, for each such \(P\), the event
\[
E_P=\left\{\widehat S_n:\ d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\right\}
\]
satisfies
\[
Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge 1-\alpha.
\]
On \(E_P\), form \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) as the set of quotient laws \(\xi\) whose representative has atom floor \(\pi_0\) and satisfies
\[
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
Let \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) be the connected components of the support of \(\widehat\lambda_n\), where links are generated by support points within distance \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  For \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define
\[
K_C(P)=\left\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\right\},
\]
\[
I_C=
\left[
\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\nu_\xi\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\},
\,
\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\nu_\xi\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}
\right],
\]
and
\[
\Delta_C(P)=
\begin{cases}
\inf\{|x-y|:\ x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)\},&
\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)\ne\emptyset,\\
+\infty,&
\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)=\emptyset.
\end{cases}
\]
Then the sets \(K_C(P)\), indexed by \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), form a nonempty-block partition of \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\): for every \(x\),
\[
x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists!\,C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\ \text{such that }x\in K_C(P),
\]
and each \(K_C(P)\) is nonempty and contained in \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\).  Every \(x\in K_C(P)\) lies in the reported support interval
\[
\left[\inf C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\ \sup C+\rho_{n,\alpha}\right],
\]
and the true cluster mass satisfies
\[
\nu_P(K_C(P))\in I_C.
\]
If \(K_C(P)\) is a singleton, then
\[
\left(\sup C+\rho_{n,\alpha}\right)-\left(\inf C-\rho_{n,\alpha}\right)
\le 4\rho_{n,\alpha}
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\delta(P)}\right\},
\]
where \(\delta(P)\) is the extended-real infimum of positive pairwise latent-effect gaps.  For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), if \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\), then \(\operatorname{length}(I_C)=0\), and in all cases
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\Delta_C(P)}\right\}.
\]
Finally, \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) has the finite constrained-program representation
\[
\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and there exists a finite transport plan from }\xi\text{ to }\widehat\lambda_n
\text{ with cost at most }R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

cced3f925738b32c44ba67bbc069780aba92a8c1.title: Matching local lower bounds
cced3f925738b32c44ba67bbc069780aba92a8c1.body:
Fix a local KL radius constant \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) with \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1\).  In the explicit two-class Bernoulli proxy construction of \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\), with \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), there exist constants \(a,c,C\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<a\le \frac18,\qquad c>0,\qquad C>0 .
\]
For every \(n\ge 1\), the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Quotient-law risk.)} For every measurable quotient-law estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) taking values in two-atomic laws with effect-support radius \(L_\tau=4\cdot 2\sqrt{2}/(1/10)\), there is a law
\[
P\in \left\{P^{\mathrm{wit}}_0,\;P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{a/\sqrt n}\right\}
\]
which belongs to the local quotient-law experiment \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\) of \(\cref{obj:def:local-quotient-experiment}\) at radius \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\), and for which
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Labeled-weight risk.)} For every \(g\) with \(0<g\le 1/4\) and every measurable simplex-valued ordered-weight estimator \(\widetilde p_n\), there is a law
\[
P\in \left\{P_{g,0},\;P_{g,h_n(g)}\right\},
\qquad
h_n(g):=a\min\left\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\right\},
\]
which belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) of \(\cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment}\) at radius \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\), and for which
\[
c\min\left\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\right\}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\sum_{i=1}^2
\left|\widetilde p_{n,i}-p_i^{\uparrow}(P)\right|
\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Quotient-law certificate.)} The two witness laws \(P^{\mathrm{wit}}_0\) and \(P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{a/\sqrt n}\) belong to \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\) at radius \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\), and satisfy
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{a/\sqrt n})_O\,\middle\|\,(P^{\mathrm{wit}}_0)_O\right)
\le
\frac{C}{n},
\qquad
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
W_1\!\left(\nu_{P^{\mathrm{wit}}_0},\nu_{P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{a/\sqrt n}}\right).
\]

\item \textbf{(Labeled-path certificate.)} For every \(g\) with \(0<g\le 1/4\), the calibrated displacement
\[
h_n(g):=a\min\left\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\right\}
\]
lies in \([-1,1]\).  The two path laws \(P_{g,h_n(g)}\) and \(P_{g,0}\) belong to \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) at radius \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\), and satisfy
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h_n(g)})_O\,\middle\|\,(P_{g,0})_O\right)
\le
C g^2 h_n(g)^2
\]
and
\[
\sum_{i=1}^2
\left|
p_i^{\uparrow}(P_{g,h_n(g)})-p_i^{\uparrow}(P_{g,0})
\right|
=
2|h_n(g)|.
\]
\end{itemize}

3eb41f1edad7d61c9c631a530d0e23b11aef227a.title: Same-class labeled minimax
3eb41f1edad7d61c9c631a530d0e23b11aef227a.body:
There exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\) such that \(0<c<C\) and the following holds.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\in\mathbb N\) satisfies \(1\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The gap scale \(g\) satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Model stratum.)} The model is the two-class, two-target-proxy, two-reference-proxy stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}\), with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).
\end{itemize}

For each full-data law \(P\) in this stratum, let \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\in\mathbb R^2\) be the ordered latent-weight target obtained from the raw quotient law \(\nu_P=(p_u,\tau_u)_{u\in\{1,2\}}\) on the radius
\[
L_\tau=4\cdot 2\cdot \sqrt{2}/(1/10).
\]
Equivalently, when the two atom masses are strictly positive and the two effects are distinct,
\[
p^{\uparrow}_j(P)
=
\sum_{u\in\{1,2\}}
\mathbf 1\!\left\{\#\{v:\tau_v<\tau_u\}=j\right\}p_u,
\qquad j\in\{0,1\},
\]
and otherwise \(p^{\uparrow}_j(P)=1/2\).

Then the labeled minimax risk on this same stratum satisfies
\[
c\,\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\sum_{j=0}^{1}\left|\widetilde p_{n,j}-p^{\uparrow}_j(P)\right|
\right]
\le
C\,\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}.
\]

4729d84fb1896ddcda70ccf037d30b137d318e62.title: Published VMW converse transfer
4729d84fb1896ddcda70ccf037d30b137d318e62.body:
Fix the published VMW scope and margin record matched to the cited VMW structural model and separated recovery regime.  There exist constants \(a,c\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<a\le \frac18,
\qquad
0<c,
\]
and, for every \(n\ge 1\), the following statements hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Quotient witness pair.)} The two laws \(P_{0}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\) belong to the published VMW structural model and satisfy the law-level finite-regularity condition requiring admissible positive dimensions, finite positive envelopes for \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\), positive treatment-arm probabilities, and positive population singular-value margins.  The collision law \(P_{0}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) lies outside the separated recovery regime of the published VMW finite-sample recovery theorem.

\item \textbf{(Quotient comparator classes.)} For every parameter class \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) of probability laws on full data with \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), if every \(P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu\) belongs to the published VMW structural model and satisfies the same law-level finite-regularity condition, and if
\[
\{P_{0}^{\mathrm{wit}},P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\}\subseteq \mathcal V_n^\nu,
\]
then every estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) taking \(n\) observed samples to a quotient law on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\), with
\[
L_\tau=4\cdot 2\cdot \frac{\sqrt 2}{1/10},
\]
has worst-case risk at least \(c/\sqrt n\):
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\ge \frac{c}{\sqrt n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Labeled path pair.)} For every \(g\in(0,1/4]\), define
\[
h(n,g)=a\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
Then \(h(n,g)\) is an admissible tangent amplitude, and the two laws \(P_{g,0}\) and \(P_{g,h(n,g)}\) belong to the published VMW structural model, satisfy the same law-level finite-regularity condition, and have spectrally separated latent effects.

\item \textbf{(Labeled-weight comparator classes.)} For every \(g\in(0,1/4]\) and every parameter class \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\) of probability laws on full data with \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), if every \(P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\) belongs to the published VMW structural model and satisfies the same law-level finite-regularity condition, and if
\[
\{P_{g,0},P_{g,h(n,g)}\}\subseteq \mathcal V_{n,g}^{p},
\]
then every labeled-weight estimator \(\widetilde p_n\) based on \(n\) observed samples has worst-case risk at least
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}:
\]
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\left\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1
\right]
\ge
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

f5a9f58a70685ff12bf76dccb607a784629d4d52.title: Uniform summary concentration
f5a9f58a70685ff12bf76dccb607a784629d4d52.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Positivity floor.)} \(0<\pi_0\) and \(\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\) and \(\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C_0\ge 1\), depending only on \(k,d_x,d_z,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), such that the following holds.  For every \(L\ge 1\), every \(n\ge 1\), every full-data law \(P\) on records \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) in the model class \(\mathcal M\) with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), and every \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))>
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le \eta .
\]
Moreover, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\{N_{t,n}=0\}
=
\left(1-P_O(T=t)\right)^n
\le
(1-k\pi_0)^n .
\]

fadabfa5e48779fb3b03862529d35eab7b6ef22f.title: Finite-net law estimator
fadabfa5e48779fb3b03862529d35eab7b6ef22f.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\) such that
\[
2\le k,\qquad k\le d_x,\qquad k\le d_z,\qquad
1\le L,\qquad 0<\pi_0\le {1\over 2k},\qquad 0<\sigma_0\le 1 .
\]
There are constants \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) and \(C>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), there is a class-dependent finite-net library \(A\) with the grid, feasibility, coverage, disjoint-cube, mesh, and lexicographic tie-breaking structure of \(\cref{obj:def:finite-net-law-estimator}\) for which the following assertions hold for every exact-real primitive provider on the admissible core parameter domain.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Total Borel estimator.)} The class-advised finite-net quotient-law estimator \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\), defined by
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}(\omega)
  =
  \operatorname{law}\!\left(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\right),
\]
is Borel measurable as a function of the observed sample \(\omega\in(\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_z}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R)^n\).

\item \textbf{(Library size.)} The number of stored representatives satisfies
\[
\#A\le C\,n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Operation count and trace.)} For every sample \(\omega\), the exact execution forming \(\widehat S_n\), scanning the library, and then running the selected spectral routine has total operation count at most
\[
C\left\{n+n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}\right\}.
\]
Its trace is exactly the concatenation of the empirical-summary trace, the exhaustive library-search trace, and, when a representative \(i\) is selected, the trace of the exact-real spectral run at \(A_i\); when no representative is selected, the final spectral trace is empty.

\item \textbf{(Selected representative.)} If the program selects \(i\) on sample \(\omega\), then \(A_i\) is a nearest representative to \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\) in \(d_S\), and every tied representative \(j\) satisfies the lexicographic rank inequality
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)\le \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(j).
\]
For the corresponding exact-real spectral run, \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}(\omega)\) is its output effect law; the observed-proxy maps are injective for both treatment arms; the singular-value threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) retains exactly indices \(j<k\) in the stacked proxy moment; and every eigenvalue of the compressed operator is one of the eigenvalues output by that run.

\item \textbf{(Perturbation-stable thresholding.)} For every stored representative \(i\) and every perturbation \(H\) of the stacked proxy moment,
\[
\|H\|<{\pi_0\sigma_0^2\over 2}
\]
implies that thresholding \(S_i+H\) at \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) recovers matrix dimension \(k\).

\item \textbf{(Representative validity.)} Each stored representative \(i\) is the observable summary of some law \(Q\in\mathcal M\) from \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and the exact-real spectral output at \(i\) equals the quotient latent-effect law \(\nu_Q\). The representative atomic law output by the spectral run is valid.

\item \textbf{(Deterministic modulus.)} For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(n\)-sample \(\omega\), and the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\) from \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}\),
\[
W_1\!\left(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}(\omega),\nu_P\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{mod}}
\left\{
2\,d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P)\right)+n^{-1/2}
\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Uniform tail bound.)} For every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\omega:
W_1\!\left(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}(\omega),\nu_P\right)
>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}
\le \eta .
\]
\end{itemize}

61c784a357a27857f07602e3339843df77fdfbf0.title: Polynomial lattice law estimator
61c784a357a27857f07602e3339843df77fdfbf0.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Set
\[
L_\tau:=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\qquad
s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\]
and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_V&:=4\sqrt{d_xk},
&K_D&:=\frac{4\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},
&A_D&:=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\\
K_f&:=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},
&c_D&:=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m&:=2\sqrt{k}Lc_V+k+kL,
&c_b&:=k+2\sqrt{k}Lc_V,
&c_{\mathrm{grid}}&:=c_D+c_m+c_b,\\
B_{\mathrm{lat}}&:=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
&&C_{\mathrm{lat}}:=\max\left\{\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}>0\), and there is a constant
\(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), there is an estimator
\(\widehat\lambda_n\) with values in quotient laws having at most \(k\) atoms in
\([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\) with the following properties.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structured lattice rule.)} With \(m_\star:=\pi_0\),
\[
H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k
+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,
\qquad
q_n:=H_n^{-1},
\qquad
\ell_n:=\lceil m_\star H_n\rceil .
\]
The estimator is induced by a Borel summary rule applied to the empirical summary
\(\widehat S_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}\).  Its finite candidate list is exactly the prescribed structured lattice: it contains every well-formed point
\(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\) once, is ordered lexicographically, and chooses the first minimizer of
\[
J_n(\vartheta):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2 .
\]
Here
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\qquad
m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,
\qquad
b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\qquad
\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^k p_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and \(\widehat\lambda_n=\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}\) for the selected first minimizer.
\item \textbf{(Atom floor.)} The estimator has atom-floor parameter \(\pi_0\): for every sample, every distinct represented atom of \(\widehat\lambda_n\) has aggregate mass at least \(\pi_0\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold recovery.)} For every full-data law \(P\in\mathcal M\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), the population summary \(S(P)\) satisfies
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j\!\left(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(P),M_1(P))\right)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j<k .
\]
Moreover, every summary \(s\) with
\(d_S(s,S(P))<\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) satisfies the same threshold-recovery equivalence at threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).
\item \textbf{(Complexity.)} The candidate list and exhaustive minimization obey
\[
\#\mathcal A_n\le
C\,n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2},
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{ops}(\widehat\lambda_n)\le
C\left\{n+n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Deterministic accuracy.)} For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every sample,
\[
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left\{
d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}
\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Uniform tail bound.)} For every \(0<\eta<1/2\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}\le \eta .
\]
\end{itemize}

62882731e0614058b8dea1fa9e2ce99f5470b9bc.title: Latent ignorability
62882731e0614058b8dea1fa9e2ce99f5470b9bc.body:
For each \(t \in \{0,1\}\), under \(P\),
\[
Y(t) \perp T \mid U.
\]

615f64b965f98c8bb23ef0dd0546e4a5c104a1f6.title: Bounded proxy product
615f64b965f98c8bb23ef0dd0546e4a5c104a1f6.body:
The proxy product is uniformly bounded:
\[
\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le L
\]
almost surely under \(P\).

4f65a026b3c0ffa9b334f0ac16556a591660ea2d.title: Bounded outcome-proxy product
4f65a026b3c0ffa9b334f0ac16556a591660ea2d.body:
The outcome-weighted proxy product is uniformly bounded:
\[
\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le L
\]
almost surely under \(P\).

79de5a7a659d6b3fa3be2326cefe761e6e664367.title: Latent-arm positivity
79de5a7a659d6b3fa3be2326cefe761e6e664367.body:
Every latent class and treatment arm has mass at least \(\pi_0\):
\[
\min_{1\le u\le k,\ t\in\{0,1\}} P(U=u,T=t)\ge \pi_0 .
\]

a0aa22604c109c5fb04b1731e391f315f82fbe63.title: Proxy rank margin
a0aa22604c109c5fb04b1731e391f315f82fbe63.body:
The reference- and target-proxy feature matrices have a uniform \(k\)th singular-value margin:
\[
\min\{\sigma_k(A_0),\sigma_k(A_1),\sigma_k(B)\}\ge \sigma_0 .
\]

b3bc5697e6c47e0b767494f726a83400d00da82e.title: Effect-gap window
b3bc5697e6c47e0b767494f726a83400d00da82e.body:
The nearest-effect gap lies in the \(g\)-window:
\[
g/2\le \delta(P)\le 2g .
\]

3497fc9a0a1a03fe62f920094405220d95b6b9ba.title: Distinct quotient effects
3497fc9a0a1a03fe62f920094405220d95b6b9ba.body: The quotient latent-effect probability law \(\nu_P\) has exactly \(k\) distinct support points.

cd2e4ad74965a17eae26a146e174b1b9ed1c240f.title: Model class \(\mathcal M\)

42a3d4f5a7fbe2fcfe4071646c8190069ef64554.title: Observable summary \(S(P)\) and metric \(d_S\)
42a3d4f5a7fbe2fcfe4071646c8190069ef64554.body:
The observable conditional moment summary is
\[
S(P):=\bigl(M_0(P),M_1(P),N_0(P),N_1(P),m_X(P)\bigr).
\]
For summaries \(s\) and \(s'\), the summary metric is
\[
d_S(s,s')
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{4}\lVert s_j-s'_j\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert s_5-s'_5\rVert_2 .
\]

09ace8a693a99bc562a889273a23d6003088f0cb.title: Empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\)
09ace8a693a99bc562a889273a23d6003088f0cb.body:
For each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the armwise treatment count is
\[
N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}.
\]
The empirical armwise moments are
\[
\widehat M_{t,n}
:=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Z_iX_i^\top}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}},
\qquad
\widehat N_{t,n}
:=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Y_iZ_iX_i^\top}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}}.
\]
The empirical target-proxy mean is
\[
\widehat m_{X,n}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i.
\]
The total empirical observable summary is
\[
\widehat S_n
:=
\bigl(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},
\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n}\bigr).
\]
On the event \(\{N_{t,n}=0\}\), the corresponding armwise matrices are the zero matrix, so \(\widehat S_n\) is a total Borel function of the sample.

0a31a5dd1645e709b507023a5cfc2186a87320e2.title: Compressed operator \(\Delta Q(P)\) and anchors
0a31a5dd1645e709b507023a5cfc2186a87320e2.body:
Choose any matrix \(V(P)\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) with orthonormal columns spanning
\[
\operatorname{row}\!\begin{bmatrix} M_0(P)\\ M_1(P)\end{bmatrix}
\subseteq \mathbb R^{d_x}.
\]
The compressed effect operator is
\[
\Delta Q(P)
:=
\{M_1(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_1(P)V(P)
-
\{M_0(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_0(P)V(P).
\]
The left and right spectral anchors are
\[
a(P)^\top:=m_X(P)^\top V(P),
\qquad
c(P):=V(P)^\top e_1.
\]

6a51596a64f9ea092f1c977866a3ad3164de873b.title: Quotient law \(\nu_P\)
6a51596a64f9ea092f1c977866a3ad3164de873b.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), define the quotient latent-effect law
\[
\nu_P:=\sum_{u=1}^{k}p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.
\]
It is interpreted as a probability measure on the latent treatment-effect values, with equal values of \(\tau_u\) assigned their aggregate mass.

7dfab433898146bdbc5029a55f4334cda7b17c4d.title: Gap stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\)
7dfab433898146bdbc5029a55f4334cda7b17c4d.body:
For a gap level \(g\), define
\[
\mathcal M(g):=
\{P\in\mathcal M:
P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}\}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal M\) is the model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).

06c527790ac51da17e3120dfcc706b42291ab088.title: Sample experiment \(\mathcal E_n\)
06c527790ac51da17e3120dfcc706b42291ab088.body:
For sample size \(n\), define the observed i.i.d. proxy experiment
\[
\mathcal E_n:=\{Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}:P\in\mathcal M\}.
\]

0e1fca08d46aeae0bf0b5e696f071c13ab50962c.title: Summary closure \(\mathcal K\)
0e1fca08d46aeae0bf0b5e696f071c13ab50962c.body:
Define the admissible summary image
\[
\mathscr S:=S(\mathcal M)=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\},
\]
and let
\[
\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}
\]
be its closure under \(d_S\). Define
\[
F:\mathscr S\to\mathcal P_k([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])
\]
by
\[
F(S(P)):=\nu_P.
\]
The functional is well defined. For \(j=0,\ldots,2k-1\),
\[
\int x^j\,d\nu_P(x)=a(P)^\top\Delta Q(P)^jc(P).
\]
Under homogeneous effects with common value \(\tau_\star\),
\[
\Delta Q(P)=\tau_\star I_k,
\qquad
\nu_P=\delta_{\tau_\star}.
\]

2b7ab62b14771343ea7007864c4c6055187781bb.title: Nearest-summary estimator \(\widehat\nu_n\)
2b7ab62b14771343ea7007864c4c6055187781bb.body:
For fixed class constants, define \(\Pi\) and \(\widehat\nu_n\) by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), let
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])
\]
be the unique continuous extension of \(F\).

\item If \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), choose a Borel nearest-summary selector satisfying
\[
\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathcal K}d_S(q,s)
\]
for each summary-space point \(s\).

\item If \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), define
\[
\Pi(s):=0
\]
in the ambient summary space.

\item Output the theoretical nearest-summary quotient-law estimator
\[
\widehat\nu_n:=
\begin{cases}
\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n)), & \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}
Thus \(\Pi\) and \(\widehat\nu_n\) are total Borel maps for every choice of the fixed class constants.

25c9e0849407dd3201137e99cebe95f1cfb621a0.title: Wasserstein sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\)
25c9e0849407dd3201137e99cebe95f1cfb621a0.body:
For fixed \(n\) and \(\alpha\), define the theoretical and computable Wasserstein confidence sets by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the original exact summary-inversion set by
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=
\begin{cases}
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\},
& \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\{\delta_0\}, & \mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]

\item Define the atom floor and computable radius
\[
m_\star:=\pi_0,
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}).
\]

\item Define
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])
\]
as the set of probability laws on \([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]\) with at most \(k\) distinct atoms, each having mass at least \(m_\star\).

\item Define the computable outer \(W_1\) confidence set
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]):
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]

\item Merge repeated atoms of the computed center and write
\[
\widehat\lambda_n=\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\widehat w_b\delta_{\widehat x_b},
\]
where
\[
-L_{\tau}\le\widehat x_1<\cdots<\widehat x_{\widehat r}\le L_{\tau},
\qquad
1\le\widehat r\le k.
\]

\item Equivalently, output \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) as the union over \(1\le r\le k\) of all laws
\[
\sum_{a=1}^rw_a\delta_{x_a}
\]
for which there exist variables \(x_1<\cdots<x_r\), \(w_a\), and \(\gamma_{ab}\) satisfying
\[
\begin{gathered}
-L_{\tau}\le x_1<\cdots<x_r\le L_{\tau},
\qquad
w_a\ge m_\star,
\qquad
\sum_{a=1}^rw_a=1,\\
\gamma_{ab}\ge0,
\qquad
\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}=w_a,
\qquad
\sum_{a=1}^{r}\gamma_{ab}=\widehat w_b,\\
\sum_{a=1}^{r}\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}
\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\le R_{n,\alpha}.
\end{gathered}
\]
\end{enumerate}
The set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) is an evaluable fixed-dimensional finite union of ordered-support, weight, and transport-plan constraint sets.

350200541e9482df8f7ba27cb2072d263e1e6a96.title: Cluster report $\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}$
350200541e9482df8f7ba27cb2072d263e1e6a96.body:
Given \(\widehat\lambda_n\), \(R_{n,\alpha}\), and \(m_\star\), define the cluster report by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the simultaneous event and association radius
\[
E_P:=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\},
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}:=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{m_\star}.
\]
\item Merge repeated atoms of \(\widehat\lambda_n\). On the resulting support, form the graph with edge relation
\[
x\sim x'
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\ne x'\ \text{ and }\ |x-x'|\le 4\rho_{n,\alpha}.
\]
Let
\[
\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}
:=
\{\text{connected components of this graph}\}.
\]
\item For each \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define the associated true and candidate atom sets
\[
K_C(P):=
\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\},
\]
\[
K_C(\xi):=
\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
\item Define the computable mass interval
\[
I_C:=
\left[
\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi)),
\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi))
\right].
\]
In the ordered-support and transport-plan representation of \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), the two endpoints are obtained from the same finite union of fixed-dimensional mixed-integer constrained programs. For each \(1\le r\le k\), introduce variables \(z_a\in\{0,1\}\) and impose
\[
z_a=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\min_{c\in C}|x_a-c|\le\rho_{n,\alpha}.
\]
The lower endpoint minimizes, and the upper endpoint maximizes,
\[
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a z_a
\]
over the ordered-support, atom-floor, simplex, and transport constraints defining \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\).
\item For each \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define the external gap
\[
\Delta_C(P):=
\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)=\emptyset\).
\item Output
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}
:=
\left\{
\left(
[\min C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\max C+\rho_{n,\alpha}],
I_C
\right):
C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

2ecf2161efd4eadf01954a316364ac17b8e9348a.title: Ordered-weight estimator $\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}$
2ecf2161efd4eadf01954a316364ac17b8e9348a.body:
Given the positive law estimator \(\widehat\nu_n\), define the ordered-weight estimator by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Write the unique positive atomic representation
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^{\widehat s_n}\widehat w_{\ell,n}\delta_{\widehat\tau_{\ell,n}},
\qquad
\widehat\tau_{1,n}<\cdots<\widehat\tau_{\widehat s_n,n},
\qquad
\widehat w_{\ell,n}>0.
\]
\item Define
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}
:=
\begin{cases}
(\widehat w_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat w_{k,n}), & \widehat s_n=k,\\
(1/k,\ldots,1/k), & \widehat s_n<k.
\end{cases}
\]
\item The ordering of the finite support and the extraction of its jump sizes are Borel operations; hence the displayed rule defines a total Borel map into \(\Delta^{k-1}\).
\end{enumerate}

5dd4cca37c3c7476a1c96c2e84054ea9066f599e.title: Two-class witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\)
5dd4cca37c3c7476a1c96c2e84054ea9066f599e.body:
For \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) is the law specified as follows:
\[
P(U=1)=0.4,
\qquad
P(U=2)=0.6,
\]
\[
P(T=1\mid U=1)=0.4,
\qquad
P(T=1\mid U=2)=0.6,
\]
\[
X=(1,X_2)^\top,
\qquad
Z=(1,Z_2)^\top,
\]
\[
B=
\begin{psmallmatrix}
1&1\\
0.2&0.8
\end{psmallmatrix},
\qquad
A_0=
\begin{psmallmatrix}
1&1\\
0.3&0.7
\end{psmallmatrix},
\qquad
A_1=
\begin{psmallmatrix}
1&1\\
0.35&0.75
\end{psmallmatrix},
\]
\[
E[Y(0)\mid U]=(0.25,0.25),
\qquad
E[Y(1)\mid U]=(0.5-\varepsilon,0.5+\varepsilon).
\]
Conditional on \(U\), the variables \(X_2,Y(0),Y(1),T\) are mutually independent Bernoulli variables with the displayed conditional means. Conditional on \((U,T)\), the variable \(Z_2\) is independent of \((X_2,Y(0),Y(1))\) and has conditional mean given by \(A_T\). The observed outcome is
\[
Y=Y(T).
\]

967d9a42968b79da5957f579ceb814ce96b75bb9.title: Local quotient experiment \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\)
967d9a42968b79da5957f579ceb814ce96b75bb9.body:
The local quotient-law KL experiment is
\[
\mathcal L_n^\nu
:=
\{P\in\mathcal M:\ P\in\mathcal M\text{ as in }\cref{obj:def:model-class}
\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:local-quotient-neighborhood}\}.
\]

1e970743bc6938a31d66219481706010be69a6d3.title: Local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\)
1e970743bc6938a31d66219481706010be69a6d3.body:
The local labeled-weight KL experiment is
\[
\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}
:=
\{P\in\mathcal M(g):\ P\in\mathcal M(g)\text{ as in }\cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}
\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood}\}.
\]

5cbf7dbe52dad09f25f5579b487e7d388b253df2.title: Constructive repair handle
5cbf7dbe52dad09f25f5579b487e7d388b253df2.body:
For laws in the model class of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), the constructive repair handle consists of the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For positive-law repair, localize the empirical compressed-operator spectrum by Bauer--Fike perturbation bounds. Within overlapping localization discs, replace individual eigenvectors by the corresponding Kato contour projectors and transport aggregate projector mass across each cluster diameter.
\item At the realized empirical summary, define the first \(2k\) spectral moments by
\[
m=(m_j)_{0\le j<2k}.
\]
Choose a valid positive \(k\)-atomic law
\[
\sum_i w_i\delta_{x_i}
\]
solving
\[
\inf_{\{(w_i,x_i)\}}
\sum_{j=0}^{2k-1}
\left|m_j-\sum_i w_i x_i^j\right|,
\]
where the infimum ranges over all valid positive \(k\)-atomic laws.
\item Extract the repaired real probability measure
\[
\sum_i w_i\delta_{x_i}
\]
from a minimizer in the preceding display.
\item For the labeled-weight converse, differentiate the Bernoulli factorization of \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\). For a weight displacement \(h\), solve the linear score-cancellation equations in the proxy and treatment primitives so that the resulting factorization-preserving path has observed score of order \(g h\).
\end{enumerate}

f285487adeb3883ab3225cecb9c7eaa764c0ea8b.title: Finite-net law estimator \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\)
f285487adeb3883ab3225cecb9c7eaa764c0ea8b.body:
For sample size \(n\), use the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\) and the fixed constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0,k,d_x,d_z\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item Set
\[
D:=4d_zd_x+d_x,\qquad
b:=4\sqrt{d_zd_x}+\sqrt{d_x},\qquad
\epsilon_n:=n^{-1/2}.
\]

\item Partition \([-L,L]^D\) into a deterministic lexicographically ordered grid of half-open cubes with side length at most \(\epsilon_n/b\).

\item If \(\mathscr S\ne\varnothing\), choose one representative \(q_{n,\ell}\in\mathscr S\) from each grid cube that intersects \(\mathscr S\), indexed in lexicographic order, and define
\[
\widehat q_n
:=
q_{n,\widehat\ell},
\qquad
\widehat\ell
:=
\min\arg\min_{\ell} d_S(q_{n,\ell},\widehat S_n).
\]

\item At \(\widehat q_n\), retain the \(k\) right singular directions of the vertically stacked proxy moment whose singular values exceed \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\). Let
\[
V
\]
denote the resulting orthonormal basis, and form the associated compressed effect operator, left spectral anchor, and right spectral anchor
\[
\Delta,\qquad a^\top,\qquad c.
\]

\item For each distinct eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\Delta\), define
\[
E_\lambda
:=
\prod_{\gamma\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta),\,\gamma\ne\lambda}
\frac{\Delta-\gamma I_k}{\lambda-\gamma},
\]
with the empty product equal to \(I_k\).

\item Output
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}
:=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta)}
a^\top E_\lambda c\,\delta_\lambda,
& \mathscr S\ne\varnothing,\\[1.25em]
\delta_0,
& \mathscr S=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}

89a72ed767c421f9c2857188c31cb711d80ec837.title: Exact sharp inversion algorithms
89a72ed767c421f9c2857188c31cb711d80ec837.body:
A natural next question is whether, in the fixed-dimensional exact-real model, one can compute in time polynomial in \(n\) the sharp summary-inversion image
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
=
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\}
\]
together with its exact support-dependent cluster extrema, using an exact representation of the image and of the extrema. The positive real law estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\), the honest outer set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), and every interval in the report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) have explicit fixed-dimensional constrained representations, including the case in which the raw empirical operator has nonreal eigenpairs. The unresolved computational target is an exact sharp polynomial-time algorithm for the original summary-inversion image and its extrema.

5fd45e570b1da0c2da2d5eda65bb8c2103951dc7.title: Observed record \(O\) and marginal \(P_O\)
5fd45e570b1da0c2da2d5eda65bb8c2103951dc7.body:
For a full-data probability law \(P\), the observed record is
\[
O=(T,X,Z,Y).
\]
The observed-data marginal of \(P\) is
\[
P_O := P\circ O^{-1}.
\]

52a3990b02615fa2e7d3560d7443ece327e5322d.title: Latent mass \(p_u\)
52a3990b02615fa2e7d3560d7443ece327e5322d.body:
For each latent class \(u\), the latent-class mass is
\[
p_u := P(U=u).
\]

1041e5b6c6a8286ae1520fa67782f2f3ef151c11.title: Latent mean \(\mu_{tu}\)
1041e5b6c6a8286ae1520fa67782f2f3ef151c11.body:
For treatment arm \(t\) and latent class \(u\), the latent conditional potential-outcome mean is
\[
\mu_{tu} := E_P\!\left[Y(t)\mid U=u\right].
\]

f32d8693973379fa573a3ca176ccef47543a93e4.title: Latent effect \(\tau_u\)
f32d8693973379fa573a3ca176ccef47543a93e4.body:
For each latent class \(u\), the latent-class treatment effect is
\[
\tau_u := \mu_{1u}-\mu_{0u}.
\]

2c9042da818a60209669c075c32df34645cd0679.title: Reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\)
2c9042da818a60209669c075c32df34645cd0679.body:
For arm \(t\), the reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\in\mathbb R^{d_z\times k}\) is defined entrywise by
\[
A_t(i,u) := E_P\!\left[Z_i\mid U=u,T=t\right].
\]

107ed117dacc8e7ffb524429d5c9674b8b4d1bf3.title: Target-proxy feature matrix \(B\)
107ed117dacc8e7ffb524429d5c9674b8b4d1bf3.body:
The target-proxy feature matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) is defined entrywise by
\[
B(i,u) := E_P\!\left[X_i\mid U=u\right].
\]

a1f6efe54862546a05e46390266791d11f1dbe7e.title: Effect-support radius \(L_\tau\)
a1f6efe54862546a05e46390266791d11f1dbe7e.body:
The derived effect-support radius is
\[
L_\tau := \frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]

bf205787534c95c9e54c2737da7ab7803274caa4.title: Effect gap \(\delta(P)\)
bf205787534c95c9e54c2737da7ab7803274caa4.body:
The effect gap \(\delta(P)\) is the smallest strictly positive distance between two positive-mass latent effects:
\[
\delta(P)
:=
\min\bigl\{|\tau_u-\tau_v|:\ p_u>0,\ p_v>0,\ \tau_u\ne\tau_v\bigr\}.
\]
When the quotient law has a single distinct support point, set \(\delta(P):=+\infty\).

c7e3c335b5a033a4db10bb6d89e10c47bb098ff9.title: Observable population moments \(M_t(P),N_t(P),m_X(P)\)
c7e3c335b5a033a4db10bb6d89e10c47bb098ff9.body:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable population moments are
\[
M_t(P):=\mathbb E_P[ZX^\top\mid T=t],
\qquad
N_t(P):=\mathbb E_P[YZX^\top\mid T=t],
\qquad
m_X(P):=\mathbb E_P[X].
\]

7122921e283e28e1469fd5ce7c77f705a35122e5.title: Summary radius \(r_{n,\alpha}\)
7122921e283e28e1469fd5ce7c77f705a35122e5.body:
For \(n\ge 1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the simultaneous concentration radius is
\[
r_{n,\alpha}
:=
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]

b832fc691f27afc71e156a33853cb321ba5606f2.title: Atomic law classes \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) and \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\)
b832fc691f27afc71e156a33853cb321ba5606f2.body:
The class \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) consists of probability laws on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\) having at most \(k\) distinct atoms. We also write
\[
\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
:=
\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]).
\]
Repeated slots and zero-weight slots represent the same law.

1dc78a0ece3a36531bf5bd5f61b4f6811ab32c71.title: Ordered mass target \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\)
1dc78a0ece3a36531bf5bd5f61b4f6811ab32c71.body:
The ordered mass target \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\) is defined as follows. When the \(k\) latent effects are distinct, \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\) is the vector of their masses ordered by increasing effect. Otherwise,
\[
p^{\uparrow}(P):=(1/k,\ldots,1/k).
\]

fbc313ae170f1a4cb15218cb8fc0184a465667b8.title: Path law \(P_{g,h}\)
fbc313ae170f1a4cb15218cb8fc0184a465667b8.body: For a gap \(g\) and displacement \(h\), \(P_{g,h}\) is the explicit two-class law obtained by perturbing the latent weights along the path while preserving the displayed proxy factorizations.

0c0b88ca5a65e4006099be517549959f5d27c0e0.title: Atom floor \(\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m,\xi)\)
0c0b88ca5a65e4006099be517549959f5d27c0e0.body: For a probability law \(\xi\), \(\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m,\xi)\) is the condition that every distinct support atom of \(\xi\) has aggregate mass at least \(m\).

17bd1af8c9529836d411bdce031240e3d77a24a7.title: Structured-lattice constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\)
17bd1af8c9529836d411bdce031240e3d77a24a7.body:
The structured-lattice constant is
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}=C_{\mathrm{lat}}(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0),
\]
defined as the maximum of the threshold-stability and grid-approximation constants displayed in the lattice construction.

cddfe12f4e925c3e8a476ca07d6c9aa92cd2377f.title: Structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\)
cddfe12f4e925c3e8a476ca07d6c9aa92cd2377f.body:
At sample size \(n\), with inputs given by the empirical moments and the tuning grids below, define \(\widehat\lambda_n\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Stack armwise matrices by
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0,M_1):=
\begin{bmatrix}
M_0^\top\\
M_1^\top
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

\item Set the population signal threshold
\[
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2
\]
and form the empirical compressed operator \(\widehat D_n\) by thresholding the empirical signal space at
\[
s_0/2=\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2.
\]

\item Let \(\mathcal V_n\), \(\mathcal R_n\), \(\mathcal P_n\), and \(\mathcal T_n\) be the prescribed polar-factor, conditioning-matrix, simplex-weight, and clipped-effect grids, respectively, and set
\[
\mathcal A_n:=\mathcal V_n\times \mathcal R_n\times \mathcal P_n\times \mathcal T_n,
\]
ordered lexicographically.

\item For each \(\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n\), evaluate the displayed lattice criterion
\[
J_n(\vartheta).
\]
Let
\[
\widehat\vartheta_n
:=
\min_{\operatorname{lex}}
\operatorname*{argmin}_{\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n} J_n(\vartheta).
\]

\item Output the effect law associated with the selected lattice point:
\[
\widehat\lambda_n:=\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

07172fbef674685171848f67c766f9eb6cf4ea4d.title: Finite-net program \(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\)
07172fbef674685171848f67c766f9eb6cf4ea4d.body:
For a stored representative library \(A=(A_i)_i\) and observed sample \(\omega\), define \(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each representative \(A_i\), compute its stacked proxy moment
\[
S_i:=\operatorname{stack}\bigl(M_0(A_i),M_1(A_i)\bigr).
\]

\item Assign each candidate its lexicographic rank
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i).
\]

\item Let \(I(A,\omega)\) be the set of nearest representatives to the empirical stacked proxy moment. Select the first nearest representative by
\[
\widehat i
:=
\operatorname*{argmin}_{i\in I(A,\omega)}
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i).
\]

\item Output the thresholded spectral effect law of \(A_{\widehat i}\):
\[
\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega):=\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_{\widehat i}).
\]
If the library is empty, output the canonical zero law:
\[
\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega):=\delta_0.
\]
\end{enumerate}

eb7502bda0a1dd6e4b6beab01cef65d61c65f45f.title: Published VMW regimes
eb7502bda0a1dd6e4b6beab01cef65d61c65f45f.body:
The published VMW structural model is the proxy-model parameter class indexed by the cited publication handle. Its law-level finite-regularity condition consists of:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Outcome and proxy envelopes.)} Finite positive envelopes for \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-arm probabilities.)} Positive marginal probabilities for each treatment arm.
\item \textbf{(Singular-value margin.)} A positive population singular-value margin.
\end{itemize}
The separated recovery regime consists of the published qualitative conditions, strict latent positivity, the finite-regularity condition, and pairwise distinct latent effects.

0109c2de170604e850a36574ae66fff506dbbf4c.title: Observed-record space \(O_{d_x,d_z}\)
0109c2de170604e850a36574ae66fff506dbbf4c.body:
The observed-record space is
\[
O_{d_x,d_z}:=\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_z}\times\mathbb R .
\]
An element \(O=(T,X,Z,Y)\in O_{d_x,d_z}\) consists of a binary treatment \(T\), a target-proxy vector \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), a reference-proxy vector \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d_z}\), and an outcome \(Y\in\mathbb R\).

f45608d73801396691c03081ebf870a2c19ee876.title: Wasserstein distance \(W_1(\nu,\xi)\)
f45608d73801396691c03081ebf870a2c19ee876.body:
For represented atomic laws
\[
\nu=\sum_i a_i\delta_{x_i},
\qquad
\xi=\sum_j b_j\delta_{y_j},
\]
the transport distance \(W_1(\nu,\xi)\) is
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
:=
\min_{\gamma_{ij}\ge 0}
\sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij}|x_i-y_j|,
\]
where the minimum is over couplings whose marginals agree with the represented masses:
\[
\sum_j\gamma_{ij}=a_i
\quad\text{for every }i,
\qquad
\sum_i\gamma_{ij}=b_j
\quad\text{for every }j .
\]

f1e8216ec6b7ffac7fbe28885d84a01996f6bbad.title: Atomic law class \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\)
f1e8216ec6b7ffac7fbe28885d84a01996f6bbad.body:
The class of laws on the effect-support interval with at most \(k\) distinct atoms is
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
:=
\left\{
\sum_{\ell=1}^s p_\ell\delta_{x_\ell}:
1\le s\le k,\ 
x_\ell\in[-L_\tau,L_\tau],\
p_\ell\ge 0,\
\sum_{\ell=1}^s p_\ell=1
\right\}.
\]
We also write
\[
\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
:=
\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]).
\]
Repeated atom locations and zero-weight slots represent the same law after aggregation. For a represented atomic law \(\xi\), the aggregated probability law is denoted by
\[
\nu_\xi .
\]

1295d1cf965b71497a74eb1d3d8e0bbe50555fb2.title: Structured lattice program \(\widehat\lambda_n\)
1295d1cf965b71497a74eb1d3d8e0bbe50555fb2.body:
At sample size \(n\), the structured lattice program takes the empirical summaries, the margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\), the effect-support radius \(L_\tau\), and the lattice scale \(H_n\) as inputs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the vertical stacking operation by
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0,M_1)
:=
[M_0^\top,M_1^\top]^\top .
\]

\item Set
\[
s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\qquad
q_n:=H_n^{-1},
\]
and threshold the empirical signal space at \(s_0/2\). Define
\[
\widehat D_n
:=
(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}
-
(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.
\]

\item Let \(\mathcal V_n\) be the prescribed grid of polar factors, \(\mathcal R_n\) the grid of invertible conditioning matrices with singular value at least \(\sigma_0/2\), \(\mathcal P_n\) the simplex grid with every coordinate at least \(\pi_0\), and \(\mathcal T_n\) the clipped effect grid in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]^k\). Set
\[
\mathcal A_n
:=
\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n,
\]
with the product ordered lexicographically.

\item For each \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal A_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta
:=
VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\qquad
m_\vartheta
:=
VR^\top p,
\qquad
b_\vartheta
:=
RV^\top e_1,
\]
\[
\lambda_\vartheta
:=
\sum_u p_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and
\[
J_n(\vartheta)
:=
\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+
\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2 .
\]

\item Let \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) be the first lexicographic minimizer of \(J_n\) over \(\mathcal A_n\):
\[
\widehat\vartheta_n
:=
\min_{\mathrm{lex}}
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n}J_n(\vartheta).
\]
The structured-lattice quotient-law estimator is
\[
\widehat\lambda_n
:=
\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

ec04f53fb2afbdbb429f23b22b05d201fd84296a.title: Finite-library program \(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\)
ec04f53fb2afbdbb429f23b22b05d201fd84296a.body:
For a stored representative library \(A=(A_i)_i\) and observed sample \(\omega\), the finite-library spectral program is defined as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each stored representative \(A_i\), define its stacked proxy moment by
\[
S_i
:=
\operatorname{stack}(M_0(A_i),M_1(A_i)).
\]

\item Let \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)\) denote the position of \(A_i\) in the fixed lexicographic library order.

\item Let
\[
\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_i)
\]
be the real atomic effect law returned by the thresholded exact-real spectral run for \(A_i\).

\item If the library is nonempty, let \(i^\star\) be a nearest representative of smallest lexicographic rank:
\[
i^\star
\in
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_i d(S_i,\widehat S_n),
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i^\star)
=
\min\left\{\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i):
i\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_j d(S_j,\widehat S_n)
\right\}.
\]
The program returns
\[
\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)
:=
(A_{i^\star},\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_{i^\star})).
\]

\item If the library is empty, the program returns the canonical zero law. The notation
\[
\operatorname{law}(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega))
\]
denotes the returned effect-law component.
\end{enumerate}

5e0eb4e4f41e103e18b5fb1e847432d062a3889b.title: Local quotient neighborhood
5e0eb4e4f41e103e18b5fb1e847432d062a3889b.body:
The observed-data marginal \(P_O\) lies in a Kullback--Leibler neighborhood of the collision-witness observed margin:
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_O\,\middle\|\,(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\right)
\le
\frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]

504435aee627d1ec1e746d47e9e970ebe22212d1.title: Path law \(P_{g,h}\)
504435aee627d1ec1e746d47e9e970ebe22212d1.body:
For an admissible gap \(g\) and displacement \(h\), \(P_{g,h}\) is the following two-class Bernoulli proxy law. Set \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(X=(1,X_2)^\top\), \(Z=(1,Z_2)^\top\), and
\[
b_1(h):=0.2,\qquad
b_2(h):=\frac{0.48-0.2h}{0.6-h},\qquad
B_h:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1\\
b_1(h)&b_2(h)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Let
\[
(q_0,s_0):=(0.48,0.24),\qquad
(q_1,s_1):=(0.52,0.32),
\]
and define the armwise joint latent weights by
\[
w_t(h)^\top:=(q_t,s_t)(B_h^\top)^{-1},
\qquad t\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The latent masses are
\[
p(h):=
\begin{pmatrix}
0.4+h\\
0.6-h
\end{pmatrix}
=
w_0(h)+w_1(h).
\]
With
\[
A_0^0:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1\\
0.3&0.7
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A_1^0:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1\\
0.35&0.75
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
B_0:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1\\
0.2&0.8
\end{pmatrix},
\]
put, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
J_t:=A_t^0\operatorname{diag}(w_t(0))B_0^\top,
\qquad
A_{t,h}:=J_t(B_h^\top)^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(w_t(h))^{-1}.
\]
The treatment probabilities and latent conditional potential-outcome means are
\[
P_{g,h}(T=1\mid U=u):=\frac{w_{1u}(h)}{p_u(h)},
\qquad
\mu_0:=
\begin{pmatrix}
0.25\\
0.25
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mu_1:=
\begin{pmatrix}
0.5-g/2\\
0.5+g/2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The law \(P_{g,h}\) assigns \(P_{g,h}(U=u)=p_u(h)\). Conditional on \(U=u\), draw \(X_2\) as a Bernoulli variable with mean \(b_u(h)\), draw \(T\) with the displayed treatment probability, and draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) as Bernoulli variables with means \(\mu_{0u}\) and \(\mu_{1u}\). Conditional on \((U,T)=(u,t)\), draw \(Z_2\) as a Bernoulli variable with mean \((A_{t,h})_{2u}\), independently of \((X_2,Y(0),Y(1))\), and set
\[
Y:=Y(T).
\]
Equivalently, the proxy moments along the path satisfy
\[
A_{t,h}\operatorname{diag}(w_t(h))B_h^\top=J_t,
\qquad t\in\{0,1\},
\]
so the displayed proxy factorizations are preserved while the ordered latent masses move from \((0.4,0.6)^\top\) to \((0.4+h,0.6-h)^\top\).

333d23f4478952d88de3ed11bd2ecad3c13f690e.title: Structured lattice program \(\widehat\lambda_n\)
333d23f4478952d88de3ed11bd2ecad3c13f690e.body:
At sample size \(n\), the structured lattice program takes the empirical summaries, the margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\), and the effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) as inputs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the vertical stacking operation by
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0,M_1):=[M_0^\top,M_1^\top]^\top .
\]

\item Set
\[
s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\qquad
H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k
+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,
\qquad
q_n:=H_n^{-1}.
\]
For a singular-value decomposition \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define
\[
G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=
\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top .
\]
The thresholded empirical compressed operator is
\[
\widehat D_n
:=
(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}
-
(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.
\]

\item Define the polar-factor grid by
\[
\mathcal V_n:=
\left\{
G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}:
G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k},\
|G_{ij}|\le 1,\
\sigma_k(G)\ge\frac12
\right\}.
\]

\item Define the conditioning-matrix grid by
\[
\mathcal R_n:=
\left\{
R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}:
\sigma_k(R)\ge\frac{\sigma_0}{2},\
\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le 2\sqrt{k}L
\right\}.
\]

\item Set \(m_\star:=\pi_0\) and
\[
\ell_n:=\lceil m_\star H_n\rceil .
\]
Define the simplex grid by
\[
\mathcal P_n:=
\left\{
H_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:
a_u\in\{\ell_n,\ldots,H_n\},\
\sum_{u=1}^k a_u=H_n
\right\}.
\]

\item Define the clipped effect grid by
\[
\mathcal T_n:=
\left([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\cap q_n\mathbb Z\right)^k .
\]
Set
\[
\mathcal A_n:=
\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n,
\]
with the product ordered lexicographically.

\item For each \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal A_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta
:=
VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\qquad
m_\vartheta
:=
VR^\top p,
\qquad
b_\vartheta
:=
RV^\top e_1,
\]
\[
\lambda_\vartheta
:=
\sum_{u=1}^k p_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and
\[
J_n(\vartheta)
:=
\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+
\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2 .
\]

\item Let \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) be the first lexicographic minimizer of \(J_n\) over \(\mathcal A_n\):
\[
\widehat\vartheta_n
:=
\min_{\mathrm{lex}}
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n}J_n(\vartheta).
\]
The structured-lattice quotient-law estimator is
\[
\widehat\lambda_n
:=
\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

eddf9d06b1347bf1f2aa43b32bc26eff60586b49.title: Finite-library program \(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\)
eddf9d06b1347bf1f2aa43b32bc26eff60586b49.body:
For a stored representative library \(A=(A_i)_i\), observed sample \(\omega\), threshold \(s_0/2=\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\), and empirical summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), the finite-library spectral program is defined as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each stored representative \(A_i\), define its stacked proxy moment by
\[
S_i
:=
\operatorname{stack}(M_0(A_i),M_1(A_i)).
\]

\item Let \(V_i\) be the matrix of the \(k\) right singular directions of \(S_i\) whose singular values exceed \(s_0/2\). Define
\[
\Delta_i
:=
\{M_1(A_i)V_i\}^{\dagger}N_1(A_i)V_i
-
\{M_0(A_i)V_i\}^{\dagger}N_0(A_i)V_i,
\]
\[
a_i^\top:=m_X(A_i)^\top V_i,
\qquad
c_i:=V_i^\top e_1 .
\]

\item For each distinct real eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\Delta_i\), define the spectral projector polynomial by
\[
E_{\lambda,i}
:=
\prod_{\gamma\ne\lambda}
\frac{\Delta_i-\gamma I_k}{\lambda-\gamma},
\]
with the empty product equal to \(I_k\). The thresholded exact-real spectral effect law is
\[
\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_i)
:=
\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta_i)}
a_i^\top E_{\lambda,i}c_i\,\delta_\lambda .
\]

\item Let \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)\) denote the position of \(A_i\) in the fixed lexicographic library order.

\item When the library contains at least one representative, let \(i^\star\) be a nearest representative of smallest lexicographic rank:
\[
i^\star
\in
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_i d_S(S_i,\widehat S_n(\omega)),
\]
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i^\star)
=
\min\left\{
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i):
i\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_j d_S(S_j,\widehat S_n(\omega))
\right\}.
\]
The program returns
\[
\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)
:=
(A_{i^\star},\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_{i^\star})).
\]

\item When the library is empty, the program returns the canonical zero law:
\[
\operatorname{law}(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega))
:=
\delta_0 .
\]
In all cases,
\[
\operatorname{law}(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega))
\]
denotes the returned effect-law component.
\end{enumerate}

99310df944bc9f20c8bde0ee2723e360663f2f5f.title: Two-class witness law
99310df944bc9f20c8bde0ee2723e360663f2f5f.body:
For every perturbation \(\varepsilon\) with
\[
0\le \varepsilon \le \frac18,
\]
the explicit two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\), with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), belongs to \(\mathcal M\). Moreover,
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Treatment masses.)}
\[
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=0)=\frac{12}{25},
\qquad
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=1)=\frac{13}{25}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Proxy determinants.)}
\[
\det(B)=\frac35,
\qquad
\det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=\frac25.
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed proxy moments.)}
\[
\det(M_0(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=\frac{3}{50},
\qquad
\det(M_1(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))
=\frac25\cdot\frac35\cdot\frac{36}{169}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Latent masses.)}
\[
p_1=\frac25,
\qquad
p_2=\frac35.
\]
\item \textbf{(Quotient law.)}
\[
\nu_{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}}
=
\frac25\,\delta_{1/4-\varepsilon}
+
\frac35\,\delta_{1/4+\varepsilon}.
\]
\end{itemize}
At \(\varepsilon=0\), the target-proxy matrix \(B\) and both reference-proxy matrices \(A_0,A_1\) are nonsingular, the quotient law is
\[
\nu_{P_{0}^{\mathrm{wit}}}=\delta_{1/4},
\]
and the two latent masses are \(2/5\) and \(3/5\).

0aca2b7442d7afa5a7ff127448b987c439401e91.title: Honest root-\(n\) confidence
0aca2b7442d7afa5a7ff127448b987c439401e91.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\) and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) for which the following holds. With
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
the prescribed structured-lattice constant is positive and is given by
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\bigl(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f\bigr)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\},
\]
where
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}\,L}{\sigma_0}
+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}}.
\end{gathered}
\]
For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\), summary-space repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\), and a prescribed structured lattice in the sense of \cref{obj:def:structured-lattice-program}, such that for every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set}, formed using \(C_0\), \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and \(\widehat\lambda_n\), satisfy the following assertions.

For every sample, both sets are nonempty, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) admits its constrained finite-transport representation around \(\widehat\lambda_n\):
\[
\nu\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\nu\in\mathcal P_{\le k,\pi_0}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\ \text{and there exists a transport plan from \(\nu\) to \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with cost at most \(R_{n,\alpha}\)}.
\]
For every full-data law \(P\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\nu_P\in \mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For every sample,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le
4C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le
2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

51d89160abfa955855b28c8410751486bd0f7349.title: Structured lattice program \(\widehat\lambda_n\)
51d89160abfa955855b28c8410751486bd0f7349.body:
At sample size \(n\), the structured lattice program takes the empirical summaries, the margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\), the effect-support radius \(L_\tau\), and the lattice scale \(H_n\) as inputs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define vertical stacking by
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0,M_1):=[M_0^\top,M_1^\top]^\top .
\]

\item Set
\[
s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\qquad
q_n:=H_n^{-1}.
\]
Threshold the empirical signal space at \(s_0/2\), and define
\[
\widehat D_n
:=
(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}
-
(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.
\]

\item Let \(\mathcal V_n\) be the prescribed grid of polar factors, \(\mathcal R_n\) the grid of invertible conditioning matrices with singular value at least \(\sigma_0/2\), \(\mathcal P_n\) the simplex grid with every coordinate at least \(\pi_0\), and \(\mathcal T_n\) the clipped effect grid in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]^k\). Define
\[
\mathcal A_n
:=
\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n,
\]
with lexicographic product order.

\item For each \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal A_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta
:=
VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\qquad
m_\vartheta
:=
VR^\top p,
\qquad
b_\vartheta
:=
RV^\top e_1,
\]
\[
\lambda_\vartheta
:=
\sum_u p_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and
\[
J_n(\vartheta)
:=
\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+
\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2 .
\]

\item The operation count for the structured lattice program is the number of evaluated lattice objectives:
\[
\operatorname{ops}(\mathcal A_n)
:=
\#\{\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n:J_n(\vartheta)\ \text{is evaluated}\}
=
|\mathcal A_n|.
\]

\item Let \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) be the first lexicographic minimizer of \(J_n\) over \(\mathcal A_n\):
\[
\widehat\vartheta_n
:=
\min_{\mathrm{lex}}
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n}J_n(\vartheta).
\]
The structured-lattice quotient-law estimator is
\[
\widehat\lambda_n
:=
\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}.
\]
