efbd6ecd599a893db1bb5e5db54a35a548a95892.title: Honest root-n confidence sets
efbd6ecd599a893db1bb5e5db54a35a548a95892.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\) and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) for which the following holds. With
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
the prescribed structured-lattice constant is positive and is given by
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\bigl(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f\bigr)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\},
\]
where
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}\,L}{\sigma_0}
+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}}.
\end{gathered}
\]
For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) and summary-space repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\) such that \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is generated by an exhaustive finite list of well-formed structured-lattice candidates, the list has exactly its stated candidate count and no duplicate candidate coordinates, its ordering agrees with the lexicographic candidate order, and \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the law attached to the first lexicographic minimizer of the structured-lattice criterion. For every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set}, formed using \(C_0\), \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and \(\widehat\lambda_n\), satisfy the following assertions.

For every sample, both sets are nonempty, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) admits its constrained finite-transport representation around \(\widehat\lambda_n\):
\[
\nu\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\nu\in\mathcal P_{\le k,\pi_0}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\ \text{and there exists a transport plan from \(\nu\) to \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with cost at most \(R_{n,\alpha}\)}.
\]
For every full-data probability law \(P\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\nu_P\in \mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For every sample,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le
4C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le
2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

925123c0cb99c6fd06116d52a7ac5fcb1dfd2574.title: Polynomial lattice estimator
925123c0cb99c6fd06116d52a7ac5fcb1dfd2574.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Set
\[
L_\tau:=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\qquad
s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\]
and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_V&:=4\sqrt{d_xk},
&K_D&:=\frac{4\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},
&A_D&:=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\\
K_f&:=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},
&c_D&:=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m&:=2\sqrt{k}Lc_V+k+kL,
&c_b&:=k+2\sqrt{k}Lc_V,
&c_{\mathrm{grid}}&:=c_D+c_m+c_b,\\
B_{\mathrm{lat}}&:=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
&&C_{\mathrm{lat}}:=\max\left\{\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}>0\), and there is a constant
\(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), there is an estimator
\(\widehat\lambda_n\) with values in quotient laws having at most \(k\) atoms in
\([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\) with the following properties.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structured lattice rule.)} With \(m_\star:=\pi_0\),
\[
H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k
+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,
\qquad
q_n:=H_n^{-1},
\qquad
\ell_n:=\lceil m_\star H_n\rceil .
\]
The estimator is induced by a total Borel summary rule applied to the empirical summary
\(\widehat S_n\) of \cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}.  Its finite candidate list is exactly the prescribed structured lattice: it contains every well-formed point
\(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\) once, is ordered lexicographically, and chooses the first minimizer of
\[
J_n(\vartheta):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2 .
\]
Here
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\qquad
m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,
\qquad
b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\qquad
\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^k p_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and \(\widehat\lambda_n=\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}\) for the selected first minimizer.
\item \textbf{(Atom floor.)} The estimator has atom-floor parameter \(\pi_0\): for every sample, every distinct represented atom of \(\widehat\lambda_n\) has aggregate mass at least \(\pi_0\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold recovery.)} For every full-data law \(P\in\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, the stacked proxy moment at \(S(P)\) satisfies
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j\!\left(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(P),M_1(P))\right)
\quad\text{for all }j<k,
\]
and
\[
\sigma_j\!\left(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(P),M_1(P))\right)<\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}
\quad\text{for all }j\ge k.
\]
Moreover, every summary \(s\) with
\(d_S(s,S(P))<\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) satisfies the same two threshold inequalities at threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).
\item \textbf{(Complexity.)} The candidate list and exhaustive minimization obey
\[
\#\mathcal A_n\le
C\,n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2},
\]
and, with \(\operatorname{ops}(\mathcal A_n):=n+\#\mathcal A_n\),
\[
\operatorname{ops}(\mathcal A_n)\le
C\left\{n+n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Deterministic accuracy.)} For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every sample,
\[
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left\{
d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}
\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Uniform tail bound.)} For every \(0<\eta<1/2\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}\le \eta .
\]
\end{itemize}

0bf560e721b3de061902e267e06f3b783edde227.title: Effect gap \(\delta(P)\)
0bf560e721b3de061902e267e06f3b783edde227.body:
The effect gap is
\[
\delta(P)
:=
\min\bigl\{|\tau_u-\tau_v|:\ p_u>0,\ p_v>0,\ \tau_u\ne\tau_v\bigr\}.
\]
If the quotient law has a single distinct support point, set
\[
\delta(P):=+\infty.
\]

9093fa981879f044cacbe4b31110c0d2528b59f0.title: Empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\)
9093fa981879f044cacbe4b31110c0d2528b59f0.body:
For each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the armwise treatment count by
\[
N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}.
\]
The empirical armwise moments are
\[
\widehat M_{t,n}
:=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Z_iX_i^\top}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}},
\qquad
\widehat N_{t,n}
:=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Y_iZ_iX_i^\top}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}}.
\]
The empirical target-proxy mean is
\[
\widehat m_{X,n}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i.
\]
The total empirical observable summary is
\[
\widehat S_n
:=
\bigl(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},
\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n}\bigr).
\]
On the event \(\{N_{t,n}=0\}\), the corresponding armwise matrices are the zero matrix, so \(\widehat S_n\) is a total Borel function of the sample.

3a93dce6e375f5db145e7efe4c8d7249f1f64d2c.title: Gap-free modulus extension
3a93dce6e375f5db145e7efe4c8d7249f1f64d2c.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(k\) is the latent cardinality with \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Set
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal M\) be the collection of probability laws satisfying the uniformly conditioned model with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), let \(S(P)\) denote the observable summary of \(P\), and let
\[
\mathcal K=\overline{\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\}}.
\]
For summaries \(s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\) and
\(q=(M'_0,M'_1,N'_0,N'_1,m'_X)\), write
\[
d_S(s,q)=
\|M_0-M'_0\|+\|M_1-M'_1\|
+\|N_0-N'_0\|+\|N_1-N'_1\|
+\left(\sum_i (m_X(i)-m'_X(i))^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Then there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\), depending on
\((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), such that, for every \(P,Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
W_1(\nu_P,\nu_Q)\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(S(P),S(Q)).
\]
Moreover, there is a continuous and Borel measurable map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
such that, for all \(q,q'\in\mathcal K\),
\[
W_1(\overline F(q),\overline F(q'))\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q'),
\]
and, for every \(Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
\overline F(S(Q))=\nu_Q.
\]
This map is unique among continuous maps
\(G:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) satisfying the same
\(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\)-Lipschitz bound and agreeing with \(Q\mapsto\nu_Q\) on every admissible summary \(S(Q)\).

d85e1ec59e499a6cfcc9f2e5535702a5840ef1a7.title: Structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\)
d85e1ec59e499a6cfcc9f2e5535702a5840ef1a7.body:
At sample size \(n\), for an empirical five-block summary \(s\), the estimator is defined as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Set
\[
H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,\qquad
q_n:=H_n^{-1},\qquad
s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2 .
\]
For matrices \(M_0,M_1\), write
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0,M_1):=[M_0^\top,M_1^\top]^\top .
\]
\item Form the thresholded empirical compressed operator
\[
\widehat D_n(s):=(M_1(s))^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}N_1(s)-(M_0(s))^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}N_0(s).
\]
\item Let \(\mathcal V_n\) be the prescribed \(q_n\)-grid of polar factors, \(\mathcal R_n\) the \(q_n\)-grid of invertible conditioning matrices with singular value at least \(\sigma_0/2\), \(\mathcal P_n\) the \(H_n^{-1}\)-simplex grid with every coordinate at least \(\pi_0\), and \(\mathcal T_n\) the clipped \(q_n\)-effect grid in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]^k\). Define the lexicographically ordered candidate set
\[
\mathcal A_n:=\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n .
\]
\item For each \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal A_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,\qquad
m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,\qquad
b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\]
and
\[
\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^k p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.
\]
\item Evaluate
\[
J_n(\vartheta;s):=
\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n(s)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-m_X(s)\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2 .
\]
Let
\[
\widehat\vartheta_n(s):=
\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n} J_n(\vartheta;s).
\]
For a sample \(\omega\) with empirical summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), output
\[
\widehat\lambda_n(\omega):=\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n(\widehat S_n(\omega))}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

28c7314d280fe6019a5d9b9fba7ee6a4f58907d1.title: Finite-library program \(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\)
28c7314d280fe6019a5d9b9fba7ee6a4f58907d1.body:
For a stored representative library \(A=(A_i)_i\) and an observed sample \(\omega\), the program is defined as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each representative \(A_i\), let \(S_i\) be its stored five-block summary and let
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)
\]
be its position in the fixed lexicographic library order.
\item Define the real atomic effect law returned by the thresholded exact-real spectral run for \(A_i\) as
\[
\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_i).
\]
\item With empirical summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), compute
\[
d_i(\omega):=
\lVert M_0(S_i)-\widehat M_{0,n}(\omega)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert M_1(S_i)-\widehat M_{1,n}(\omega)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert N_0(S_i)-\widehat N_{0,n}(\omega)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert N_1(S_i)-\widehat N_{1,n}(\omega)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_X(S_i)-\widehat m_{X,n}(\omega)\rVert_2 .
\]
\item If the library is nonempty, select
\[
i^\star(\omega):=
\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\operatorname*{arg\,min}_i d_i(\omega).
\]
The program returns
\[
\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega):=\bigl(A_{i^\star(\omega)},\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_{i^\star(\omega)})\bigr),
\]
and its effect-law component is
\[
\operatorname{law}(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega))
:=\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_{i^\star(\omega)}).
\]
\item If the library is empty, the program returns the canonical zero law,
\[
\operatorname{law}(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)):=\delta_0 .
\]
\end{enumerate}

34c07435b695a122679b69b58264d7bb517f78a5.title: Distinct positive-mass effects
34c07435b695a122679b69b58264d7bb517f78a5.body: The positive-mass latent effects \(\tau_u\) take exactly \(k\) distinct values.

c27685be9bc973e875d1ce5a150f322b8b7d860f.title: Local quotient neighborhood
c27685be9bc973e875d1ce5a150f322b8b7d860f.body: The Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(P_O\) to the observed margin of the two-class collision witness at perturbation zero is at most \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}/n\).

c406de9a6e4bf630c498635a63d15132c63c9046.title: Local weight neighborhood
c406de9a6e4bf630c498635a63d15132c63c9046.body: The Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(P_O\) to the observed margin of the two-class witness at perturbation \(g/2\) is at most \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}/n\).

c3ca0a4ea3f8be9986b38ba0ea6dbf0e26124413.title: Gap-free modulus
c3ca0a4ea3f8be9986b38ba0ea6dbf0e26124413.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent dimension.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Set
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal M\) be the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class with parameters
\((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\). For a five-block summary \(s\), write its coordinate projections as
\[
s=\bigl(M_0(s),M_1(s),N_0(s),N_1(s),m_X(s)\bigr),
\]
where \(M_t(s)\) is the \(t\)-th \(ZX^\top\)-moment block, \(N_t(s)\) is the \(t\)-th \(YZX^\top\)-moment block, and \(m_X(s)\) is the target-proxy mean block. Define
\[
\mathcal K=\overline{\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\}},
\]
and, for summaries \(s,q\),
\[
d_S(s,q)=
\|M_0(s)-M_0(q)\|+\|M_1(s)-M_1(q)\|
+\|N_0(s)-N_0(q)\|+\|N_1(s)-N_1(q)\|
+\left(\sum_i (m_X(s)_i-m_X(q)_i)^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Then there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) such that, for every \(P,Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
W_1(\nu_P,\nu_Q)\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(S(P),S(Q)).
\]
Moreover, there is a continuous and Borel measurable map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
such that, for all \(q,q'\in\mathcal K\),
\[
W_1(\overline F(q),\overline F(q'))\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q'),
\]
and, for every \(Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
\overline F(S(Q))=\nu_Q.
\]
The map \(\overline F\) is unique among continuous maps
\(G:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) satisfying
\[
W_1(G(q),G(q'))\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q')
\]
for all \(q,q'\in\mathcal K\) and
\[
G(S(Q))=\nu_Q
\]
for every \(Q\in\mathcal M\).

7e09376b563505d2f262562ba9124b407e725be3.title: Structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\)
7e09376b563505d2f262562ba9124b407e725be3.body:
At sample size \(n\), for an empirical five-block summary \(s\), the estimator is defined as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Write the coordinate projections of a five-block summary \(s\) as
\[
M_t(s):=s.M_t,\qquad
N_t(s):=s.N_t,\qquad
m_X(s):=s.m_X,\qquad t\in\{0,1\}.
\]
\item Set
\[
H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,\qquad
q_n:=H_n^{-1},\qquad
s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2 .
\]
For matrices \(M_0,M_1\), write
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0,M_1):=[M_0^\top,M_1^\top]^\top .
\]
\item Form the thresholded empirical compressed operator
\[
\widehat D_n(s):=(M_1(s))^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}N_1(s)-(M_0(s))^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}N_0(s).
\]
\item Let \(\mathcal V_n\) be the prescribed \(q_n\)-grid of polar factors, \(\mathcal R_n\) the \(q_n\)-grid of invertible conditioning matrices with singular value at least \(\sigma_0/2\), \(\mathcal P_n\) the \(H_n^{-1}\)-simplex grid with every coordinate at least \(\pi_0\), and \(\mathcal T_n\) the clipped \(q_n\)-effect grid in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]^k\). Define the lexicographically ordered candidate set
\[
\mathcal A_n:=\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n .
\]
\item For each \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal A_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,\qquad
m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,\qquad
b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\]
and
\[
\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^k p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.
\]
\item Evaluate
\[
J_n(\vartheta;s):=
\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n(s)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-m_X(s)\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2 .
\]
Let
\[
\widehat\vartheta_n(s):=
\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n} J_n(\vartheta;s).
\]
For a sample \(\omega\) with empirical five-block summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), output
\[
\widehat\lambda_n(\omega):=\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n(\widehat S_n(\omega))}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

\]
\item For each representative \(A_i\), let \(S_i\) be its stored five-block summary and let
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)

852c175b814e63997c56e3096a9c8462e352d067.title: Local KL radius constant \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\)
852c175b814e63997c56e3096a9c8462e352d067.body:

4f6a5e85f00e6e6c00956275c42e57c71dbfe9fd.title: Honest root-\(n\) confidence
4f6a5e85f00e6e6c00956275c42e57c71dbfe9fd.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\) and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) for which the following holds. With
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
the prescribed structured-lattice constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is positive and is given by
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\bigl(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f\bigr)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\},
\]
where
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}\,L}{\sigma_0}
+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}}.
\end{gathered}
\]
For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\), summary-space repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\), and a prescribed structured lattice in the sense of \cref{obj:def:structured-lattice-program}, such that for every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set}, formed using \(C_0\), \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and \(\widehat\lambda_n\), satisfy the following assertions.

For every sample, both sets are nonempty, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) admits its constrained finite-transport representation around \(\widehat\lambda_n\):
\[
\nu\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\nu\in\mathcal P_{\le k,\pi_0}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\ \text{and there exists a transport plan from \(\nu\) to \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with cost at most \(R_{n,\alpha}\)}.
\]
For every full-data probability law \(P\) satisfying the model conditions in \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\nu_P\in \mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For every sample,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le
4C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le
2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

453469df887eae9d95da371e37527934e8e4d11e.title: Honest root-\(n\) confidence
453469df887eae9d95da371e37527934e8e4d11e.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\) and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).

\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
the prescribed structured-lattice constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is positive and is given by
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\bigl(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f\bigr)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\},
\]
where
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad

c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}}.
\end{gathered}

The estimator is represented by an exhaustive finite list of well-formed structured-lattice candidates, the list is unique up to equality of its four candidate coordinates and ordered lexicographically, and \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the effect law of the first lexicographic minimizer of the structured-lattice criterion \(J_n\) evaluated at the empirical summary.

For every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set}, formed using \(C_0\), \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and \(\widehat\lambda_n\), satisfy the following assertions.

For every sample, both sets are nonempty, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) admits its constrained finite-transport representation around \(\widehat\lambda_n\):
\[
\nu\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\nu\in\mathcal P_{\le k,\pi_0}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\ \text{and there exists a transport plan from \(\nu\) to \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with cost at most \(R_{n,\alpha}\)}.
\]
For every full-data law \(P\) satisfying the model conditions in \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\nu_P\in \mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For every sample,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le
4C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le
2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

6229369f69501d6e9f71fa038ba71b0c77c8181c.title: Kullback--Leibler divergence \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\Vert\nu)\)
6229369f69501d6e9f71fa038ba71b0c77c8181c.body:
For probability laws \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) on the same measurable space,
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\Vert\nu)
\]
denotes their Kullback--Leibler divergence, with value \(+\infty\) unless \(\mu\) is absolutely continuous with respect to \(\nu\).

5aba769c8fc71c27a7645c089ef2dc418e3539ee.title: Empirical summary primitives \(\widehat S_n\)
5aba769c8fc71c27a7645c089ef2dc418e3539ee.body:
For an observed sample \((T_i,X_i,Z_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\), define the armwise counts by
\[
N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{T_i=t\},
\qquad t\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The armwise empirical proxy moment and outcome-proxy moment are
\[
\widehat M_{t,n}
:=
\frac{1}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}}
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{T_i=t\} Z_iX_i^\top,
\qquad t\in\{0,1\},
\]
and
\[
\widehat N_{t,n}
:=
\frac{1}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}}
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{T_i=t\} Y_iZ_iX_i^\top,
\qquad t\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The empirical target-proxy mean is
\[
\widehat m_{X,n}:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n X_i.
\]
The empirical observable summary is
\[
\widehat S_n
:=
(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},
  \widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},
  \widehat m_{X,n}).
\]

b52bb309db3923bfda7e02dbb7942a9e178ccb90.title: First basis vector \(e_1\)
b52bb309db3923bfda7e02dbb7942a9e178ccb90.body:
Let \(e_1\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), where \(d_x\) is the target-proxy dimension, be the first canonical basis vector:
\[
e_1:=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top.
\]

88fe044a37ac046ff46fc066f818adda54cebe81.title: Two-class witness validity
88fe044a37ac046ff46fc066f818adda54cebe81.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\) with
\[
0\le \varepsilon \le \frac18,
\]
the explicit two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\), with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), belongs to \(\mathcal M\). Moreover,
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Treatment masses.)}
\[
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=0)=\frac{12}{25},
\qquad
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=1)=\frac{13}{25}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Proxy determinants.)}
\[
\det(B)=\frac35,
\qquad
\det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=\frac25.
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed proxy moments.)}
\[
\det(M_0(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=\frac{3}{50},
\qquad
\det(M_1(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))
=\frac25\cdot\frac35\cdot\frac{36}{169}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Latent masses.)}
\[
p_1=\frac25,
\qquad
p_2=\frac35.
\]
\item \textbf{(Quotient law.)}
\[
\nu_{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}}
=
\frac25\,\delta_{1/4-\varepsilon}
+
\frac35\,\delta_{1/4+\varepsilon}.
\]
\end{itemize}
At \(\varepsilon=0\), the target-proxy matrix \(B\) and both reference-proxy matrices \(A_0,A_1\) are nonsingular, the quotient law is
\[
\nu_{P_{0}^{\mathrm{wit}}}=\delta_{1/4},
\]
and the two latent masses are unequal.

33cbe408c19d4755a79892d2ff3c140c4d52ecf2.title: Honest computable confidence sets
33cbe408c19d4755a79892d2ff3c140c4d52ecf2.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Conditioning constants.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\) and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every uniform boundedness radius \(L\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) and the prescribed structured-lattice constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is positive. With
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
this constant is
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\bigl(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f\bigr)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\},
\]
where
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}\,LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}\,L}{\sigma_0}
+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}\,Lc_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}}.
\end{gathered}
\]
For every sample size \(n\ge 1\), there exist a structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\), summary-space repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\), and an exhaustive finite structured lattice whose candidates are well formed, contain each well-formed structured-lattice point exactly once, are ordered lexicographically, and whose selected candidate is the lexicographically first minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\). For every miscoverage level \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set}, formed using \(C_0\), \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and \(\widehat\lambda_n\), satisfy the following assertions.

For every sample, both sets are nonempty, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) admits its constrained finite-transport representation around \(\widehat\lambda_n\):
\[
\nu\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\nu\in\mathcal P_{\le k,\pi_0}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\ \text{and}\ 
\exists\gamma:\nu\leadsto\widehat\lambda_n
\ \text{with transport cost at most }R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
For every full-data probability law \(P\) satisfying the model conditions in \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\nu_P\in \mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For every sample,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le
4C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le
2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

519362330fa5d3c76f36a827b989dbf8a9b14fba.title: Path law \(P_{g,h}\)
519362330fa5d3c76f36a827b989dbf8a9b14fba.body:
For a gap \(g\) and displacement \(h\), define
\[
b_1(h):=0.2,
\qquad
b_2(h):=\frac{0.48-0.2h}{0.6-h},
\qquad
B_h:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1\\
b_1(h)&b_2(h)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Let
\[
(q_0,s_0):=(0.48,0.24),
\qquad
(q_1,s_1):=(0.52,0.32),
\]
and, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set
\[
w_t(h)^\top:=(q_t,s_t)(B_h^\top)^{-1},
\qquad
w_t(h)=(w_{t1}(h),w_{t2}(h))^\top .
\]
The latent masses are
\[
p(h):=
\begin{pmatrix}
0.4+h\\
0.6-h
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
p_u(h)=w_{0u}(h)+w_{1u}(h),
\qquad u\in\{1,2\}.
\]
With
\[
A_0^0:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1\\
0.3&0.7
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A_1^0:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1\\
0.35&0.75
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
B_0:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1\\
0.2&0.8
\end{pmatrix},
\]
define, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
J_t:=A_t^0\operatorname{diag}(w_t(0))B_0^\top,
\qquad
A_{t,h}:=J_t(B_h^\top)^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(w_t(h))^{-1}.
\]
The treatment probabilities and latent conditional potential-outcome means are
\[
\pi_u(h):=\frac{w_{1u}(h)}{p_u(h)},
\qquad
\mu_0:=
\begin{pmatrix}
0.25\\
0.25
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mu_1:=
\begin{pmatrix}
0.5-g/2\\
0.5+g/2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(u\in\{1,2\}\) and \(t,x,z,y_0,y_1\in\{0,1\}\), \(P_{g,h}\) assigns mass
\[
\begin{aligned}
&p_u(h)\,
\pi_u(h)^t\{1-\pi_u(h)\}^{1-t}\,
b_u(h)^x\{1-b_u(h)\}^{1-x}\,
(A_{t,h})_{2u}^{z}\{1-(A_{t,h})_{2u}\}^{1-z} \\
&\qquad\qquad{}\times
\mu_{0u}^{y_0}(1-\mu_{0u})^{1-y_0}\,
\mu_{1u}^{y_1}(1-\mu_{1u})^{1-y_1}
\end{aligned}
\]
to the full-data point
\[
\bigl(U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y\bigr)
=
\bigl(u,t,(1,x)^\top,(1,z)^\top,y_0,y_1,y_t\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, the proxy factorizations along the path satisfy
\[
A_{t,h}\operatorname{diag}(w_t(h))B_h^\top=J_t,
\qquad t\in\{0,1\},
\]
and the ordered latent masses are
\[
p(h)=(0.4+h,\,0.6-h)^\top .
\]

20b655bc2c16460fb8a3dfa50de7c8c5cb16b446.title: Wasserstein confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\)
20b655bc2c16460fb8a3dfa50de7c8c5cb16b446.body:
For fixed latent cardinality \(k>0\), proxy dimensions \(d_x,d_z\), and an observed sample \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\), define the theoretical summary-inversion set and the computable Wasserstein set by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=
\begin{cases}
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\},
& \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\{\delta_0\}, & \mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]

\item Define the atom floor and radius
\[
m_\star:=\pi_0,
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\bigl(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

\item Define
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])
:=
\left\{
\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]):
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi)
\right\}.
\]

\item Define
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]):
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]

\item Merge repeated atoms of the computed center and write
\[
\widehat\lambda_n=\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\widehat w_b\delta_{\widehat x_b},
\qquad
-L_{\tau}\le\widehat x_1<\cdots<\widehat x_{\widehat r}\le L_{\tau},
\qquad
1\le\widehat r\le k.
\]

\item The set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) is the union over \(1\le r\le k\) of the laws
\[
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a\delta_{x_a}
\]
for which there exist \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\), \(w_1,\ldots,w_r\), and \((\gamma_{ab})_{1\le a\le r,\,1\le b\le\widehat r}\) satisfying
\[
-L_{\tau}\le x_1<\cdots<x_r\le L_{\tau},
\]
\[
w_a\ge m_\star,
\qquad
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a=1,
\]
\[
\gamma_{ab}\ge0,
\qquad
\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}=w_a,
\qquad
\sum_{a=1}^{r}\gamma_{ab}=\widehat w_b,
\]
and
\[
\sum_{a=1}^{r}\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}
\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\le R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

a470d20e44a6a51ce17e2aa28814de2d4f312c44.title: Ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\)
a470d20e44a6a51ce17e2aa28814de2d4f312c44.body:
Given the positive quotient-law estimator \(\widehat\nu_n\), define the ordered-weight estimator by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Write the positive law estimator uniquely as
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^{\widehat s_n}
\widehat w_{\ell,n}\delta_{\widehat\tau_{\ell,n}},
\qquad
\widehat\tau_{1,n}<\cdots<\widehat\tau_{\widehat s_n,n},
\qquad
\widehat w_{\ell,n}>0.
\]

\item Define
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}
:=
\begin{cases}
(\widehat w_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat w_{k,n}), & \widehat s_n=k,\\
(1/k,\ldots,1/k), & \widehat s_n<k.
\end{cases}
\]

\item The ordering of the finitely many support points and extraction of their jump sizes define a total Borel map
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:O_{d_x,d_z}^n\to\Delta^{k-1}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

d2c5d25abafd572bf4308e7454c5454035accc85.title: Published VMW regimes
d2c5d25abafd572bf4308e7454c5454035accc85.body: The published VMW scope handle is the cited-publication interface for the proxy-model parameter class and recovery regime. It consists of three law-level predicates, each indexed by the fixed latent cardinality \(k\), target-proxy dimension \(d_x\), reference-proxy dimension \(d_z\), and a full-data probability law \(P\) on records \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\): the published model predicate, the published finite-regularity predicate, and the published recovery-regime predicate. The finite-regularity predicate requires finite positive envelopes for \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\), positive marginal treatment-arm probabilities, and a positive population singular-value margin. The separated recovery-regime predicate additionally requires the published qualitative conditions, strict latent positivity, finite regularity, and pairwise distinct latent effects. The handle also includes the published estimator, which maps an observed sample of size \(n\) from records \((T,X,Z,Y)\) to a triple consisting of treatment effects in \(\mathbb R^k\), an anchor-normalized \(d_x\times k\) feature matrix, and simplex-projected mixture weights in \(\mathbb R^k\).

2e95f65d67992b94a2b0509bf293de5a8faa3406.title: Wasserstein confidence set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\)
2e95f65d67992b94a2b0509bf293de5a8faa3406.body:
For fixed latent cardinality \(k>0\), proxy dimensions \(d_x,d_z\), an observed sample \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) with \(O_i=(T_i,X_i,Z_i,Y_i)\in O_{d_x,d_z}\), parameters satisfying \(n>0\), \(0<\alpha<1/2\), \(1\le C_0\), \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), use the derived effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) from \(\cref{obj:def:effect-radius}\), the simultaneous concentration radius \(r_{n,\alpha}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:summary-radius}\), the repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\), and the structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) from \(\cref{obj:def:structured-lattice-program}\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the theoretical summary-inversion set by
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=
\begin{cases}
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\},
& \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\{\delta_0\}, & \mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]

\item Define the atom floor and radius by
\[
m_\star:=\pi_0,
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\bigl(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

\item Define the mass-floored atomic class by
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])
:=
\left\{
\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]):
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi)
\right\}.
\]

\item Define the computable Wasserstein set by
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]):
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]

\item Merge repeated atoms of the computed center and write
\[
\widehat\lambda_n=\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\widehat w_b\delta_{\widehat x_b},
\qquad
-L_{\tau}\le\widehat x_1<\cdots<\widehat x_{\widehat r}\le L_{\tau},
\qquad
1\le\widehat r\le k.
\]
Equivalently, \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) is the union over \(1\le r\le k\) of the laws
\[
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a\delta_{x_a}
\]
for which there exist variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\), \(w_1,\ldots,w_r\), and \(\gamma_{ab}\) satisfying
\[
-L_{\tau}\le x_1<\cdots<x_r\le L_{\tau},
\qquad
w_a\ge m_\star,
\qquad
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a=1,
\]
\[
\gamma_{ab}\ge0,
\qquad
\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}=w_a,
\qquad
\sum_{a=1}^{r}\gamma_{ab}=\widehat w_b,
\qquad
\sum_{a=1}^{r}\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}
\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\le R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

4ea4da7e305bf96221077921a52dae7cf0c0a949.title: Wasserstein confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\)
4ea4da7e305bf96221077921a52dae7cf0c0a949.body:
For fixed \(k,n,\alpha,\pi_0,C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), radius \(r_{n,\alpha}\), repair pair \((\overline F,\Pi)\), closure \(\mathcal K\), support radius \(L_\tau\), and lattice center \(\widehat\lambda_n\), define the sets as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the theoretical summary-inversion set by
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=
\begin{cases}
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\},
& \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\{\delta_0\}, & \mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]

\item Define the atom floor and computable radius by
\[
m_\star:=\pi_0,
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\bigl(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

\item Define the mass-floored atomic class by
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])
:=
\left\{
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a\delta_{x_a}:
1\le r\le k,\ 
-L_{\tau}\le x_1<\cdots<x_r\le L_{\tau},\
w_a\ge m_\star,\ 
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a=1
\right\}.
\]

\item Define the computable Wasserstein set by
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]):
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]

\item Merge repeated atoms of the center and write
\[
\widehat\lambda_n=\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\widehat w_b\delta_{\widehat x_b},
\qquad
-L_{\tau}\le\widehat x_1<\cdots<\widehat x_{\widehat r}\le L_{\tau},
\qquad
1\le\widehat r\le k.
\]
The set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) has the finite-dimensional representation
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
=
\bigcup_{r=1}^k
\left\{
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a\delta_{x_a}:
\begin{gathered}
-L_{\tau}\le x_1<\cdots<x_r\le L_{\tau},\quad
w_a\ge m_\star,\quad
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a=1,\\
\gamma_{ab}\ge0,\quad
\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}=w_a,\quad
\sum_{a=1}^{r}\gamma_{ab}=\widehat w_b,\quad
\sum_{a=1}^{r}\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}
\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\le R_{n,\alpha}
\end{gathered}
\right\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

c8803b31dd35ab2d00087813c0027772d84f3783.title: Published VMW scope handle
c8803b31dd35ab2d00087813c0027772d84f3783.body:
The published VMW scope handle consists of the following publication-level objects, indexed by the fixed latent cardinality \(k\), target-proxy dimension \(d_x\), reference-proxy dimension \(d_z\), and a full-data law \(P\) for \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Published model predicate.)} A law-level predicate specifying the published proxy-model parameter class.
\item \textbf{(Published finite-regularity predicate.)} A law-level predicate specifying the published finite-regularity regime.
\item \textbf{(Published recovery-regime predicate.)} A law-level predicate specifying the published recovery regime.
\item \textbf{(Published estimator.)} For each sample size \(n\), an estimator that maps an observed sample in \(O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) to a triple consisting of treatment effects in \(\mathbb R^k\), an anchor-normalized feature matrix in \(\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\), and weight coordinates in \(\mathbb R^k\).
\end{itemize}

22f5cc8c3f3463fc655407cdce8a32afe769b47d.title: Wasserstein confidence sets \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\)
22f5cc8c3f3463fc655407cdce8a32afe769b47d.body:
Given tuning parameters \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0,\alpha,C_0,C_{\mathrm{lat}}\in\mathbb R\), an observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\) on \(\mathcal K\), and a prescribed structured-lattice estimator, define the confidence sets as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Impose the parameter conditions
\[
0<k,\qquad 0<n,\qquad 1\le L,\qquad 0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1},\qquad 0<\alpha<\frac12,\qquad 1\le C_0,\qquad 0<C_{\mathrm{lat}}.
\]
Set the derived effect-support radius
\[
L_\tau:=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
and assume
\[
0\le L_\tau.
\]

\item Let \(\widehat S_n\) be the empirical five-block observable summary of \(\omega\), and define the simultaneous concentration radius
\[
r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]

\item Let \((\overline F,\Pi)\) satisfy the repair conditions
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
is continuous and extends the summary-to-quotient-law map on model summaries,
\[
\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{q\in\mathcal K} d_S(q,s)\quad\text{whenever }\mathcal K\ne\varnothing,
\]
\[
\Pi(s)=0\quad\text{whenever }\mathcal K=\varnothing,
\]
and the induced repaired estimator is measurable.

\item Let \(\widehat\lambda_n\) be the valid \(k\)-atomic law returned at \(\omega\) by a measurable prescribed structured-lattice estimator at support radius \(L_\tau\). The estimator is generated by an exhaustive duplicate-free lexicographically ordered list of well-formed \(H_n,q_n\) lattice candidates and selects the first lexicographic minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\) with threshold
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}.
\]

\item Define the original summary-inversion confidence set
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=
\begin{cases}
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le 2r_{n,\alpha}\},& \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\{\delta_0\},& \mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]

\item Define the atom-floor constant and computable radius by
\[
m_\star:=\pi_0,
\]
\[
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\bigl(r_{n,\alpha}+(\sqrt n)^{-1}\bigr).
\]

\item Define the mass-floor subclass
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi)\}.
\]

\item Output the computable \(W_1\) confidence set centered at \(\widehat\lambda_n\):
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi),\
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

fa3c3e76876998620c8aa606f0af21c10336bcb6.title: Ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\)
fa3c3e76876998620c8aa606f0af21c10336bcb6.body:
Given the quotient-law estimator \(\widehat\nu_n\), define \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Write the positive law estimator uniquely as
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^{\widehat s_n}
\widehat w_{\ell,n}\delta_{\widehat\tau_{\ell,n}},
\qquad
\widehat\tau_{1,n}<\cdots<\widehat\tau_{\widehat s_n,n},
\qquad
\widehat w_{\ell,n}>0
\quad
(1\le \ell\le \widehat s_n).
\]
\item If \(\widehat s_n=k\), set
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}
=
(\widehat w_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat w_{k,n}).
\]
\item If \(\widehat s_n<k\), set
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}
=
(1/k,\ldots,1/k).
\]
\item The output is the total Borel map
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\in\Delta^{k-1}.
\]
Ordering the finitely many support points and extracting their jump sizes are Borel operations, and the declared inputs of the construction are \(\widehat\nu_n\) and \(k\).
\end{enumerate}

b8d50a727d2f0b917bb65ed2e206a49a6589c0e7.title: Arm mass lower bound
b8d50a727d2f0b917bb65ed2e206a49a6589c0e7.body:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law on \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), with fixed latent cardinality \(k\), target-proxy dimension \(d_x\), and reference-proxy dimension \(d_z\).  Suppose that \(P\) satisfies the latent-arm positivity condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}\) with latent-arm positivity margin \(\pi_0\).  Then, for every treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
k\pi_0 \le P(T=t).
\]

b0e4c4908848da3e603a3407004bceaaf0f1e3e6.title: Coordinate envelope bounds
b0e4c4908848da3e603a3407004bceaaf0f1e3e6.body:
Let \(P\), a full-data law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), be indexed by latent cardinality \(k\), target-proxy dimension \(d_x\), reference-proxy dimension \(d_z\), and uniform boundedness radius \(L\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Target dimension.)} \(k\le d_x\).
\end{itemize}
Then, \(P\)-almost surely,
\[
|X_i|\le L\quad\text{for every }1\le i\le d_x,
\qquad
|Z_j|\le L\quad\text{for every }1\le j\le d_z,
\qquad
|Y Z_j|\le L\quad\text{for every }1\le j\le d_z.
\]

62eacee6433e67ed0bc49bdbf5b0f2a37a8a2d9a.title: Latent mean envelope
62eacee6433e67ed0bc49bdbf5b0f2a37a8a2d9a.body:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law.  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(L\ge 1\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and every treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the latent conditional potential-outcome mean \(\mu_{tu}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:latent-mean}\) satisfies
\[
|\mu_{tu}|\le \frac{L_\tau}{2},
\]
where \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) is the derived effect-support radius in \(\cref{obj:def:effect-radius}\).

d2f823714f6297967f371e34fe27c545d51bea06.title: Observed proxy moment factorization
d2f823714f6297967f371e34fe27c545d51bea06.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(2\le k\) and \(k\le d_x\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform bounds.)} \(1\le L\) and \(0<\pi_0\).
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise \(ZX^\top\) moment \(M_t(P)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}\) satisfies
\[
M_t(P)=A_t\,\Gamma_t\,B^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma_t=\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\},
\]
where \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix in \(\cref{obj:def:reference-feature}\) and \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix in \(\cref{obj:def:target-feature}\).

f022a05e4c12192afcdd140bc78943b1c8368765.title: Witness latent masses
f022a05e4c12192afcdd140bc78943b1c8368765.body:
Let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) be the two-class Bernoulli witness law from \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\), and let \(p_u\) denote the latent-class mass from \(\cref{obj:def:latent-mass}\). For every \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
0\le \varepsilon\le \frac18
\]
and every latent class \(u\in\{1,2\}\),
\[
p_u(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})
=
\begin{cases}
\frac25, & u=1,\\[2pt]
\frac35, & u=2.
\end{cases}
\]

75b526cf9ad5042fe978c54830b6e9cf4db4fa90.title: Witness latent effects
75b526cf9ad5042fe978c54830b6e9cf4db4fa90.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\) with \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\), let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) be the two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law in \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\).  For every latent class \(u\in\{1,2\}\), the latent-class treatment effect \(\tau_u\) from \(\cref{obj:def:latent-effect}\) satisfies
\[
\tau_u(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})
=
\begin{cases}
\frac14-\varepsilon, & u=1,\\
\frac14+\varepsilon, & u=2.
\end{cases}
\]

fc0f92e99490f1dad23868ce65b9124d6a89fdf3.title: Latent effect envelope
fc0f92e99490f1dad23868ce65b9124d6a89fdf3.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P\) be a full-data law in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform bounds.)} \(1\le L\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\) satisfies the model conditions in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), the latent-class treatment effect \(\tau_u=\mu_{1u}-\mu_{0u}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:latent-effect}\) is bounded by the derived effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) from \(\cref{obj:def:effect-radius}\):
\[
|\tau_u|\le L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]

bfd55425a43d3bd6a73bbe948e46cc0a1e7498fd.title: Witness determinant calculation
bfd55425a43d3bd6a73bbe948e46cc0a1e7498fd.body:
For every real \(\varepsilon\) with \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\), let \(B\) be the target-proxy feature matrix of the two-class Bernoulli witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \cref{obj:def:target-feature,obj:def:two-class-witness}. Then its \(2\times2\) determinant is
\[
B_{00}B_{11}-B_{01}B_{10}=\frac35 .
\]

a092bfffb6935d0ad89a64552975706a9fd14a11.title: Witness reference determinant
a092bfffb6935d0ad89a64552975706a9fd14a11.body:
Let \(A_t\) denote the reference-proxy feature matrix of the two-class Bernoulli witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness,obj:def:reference-feature}. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Witness scale.)} The collision-witness effect displacement satisfies \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment arm.)} The arm \(t\) belongs to \(\{0,1\}\).
\end{itemize}
For a \(2\times 2\) matrix \(A\), write \(\det(A)=A_{00}A_{11}-A_{01}A_{10}\). Then
\[
\det(A_t)=\frac{2}{5}.
\]

8cfd0fec5acfd75c41fb5db704c2a460b57c5657.title: Observed arm masses

367c80becb4d612dfab2a038c11c1d412e30ccd9.title: Path proxy-rank margin
367c80becb4d612dfab2a038c11c1d412e30ccd9.body:
For real numbers \(g\) and \(h\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative gap.)} \(0\le g\).
\item \textbf{(Gap range.)} \(g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path amplitude.)} \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(P_{g,h}\) be the factorization-preserving two-class path law of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family}. Then \(P_{g,h}\) satisfies the proxy-rank margin of \cref{obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin} with \(\sigma_0=1/10\): for the reference-proxy feature matrices \(A_0(P_{g,h})\) and \(A_1(P_{g,h})\) from \cref{obj:def:reference-feature} and the target-proxy feature matrix \(B(P_{g,h})\) from \cref{obj:def:target-feature},
\[
\min\bigl\{\sigma_{\min}(A_0(P_{g,h})),\sigma_{\min}(A_1(P_{g,h})),\sigma_{\min}(B(P_{g,h}))\bigr\}\ge 1/10.
\]

96ca1136d174c6073a4b00b3c708465c7394e495.title: Path model membership

66ae63359debea2248b83780580a92d6f4e280cd.title: Path stratum membership
66ae63359debea2248b83780580a92d6f4e280cd.body:
For real numbers \(g\) and \(h\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(0<g\).
\item \textbf{(Small gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Small path perturbation.)} The path perturbation satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) from \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum} with constants \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). In particular, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, the gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\), its smallest positive effect gap from \cref{obj:def:effect-gap} obeys
\[
\frac{g}{2}\le \delta(P_{g,h})\le 2g,
\]
indeed \(\delta(P_{g,h})=g\), and its two latent effects from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} are distinct.

19617210583cbbc8a0f378fa1a2e7ebe31e5a635.title: Path local experiment membership
19617210583cbbc8a0f378fa1a2e7ebe31e5a635.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in\mathbb R\) be the local Kullback--Leibler radius constant of \cref{obj:def:local-kl-radius}, and let \(g,h\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Local radius.)} \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1\).
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Local KL calibration.)}
\[
16000\,g^2h^2\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
For the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family}, \(P_{g,h}\) belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) of \cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment} with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).  Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\) lies in the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}, and its observed-data marginal satisfies the neighborhood bound
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\Vert(P_{g,0})_O\right)\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n},
\qquad
P_{g,0}=P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}.
\]

8254b9036adb4c97e353e0c7a4a9e75d01061e7d.title: Ordered mass invariance
8254b9036adb4c97e353e0c7a4a9e75d01061e7d.body:
Let \(k\in\mathbb N\) and let \(L_\tau\in\mathbb R\).  Let \(\xi\) and \(\xi'\) be represented atomic laws with \(k\) labelled slots as in \(\cref{obj:def:atomic-law-class}\).  If they represent the same probability law,
\[
\nu_\xi=\nu_{\xi'},
\]
then their effect-ordered mass vectors from \(\cref{obj:def:ordered-mass-target}\) coincide:
\[
p^{\uparrow}(\xi)=p^{\uparrow}(\xi').
\]

d4a4cdf857fb1b8eab08ff36efbb5812b37c5265.title: Latent mean envelope
d4a4cdf857fb1b8eab08ff36efbb5812b37c5265.body:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law.  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(L\ge 1\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with the bounded-target-proxy, latent-arm-positivity, and proxy-rank-margin conditions in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}
Then, for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and every treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the latent conditional potential-outcome mean \(\mu_{tu}\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-mean} satisfies
\[
|\mu_{tu}|\le \frac{L_\tau}{2},
\]
where \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) is the derived effect-support radius in \cref{obj:def:effect-radius}.

b9a3193f7cece2131a9c855171b0f14353f07146.title: Latent effect envelope
b9a3193f7cece2131a9c855171b0f14353f07146.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P\) be a full-data probability law in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform bounds.)} \(1\le L\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\) satisfies the model conditions in \cref{obj:def:model-class} with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), including the bounded target-proxy condition in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}, the latent-arm positivity condition in \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}, and the proxy-rank margin condition in \cref{obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}
Then, for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), the latent-class treatment effect \(\tau_u=\mu_{1u}-\mu_{0u}\) of \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} satisfies
\[
|\tau_u|\le L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
where \(L_\tau\) is the derived effect-support radius in \cref{obj:def:effect-radius}.

fbdd322371729c6b142475f4e57b1f0f5d65377b.title: Proxy moment factorization
fbdd322371729c6b142475f4e57b1f0f5d65377b.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\) and \(k\le d_x\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(1\le L\) and \(0<\pi_0\), where \(\pi_0\) is the latent-arm positivity margin.
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\). This includes the reference- and target-proxy separation conditions in \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation}, the bounded target-proxy condition in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}, and the latent-arm positivity condition in \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}.
\end{itemize}
Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise \(ZX^\top\) moment \(M_t(P)\) from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments} satisfies
\[
M_t(P)=A_t\,\Gamma_t\,B^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma_t=\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\}.
\]
Here \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix in \cref{obj:def:reference-feature}, and \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix in \cref{obj:def:target-feature}.

915fa0e73665afc02567e122d2f594881a6f98cd.title: Path stratum membership
915fa0e73665afc02567e122d2f594881a6f98cd.body:
For real numbers \(g\) and \(h\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(0<g\).
\item \textbf{(Small gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Small path perturbation.)} The path perturbation satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) from \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum} with constants \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). The membership is in the model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class} with the boundedness, latent-arm positivity, and proxy-rank margins specified in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}; the gap window and distinct-effect requirements are those of \cref{obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}. In particular, the gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\), its smallest positive effect gap from \cref{obj:def:effect-gap} obeys
\[
\frac{g}{2}\le \delta(P_{g,h})\le 2g,
\]
indeed \(\delta(P_{g,h})=g\), and its two latent effects from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} are distinct.

5fe84b8742e36e0f46d6c053e806425b293012ce.title: Path local weight inclusion
5fe84b8742e36e0f46d6c053e806425b293012ce.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in\mathbb R\) be the local Kullback--Leibler radius constant of \cref{obj:def:local-kl-radius}, and let \(g,h\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Local radius.)} \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1\).
\item \textbf{(Gap window.)} As in \cref{obj:ass:gap-window}, \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Local KL calibration.)}
\[
16000\,g^2h^2\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
For the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family}, \(P_{g,h}\) belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) of \cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment} with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).  Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\) lies in the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}, and it satisfies the local labeled-weight neighborhood condition of \cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood} through the observed-data marginal bound
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\middle\|(P_{g,0})_O\right)\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n},
\qquad
P_{g,0}=P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}.
\]

a53a525df972168c7016c484102ac1be53a2d9c9.title: Proxy coordinate envelopes
a53a525df972168c7016c484102ac1be53a2d9c9.body:
Let \(P\), a full-data law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), be indexed by latent cardinality \(k\), target-proxy dimension \(d_x\), reference-proxy dimension \(d_z\), and uniform boundedness radius \(L\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\) and \(k\le d_x\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope and anchor conditions.)} The bounded target-proxy, bounded proxy-product, bounded outcome--proxy-product, and anchor conditions in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:anchor} hold.
\end{itemize}
Then, \(P\)-almost surely,
\[
|X_i|\le L\quad\text{for every }1\le i\le d_x,
\qquad
|Z_j|\le L\quad\text{for every }1\le j\le d_z,
\qquad
|Y Z_j|\le L\quad\text{for every }1\le j\le d_z.
\]

375b4b76b8e79d41c56e003e130aa9013a903462.title: Separated recovery regime
375b4b76b8e79d41c56e003e130aa9013a903462.body:
A full-data law \(P\) lies in the separated recovery regime when it satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} The published VMW structural model conditions.
\item \textbf{(Anchor normalization.)} \(X_1=1\) almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Finite regularity.)} The published VMW finite-regularity condition.
\item \textbf{(Spectral separation.)} \(\tau_u\ne\tau_v\) whenever \(u\ne v\).
\end{itemize}
In this regime, the separated-recovery estimator analyzed by \citet[Theorem~7.2]{VirkMazaheriWu2026} is evaluated under its stated sample-size and radius conditions and returns simultaneous high-probability bounds for the treatment effects, the anchor-normalized feature matrix, and the simplex-projected mixture weights.

a915b27488421775a282e1442a56a47741102696.title: Ordered masses invariant
a915b27488421775a282e1442a56a47741102696.body:
Let \(k\in\mathbb N\) and \(L_\tau\in\mathbb R\).  Let \(\xi\) and \(\xi'\) be valid represented atomic laws with \(k\) labelled slots as in \cref{obj:def:atomic-law-class}.  For a labelled representative \(\zeta\), write \(w^{\uparrow}(\zeta)\in\mathbb R^k\) for the ordered-mass vector produced by the rule in \cref{obj:def:ordered-mass-target}, including its barycentric fallback for representatives outside the strict-positive, injective-location case.  If the two representatives induce the same aggregated probability law,
\[
\nu_\xi=\nu_{\xi'},
\]
then the ordered-mass vectors computed from the two labelled representatives coincide:
\[
w^{\uparrow}(\xi)=w^{\uparrow}(\xi').
\]

52eab854ae9dd0bd176bfd5f1c3a325c5a748f86.title: Total Borel repair
52eab854ae9dd0bd176bfd5f1c3a325c5a748f86.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0,\alpha,C_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Model radii.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(1\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Confidence parameters.)} The miscoverage level satisfies \(0<\alpha<1/2\), and the simultaneous-concentration constant satisfies \(1\le C_0\).
\item \textbf{(Empirical summary.)} The empirical summary map \(\widehat S_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}\) is measurable.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists repair data \(R\) of the form specified in \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\) such that the estimator \(\widehat\nu_n\) induced by \(R\) is Borel measurable.  Moreover, writing \(\mathcal K\) for the \(d_S\)-closure of the admissible summary image, if \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), then for every sample \(\omega\),
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=\delta_0.
\]
For every sample \(\omega\), the sharp summary-inversion confidence set \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(\omega)\) associated with \(R\), with singleton value \(\{\delta_0\}\) when \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\) and otherwise consisting of the laws \(\nu=\overline F(q)\) with \(q\in\mathcal K\) and \(d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega)))\le 2r_{n,\alpha}\), is nonempty.

e8c5d3e76375e9db95a58b5c149f3c056e6e85ed.title: Compact summary closure
e8c5d3e76375e9db95a58b5c149f3c056e6e85ed.body:
Let
\[
\mathscr S=\{S(P): P\in\mathcal M\},
\qquad
\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S},
\]
where \(\mathcal M\) is the class of full-data probability laws satisfying the uniformly conditioned model restrictions with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\). For summaries \(s,q\), write
\[
d_S(s,q)=
\|s.M_0-q.M_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|s.M_1-q.M_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|s.N_0-q.N_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|s.N_1-q.N_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\Bigl(\sum_i (s.m_X(i)-q.m_X(i))^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Boundedness radius.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy-rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists \(B\in\mathbb R\) such that every admissible summary satisfies
\[
d_S(s,0)\le B
\qquad\text{for all }s\in\mathscr S.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal K\) is compact, and
\[
\mathcal K\neq\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\neq\varnothing .
\]

da1f65dfd3bc6b5347d949f3b0fd2378ef06825e.title: Gap-free modulus extension
da1f65dfd3bc6b5347d949f3b0fd2378ef06825e.body:
Fix natural numbers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and real constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent dimension.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Bound and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), let \(\mathcal K\) be the \(d_S\)-closure of the admissible summary image \(\mathscr S=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\}\), and let
\[
d_S(s,q)
=
\|M_0(s)-M_0(q)\|+\|M_1(s)-M_1(q)\|
+\|N_0(s)-N_0(q)\|+\|N_1(s)-N_1(q)\|
+\Bigl(\sum_i (m_X(s)_i-m_X(q)_i)^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
There exists a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) such that, for every \(P,Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
W_1(\nu_P,\nu_Q)\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(S(P),S(Q)),
\]
where \(W_1\) is the minimum finite-transport cost between the represented at-most-\(k\) atomic laws on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\).

Moreover, there is a map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
such that \(\overline F\) is continuous and Borel measurable,
\[
W_1(\overline F(q),\overline F(q'))
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q')
\qquad\text{for all }q,q'\in\mathcal K,
\]
and
\[
\overline F(S(Q))=\nu_Q
\qquad\text{for every }Q\in\mathcal M.
\]
This extension is unique among continuous maps \(G:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) that satisfy the same \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\)-Lipschitz bound and agree with \(Q\mapsto\nu_Q\) on \(\mathscr S\): every such \(G\) obeys \(G(q)=\overline F(q)\) for all \(q\in\mathcal K\).

578d249d73dd60ff01cd9f5c5bac7618ad797028.title: Collision-uniform root-n rate
578d249d73dd60ff01cd9f5c5bac7618ad797028.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform bounds.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) taking values in \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), with
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0,
\]
and a nearest-summary repair estimator \(\widehat\nu_n=\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\) from \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\), such that \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the first lexicographic minimizer over a finite exhaustive structured lattice of well-formed candidates \(\vartheta\) for the criterion
\[
J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n),
\]
with tie-breaking by the lattice order and output \(\lambda_\vartheta\).  Both estimators are Borel sample maps.  For every \(\eta\) satisfying \(0<\eta<1/2\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\), and \(Q_P^{(n)}\)-sample,
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
\max\!\left\{
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P),
W_1(\widehat\nu_n,\nu_P)
\right\}
>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}\le \eta .
\]
Moreover, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\{N_{t,n}=0\}\le (1-k\pi_0)^n .
\]

0c1c6ed9912a050d87baadb458c378c822589891.title: Honest root-\(n\) confidence
0c1c6ed9912a050d87baadb458c378c822589891.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\) such that
\[
2\le k,\qquad k\le d_x,\qquad k\le d_z,\qquad
0<\pi_0\le {1\over 2k},\qquad 0<\sigma_0\le 1 .
\]
There exists a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every boundedness radius \(L\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) for which the prescribed structured-lattice constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is positive and the following holds.  For every sample size \(n\ge 1\), there exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structured lattice estimator.)} a measurable estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) taking values in \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), generated by a finite exhaustive list of well-formed structured-lattice candidates, ordered lexicographically, with \(\widehat\lambda_n\) equal to the effect law of the first lexicographic minimizer of the structured-lattice criterion;
\item \textbf{(Summary repair data.)} a continuous extension \(\overline F\) on the summary closure \(\mathcal K\), a measurable nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\) with its empty-closure fallback, and the associated measurable repaired summary-to-law map.
\end{itemize}
For every miscoverage level \(\alpha\) satisfying
\[
0<\alpha< {1\over 2},
\]
let \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\), \(R_{n,\alpha}\), and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) be the confidence-set objects of \(\cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set}\) formed from this repair data and this structured-lattice estimator, with \(m_\star=\pi_0\) and center \(\widehat\lambda_n\).  Then, on every sample, both \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) are nonempty, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) has the finite constrained transport representation
\[
\nu\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\nu)\ \text{and there exists a transport plan }\gamma\text{ from }\nu\text{ to }\widehat\lambda_n
\text{ with cost at most }R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
Moreover, for every full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\nu_P\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
Finally, on every sample,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le
4C_{\mathrm{mod}}\, r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le
2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

7f743545f2627cf28e559dafa95ef41e3042e358.title: Ordered-weight upper bound
7f743545f2627cf28e559dafa95ef41e3042e358.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent size.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), one can choose the simplex-valued measurable ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:labeled-weight-estimator}\) so that, for every gap scale \(g\) satisfying \(0<g\le1/4\) and every full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M(g)\),
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\left\|\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1\right]
\le
C\min\left\{1,\left(\sqrt n\,g\right)^{-1}\right\}.
\]

9b8561fe7ae57d62153b074e996b867938447ee8.title: Compact loss selector
9b8561fe7ae57d62153b074e996b867938447ee8.body:
For every \(d\in\mathbb N\), every set \(\mathcal K\subseteq \mathbb R^d\), and every loss \(d_S:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty feasible set.)} \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty.
\item \textbf{(Compact feasible set.)} \(\mathcal K\) is compact.
\item \textbf{(Continuous loss.)} The map \((s,q)\mapsto d_S(s,q)\) is continuous.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a Borel measurable map \(\Pi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) such that, for every \(s\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K
\quad\text{and}\quad
d_S(s,\Pi(s))\le d_S(s,q)\ \text{for every }q\in\mathcal K .
\]

701111dcb58fc1f9da6006ac2ce518da72d36c6f.title: Same-class quotient minimax
701111dcb58fc1f9da6006ac2ce518da72d36c6f.body:
For the specialization \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), let \(\mathcal M\) be the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).  The derived effect-support radius is
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0=80\sqrt 2 .
\]
There exist real constants \(c\) and \(C\) such that
\[
0<c<C
\]
and, for every sample size \(n\ge 1\), the following two statements hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Lower bound.)} For every measurable estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) mapping an \(n\)-sample of observed records to a represented atomic law modulo the radius \(L_\tau\), there exists a full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M\) such that
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
  W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right].
\]
\item \textbf{(Upper bound.)} There exists a measurable estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) mapping an \(n\)-sample of observed records to a represented atomic law modulo the radius \(L_\tau\) such that, for every full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
  W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{\sqrt n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Equivalently, on this same specialized class,
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
  W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{\sqrt n}
\]
for every \(n\ge 1\), where the infimum ranges over measurable estimators with output radius \(L_\tau\).

7ed48aa3938a032d0ac94af0d7dbc4997a225338.title: Published converse transfer
7ed48aa3938a032d0ac94af0d7dbc4997a225338.body:
Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).  There exist constants \(a,c\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<a\le \frac18,
\qquad
0<c .
\]
For every \(n\ge 1\), the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Quotient witness pair.)} The two laws \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\) belong to the published VMW model and satisfy VMW Assumption 4, while \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) lies outside the published separated recovery regime.
\item \textbf{(Quotient lower bound.)} For every class \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) of full-data probability laws such that every \(P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu\) belongs to the published VMW model and satisfies VMW Assumption 4, if \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) contains laws equal to \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\), then every estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) of the quotient effect law with support radius \(4\cdot 2\sqrt2/(1/10)\) has worst-case risk at least \(c/\sqrt n\):
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\ge \frac{c}{\sqrt n}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Separated labeled path.)} For every \(g\) in the gap-scale domain, define
\[
h(n,g):=\operatorname{calibratedDisplacement}(a,n,g).
\]
Then \(h(n,g)\) is in the tangent-amplitude domain, and the endpoint laws \(P_{g,0}\) and \(P_{g,h(n,g)}\) both belong to the published VMW model, satisfy VMW Assumption 4, and have spectrally separated latent effects.
\item \textbf{(Labeled-weight lower bound.)} For every \(g\) in the gap-scale domain and every class \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) of full-data probability laws such that every \(P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) belongs to the published VMW model and satisfies VMW Assumption 4, if \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) contains laws equal to \(P_{g,0}\) and \(P_{g,h(n,g)}\), then every estimator \(\widetilde p_n\) of the ordered latent weights satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^p}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\left\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1
\right]
\ge
c\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

3bb87f9ba58b44c9b2b43986ac3e4a8cfd9425a8.title: Cluster-adaptive report validity
3bb87f9ba58b44c9b2b43986ac3e4a8cfd9425a8.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(\pi_0\in\mathbb R\), and \(\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Latent mass.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), if
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
and
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
      +\frac{2\sqrt{k}L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}Lc_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}Lc_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
\end{gathered}
\]
then the prescribed structured-lattice stability constant
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\,
(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\}
\]
is positive.  For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a measurable structured-lattice estimator
\(\widehat\lambda_n\) and repair data consisting of a continuous extension on \(\mathcal K\) and a Borel nearest-summary selector, such that \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is obtained from an exhaustive lexicographically ordered finite list of well-formed structured-lattice candidates by choosing the first minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\).

For every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the estimator has atom floor \(\pi_0\).  Moreover, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) and every sample,
\[
W_1\!\left(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
\left\{
d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n,S(P)\right)+\frac{1}{\sqrt n}
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
r_{n,\alpha}
=
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}},
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}
=
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\right),
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\pi_0},
\]
with \(\widehat S_n\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}\), and set
\[
E_P=\left\{\omega:
d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P)\right)\le r_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge 1-\alpha.
\]
For every sample \(\omega\in E_P\), the cluster report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) centered at \(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)\) satisfies the following properties for the representative atomic law \(\nu_P\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Partition.)} Each support point \(x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\) belongs to a unique empirical component \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) with \(x\in K_C(P)\).
\item \textbf{(Association.)} For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), the set \(K_C(P)\) is nonempty and is contained in \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\).
