\item \textbf{(Support interval.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(x\in K_C(P)\), then \(x\) lies in the reported support interval for \(C\).
\item \textbf{(Mass interval.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), then the reported mass interval \(I_C\) contains \(\nu_P(K_C(P))\).
\item \textbf{(Singleton width.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\operatorname{card}(K_C(P))=1\), then the reported support interval for \(C\) has length at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\), and
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\delta(P)}\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(External-gap width.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\), then \(\operatorname{length}(I_C)=0\).  For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\),
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\Delta_C(P)}\right\},
\]
with the displayed right side read as zero when \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\).
\item \textbf{(Constrained representation.)} The computable class
\(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) has the finite constrained-program representation
\[
\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and}\ 
\exists\gamma\ \text{with transport cost at most } R_{n,\alpha}
\text{ from }\xi\text{ to }\widehat\lambda_n(\omega).
\]
\end{itemize}

c4d00e0cae34771f084c001859de513d102aa1c4.title: Uniform summary concentration
c4d00e0cae34771f084c001859de513d102aa1c4.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Positivity calibration.)} \(0<\pi_0\) and
\[
\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Rank-margin calibration.)} \(0<\sigma_0\) and \(\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\in\mathbb R\) with \(1\le C_0\) such that the following holds. For every \(L\in\mathbb R\) and \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(1\le L\) and \(1\le n\), every full-data probability law \(P\) on records \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\in \{1,\ldots,k\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_z}\times\mathbb R^3\) in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) with radius \(L\), latent-arm positivity margin \(\pi_0\), and proxy-rank singular-value margin \(\sigma_0\), and every tail probability \(\eta\) satisfying \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))>
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le \eta .
\]
Moreover, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\{N_{t,n}=0\}
=
\left(1-P_O\{O:T=t\}\right)^n
\le
(1-k\pi_0)^n .
\]

fd59b912559b36a1a7ac78a1f74d30f3d66bf8fd.title: Arm mass lower bound
fd59b912559b36a1a7ac78a1f74d30f3d66bf8fd.body:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law in the setting of \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Suppose \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity} with margin \(\pi_0\). Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
k\pi_0 \le P(T=t).
\]

10ffacd5b0ee5089ca9b3f8c95c4a308bd98362f.title: Polynomial finite-net estimator
10ffacd5b0ee5089ca9b3f8c95c4a308bd98362f.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and real constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\). Suppose
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Bounds and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there are constants \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) and \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 1\), there is a class-dependent finite library \(A=(A_i)_i\) of representative summaries as in \(\cref{obj:def:finite-net-law-estimator}\) with the following properties. For every uniform provider of the fixed-parameter exact-real primitives on the admissible core parameter domain, the finite-net estimator \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) is Borel measurable, and
\[
|A|\le C n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}.
\]
For every observed sample \(\omega=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), the operation count of the same exact-real execution that returns \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}(\omega)\) is at most
\[
C\{n+n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}\}.
\]
Its trace is exactly the empirical-summary trace, followed by the exhaustive finite-library search trace, and followed by the selected spectral-run trace when a representative is selected; if no representative is selected, the final spectral-run trace is empty.

If the program selects index \(i\) on sample \(\omega\), then \(S_i\) is a nearest library summary to the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}\):
\[
d_S(S_i,\widehat S_n(\omega))\le d_S(S_j,\widehat S_n(\omega))
\qquad\text{for every }j.
\]
Among all tied nearest summaries, \(i\) has minimal lexicographic rank:
\[
d_S(S_i,\widehat S_n(\omega))=d_S(S_j,\widehat S_n(\omega))
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)\le \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(j).
\]
For the exact spectral run at \(S_i\), the estimator equals the run's returned effect law. For each treatment value \(t\), the observed proxy moment at \(S_i\), multiplied by the run's basis matrix, defines an injective Euclidean linear map. The stacked proxy moment at \(S_i\) satisfies the exact threshold characterization
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(S_i),M_1(S_i)))
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j<k,
\]
for every singular-value index \(j\). Every eigenvalue of the compressed operator formed at \(S_i\) with the run's basis and spans appears among the eigenvalues returned by that run.

For every stored representative \(S_i\) and every rectangular perturbation \(H\in\mathbb R^{2d_z\times d_x}\),
\[
\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}
\]
implies that singular-value thresholding at \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) recovers exactly the \(k\)-dimensional matrix signal space for
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0(S_i),M_1(S_i))+H.
\]
For every index \(i\), there is a model law \(Q\in\mathcal M\) from \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) whose observable summary is \(S_i\), and the exact spectral run at \(S_i\) returns the quotient law \(\nu_Q\). Each returned representative effect law is a valid atomic law.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) satisfies
\[
W_1\!\left(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}(\omega),\nu_P\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{mod}}\left\{2d_S(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}.
\]
Finally, for every tail level \(\eta\) with \(0<\eta<1/2\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left(
W_1\!\left(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}},\nu_P\right)
>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right)
\le \eta .
\]

94db1ca48ddf30150b7387970a536cdac2f0fe63.title: Observed proxy moment factorization
94db1ca48ddf30150b7387970a536cdac2f0fe63.body:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Target dimension.)} \(k\le d_x\).
\item \textbf{(Boundedness radius.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} \(\pi_0>0\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise proxy moment \(M_t(P)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}\) factors as
\[
M_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_t B^\top,
\]
where \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix of \(\cref{obj:def:reference-feature}\), \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix of \(\cref{obj:def:target-feature}\), and
\[
\Gamma_t
=
\operatorname{diag}\left\{
\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k
\right\}.
\]

01d911ae264ef17290d163aaec379220b4295235.title: Coordinate envelope bounds
01d911ae264ef17290d163aaec379220b4295235.body:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be a full-data probability law as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Target-proxy dimension.)} \(k\le d_x\).
\end{itemize}
Then the model envelope \(L\) bounds the target proxy, the reference proxy, and the outcome--reference-proxy products \(P\)-almost surely:
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|X_i|\le L\text{ for every }1\le i\le d_x\,\}=1,
\]
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|Z_j|\le L\text{ for every }1\le j\le d_z\,\}=1,
\]
and
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|Y Z_j|\le L\text{ for every }1\le j\le d_z\,\}=1.
\]

0aa06b921aaeda939ffe89a303c1a53d62f68555.title: Latent mean envelope
0aa06b921aaeda939ffe89a303c1a53d62f68555.body:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be a full-data law in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class of \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Model constants.)} \(1\le L\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and every treatment state \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the latent conditional potential-outcome mean \(\mu_{tu}\) of \cref{obj:def:latent-mean} satisfies
\[
|\mu_{tu}|\le \frac{L_\tau}{2},
\]
where \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) is the derived effect-support radius from \cref{obj:def:effect-radius}.

9a8e107c926500e07f2839772ac061f244396336.title: Latent effect envelope
9a8e107c926500e07f2839772ac061f244396336.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), let \(P\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and fix a latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).
\end{itemize}
Then the latent-class treatment effect \(\tau_u\) in \(\cref{obj:def:latent-effect}\) satisfies the envelope
\[
|\tau_u|\le L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
where \(L_\tau\) is the derived effect-support radius in \(\cref{obj:def:effect-radius}\).

4a80f8eeff855c3a2c3210c47737bad10d1324f4.title: Witness latent masses
4a80f8eeff855c3a2c3210c47737bad10d1324f4.body:
For every \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\) with \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\), let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) be the two-class witness law of \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\).  For each latent class \(u\in\{0,1\}\), the latent-class mass \(p_u\) from \(\cref{obj:def:latent-mass}\) satisfies
\[
p_u(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})
=
\begin{cases}
2/5, & u=0,\\
3/5, & u=1.
\end{cases}
\]

17d201fb20d1406fae64a05e58fcc5f0a8364c7c.title: Witness latent effects
17d201fb20d1406fae64a05e58fcc5f0a8364c7c.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\) with \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\) and every latent class \(u\in\{1,2\}\), the latent-class treatment effect \(\tau_u\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} under the two-class Bernoulli witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness} is
\[
\tau_u(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})
=
\begin{cases}
\frac14-\varepsilon, & u=1,\\
\frac14+\varepsilon, & u=2.
\end{cases}
\]

039d3e7b3aca9a926a6bc6f5ba33e4ea41de94e0.title: Observed arm mass
039d3e7b3aca9a926a6bc6f5ba33e4ea41de94e0.body:
For any collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\) and any treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Lower bound.)} \(0\le \varepsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Upper bound.)} \(\varepsilon\le 1/8\).
\end{itemize}
For the two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\), its observed-data marginal from \(\cref{obj:def:observed-margin}\) satisfies
\[
(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O(T=t)
=
\begin{cases}
12/25, & t=0,\\
13/25, & t=1.
\end{cases}
\]

4546791703dda7d14b3793e1f8944bf7317913ea.title: Witness feature determinant
4546791703dda7d14b3793e1f8944bf7317913ea.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\), let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) be the two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law from \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\), and let \(B\) be its target-proxy feature matrix from \(\cref{obj:def:target-feature}\). Then
\[
B_{00}B_{11}-B_{01}B_{10}=\frac35 .
\]

debe4e82080750157c356eed4a091db9bed6a5be.title: Polynomial lattice estimator
debe4e82080750157c356eed4a091db9bed6a5be.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Radius and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Put \(L_\tau:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) and \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\).  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_V&:=4\sqrt{d_xk},
&
K_D&:=\frac{4\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},
&
A_D&:=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\\
K_f&:=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},
&
c_D&:=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m&:=2\sqrt{k}Lc_V+k+kL,
&
c_b&:=k+2\sqrt{k}Lc_V,
&
c_{\mathrm{grid}}&:=c_D+c_m+c_b,\\
B_{\mathrm{lat}}&:=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
&
C_{\mathrm{lat}}&:=\max\!\left\{\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}>0\), and there is a finite constant
\(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), there is a total Borel summary rule whose empirical-summary estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the lexicographically first minimizer over the prescribed structured lattice with effect radius \(L_\tau\), atom floor \(\pi_0\), and threshold \(s_0/2\).  For every sample, every distinct represented atom of \(\widehat\lambda_n\) has aggregate mass at least \(\pi_0\).

For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), the stacked observable proxy moment at \(S(P)\), and at every summary \(s\) with
\[
d_S(s,S(P))<\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2},
\]
has exactly its first \(k\) singular values at least \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) and all remaining singular values below \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).  The deterministic loss bound
\[
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega),\nu_P)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left\{
d_S(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P))+\frac{1}{\sqrt n}
\right\}
\]
holds for every sample \(\omega\), where \(\widehat S_n\) is the empirical summary in \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}\).  The candidate list and exhaustive-search operation count satisfy
\[
|\mathcal A_n|
\le C\, n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{Work}_n
\le
C\left(n+n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\right).
\]
Finally, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\), and the observed product experiment \(Q_P^{(n)}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}
\le \eta .
\]

2f93d94244c2bccddb0469324b127fcd758ba2a8.title: Witness reference-feature determinant
2f93d94244c2bccddb0469324b127fcd758ba2a8.body:
For the two-class Bernoulli witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and the reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\) in \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness,obj:def:reference-feature}\), suppose
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Perturbation range.)} The collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\).
\item \textbf{(Arm.)} The treatment arm \(t\) is binary, \(t\in\{0,1\}\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\det(A_t)=\frac25 .
\]

087496821b201dbb8505fb50998ee180faf3430f.title: Path proxy-rank margin

6d1d0071d54e912d0e81509f89a4fe69807a260a.title: Path model membership
6d1d0071d54e912d0e81509f89a4fe69807a260a.body:
Let \(g,h\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gap range.)} \(0\le g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the uniformly conditioned model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class} with
\[
k=d_x=d_z=2,\qquad L=2,\qquad \pi_0=1/10,\qquad \sigma_0=1/10 .
\]
Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\) satisfies the core numerical domain for \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), together with \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:latent-ignorability,obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}, using latent-arm positivity margin \(1/10\) and proxy-rank margin \(1/10\).

64a26cc3c795f636982b6371720efa29a0e8efa8.title: Path stratum membership
64a26cc3c795f636982b6371720efa29a0e8efa8.body:
For real numbers \(g\) and \(h\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} The path displacement satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Model constants.)} The model-class and gap-stratum constants in \cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:def:gap-stratum} are \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}. In particular, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M\), the scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\), its smallest positive effect gap \(\delta(P_{g,h})\) from \cref{obj:def:effect-gap} obeys
\[
\frac{g}{2}\le \delta(P_{g,h})\le 2g,
\]
indeed \(\delta(P_{g,h})=g\), and the two latent effects of \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} are distinct.

de3bf1a9b98bf141f9d0f0a4a6f4908c09529b8f.title: Ordered masses are invariant
de3bf1a9b98bf141f9d0f0a4a6f4908c09529b8f.body:
Let \(\xi\) and \(\xi'\) be represented atomic laws with at most \(k\) slots on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:atomic-law-class,obj:def:effect-radius}\).  If they represent the same aggregated probability law, \(\nu_\xi=\nu_{\xi'}\), then their effect-ordered mass vectors from \(\cref{obj:def:ordered-mass-target}\) coincide:
\[
p^{\uparrow}(\xi)=p^{\uparrow}(\xi').
\]
Equivalently, \(p^{\uparrow}\) is a function of the represented probability law in \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\).

1ae4848c71a81bfab4d3b827446cf273619a23a1.title: Two-class witness validity
1ae4848c71a81bfab4d3b827446cf273619a23a1.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\) satisfying
\[
0\le \varepsilon \le \frac18,
\]
the explicit two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\) with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\). Moreover,
\[
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=0)=0.48,\qquad
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=1)=0.52,
\]
\[
\det(B)=0.6,\qquad
\det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=0.4,
\]
\[
\det(M_0(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.06,\qquad
\det(M_1(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.4\cdot 0.6\cdot \frac{36}{169},
\]
and the quotient latent-effect law is
\[
\nu_{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}}
=
0.4\,\delta_{0.25-\varepsilon}
+
0.6\,\delta_{0.25+\varepsilon}.
\]
At \(\varepsilon=0\), the proxy feature and observable moment matrices above are nonsingular, the quotient latent-effect law is \(\delta_{0.25}\), and the two latent-class masses are distinct.

bf63e42b8eb5308a0cc4b217e11b523ebb4bf510.title: Observed VMW margins
bf63e42b8eb5308a0cc4b217e11b523ebb4bf510.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform model class.)} The full-data law \(P\) belongs to the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with parameters \(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).
\end{itemize}
Then the following quantitative observed-margin conclusions hold.  For each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0,
\]
and the observable armwise \(ZX^\top\) moment factors as
\[
M_t(P)
=
A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top .
\]
Moreover, for every orthonormal signal basis \(V\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) spanning the signal space of \(S(P)\),
\[
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)V\}
=
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)\},
\qquad
\pi_0\sigma_0^2\le \sigma_k\{M_t(P)V\}.
\]
The stacked observed proxy moment satisfies
\[
\pi_0\sigma_0^2
\le
\sigma_k\!\left(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(P),M_1(P))\right).
\]
The observable envelopes are
\[
\|M_t(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,
\qquad
\|N_t(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,
\qquad
\|m_X(P)\|_2\le L .
\]
Writing \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
|Y(t)|\le L_\tau/2
\quad\text{for \(P\)-almost every full-data record conditional on \(U=u\),}
\]
and
\[
|\mu_{tu}|\le L_\tau/2,
\qquad
|\tau_u|\le L_\tau .
\]
Finally, \(P\) belongs to the published VMW parameter class represented by the supplied scope handle.

f4e76d8809af1c8d29bedba32d0c2674fbe285ba.title: Path local weight membership
f4e76d8809af1c8d29bedba32d0c2674fbe285ba.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) and let \(c_{\mathrm{loc}},g,h\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Local radius.)} \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1\).
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Observed KL calibration.)}
\[
16000\,g^2h^2\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:path-law-family}\) belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) of \(\cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment}\) with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M(g)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}\), the local-radius constant satisfies the displayed bounds above, and its observed-data marginal obeys the neighborhood condition of \(\cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood}\):
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\,\Vert\,(P_{g,0})_O\right)
\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n},
\qquad
P_{g,0}=P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}.
\]

7173750e290006626b4ea81135e27c8826a0056f.title: Same-class labeled minimax
7173750e290006626b4ea81135e27c8826a0056f.body:
There exist real constants \(c\) and \(C\) such that \(0<c<C\) and, for every sample size \(n\ge 1\) and every gap scale \(g\) with \(0<g\le 1/4\), the gap stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}\) satisfies
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\left\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1
\right]
\le
C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
Here the infimum is over all measurable simplex-valued labeled weight estimators based on \(n\) observed records in the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), and \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\) is the effect-ordered latent-mass vector with the barycentric collision fallback.

bc3437e593ded7b5aa04eba4cf5b00402a494694.title: Matching local lower bounds
bc3437e593ded7b5aa04eba4cf5b00402a494694.body:
Fix \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in(0,1)\). There exist constants \(a,c,C\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<a\le \frac18,\qquad c>0,\qquad C>0,
\]
and, for every integer \(n\ge 1\), the following statements hold for the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Quotient-law risk.)} For every measurable quotient-law estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) with support radius \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), there is a law \(P\) in the local quotient-law experiment \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\) of \(\cref{obj:def:local-quotient-experiment}\) such that
\[
P=P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}
\quad\text{or}\quad
P=P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}},
\]
with \(P_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{wit}}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}\), and
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)\right].
\]
\item \textbf{(Ordered-weight risk.)} For every \(g\in(0,1/4]\) and every measurable ordered-weight estimator \(\widetilde p_n\) taking values in the simplex, there is a law \(P\) in the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment}\) such that
\[
P=P_{g,0}
\quad\text{or}\quad
P=P_{g,h(n,g)},
\qquad
h(n,g)=a\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\},
\]
with \(P_{g,h}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:path-law-family}\), and
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\|_1\right].
\]
\item \textbf{(Quotient-law certificate.)} The two witness laws \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) belong to the corresponding local quotient-law experiments, and their observed-data marginals and quotient laws satisfy
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\Vert (P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\right)
\le
\frac{C}{n},
\qquad
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
W_1\!\left(\nu_{P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}},\nu_{P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}}\right).
\]
\item \textbf{(Labeled-path certificate.)} For every \(g\in(0,1/4]\), with
\[
h=h(n,g)=a\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\},
\]
the displacement \(h\) lies in the tangent-amplitude domain, the laws \(P_{g,h}\) and \(P_{g,0}\) both belong to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\), and
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\Vert (P_{g,0})_O\right)
\le
C g^2h^2,
\qquad
\sum_i\left|p_i^{\uparrow}(P_{g,h})-p_i^{\uparrow}(P_{g,0})\right|
=
2|h|.
\]
\end{itemize}

cb5739f953e1a0395eb4c24c81d59bfc13a9f623.title: Empirical summary primitives \(\widehat S_n\)
cb5739f953e1a0395eb4c24c81d59bfc13a9f623.body:
For an observed sample of size \(n\), let \(N_{t,n}\) be the number of observations in arm \(t\). Define the empirical armwise proxy moment \(\widehat M_{t,n}\) and outcome-proxy moment \(\widehat N_{t,n}\) using the total empty-arm convention:
\[
\widehat M_{t,n}
=
\frac{1}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}}
\sum_{i:T_i=t} Z_iX_i^\top,
\qquad
\widehat N_{t,n}
=
\frac{1}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}}
\sum_{i:T_i=t} Y_iZ_iX_i^\top .
\]
Let the empirical target-proxy mean be
\[
\widehat m_{X,n}
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i .
\]
The empirical five-block observable summary is
\[
\widehat S_n
=
\bigl(
\widehat M_{0,n},
\widehat M_{1,n},
\widehat N_{0,n},
\widehat N_{1,n},
\widehat m_{X,n}
\bigr).
\]

bc4c86365d20bbca14a2ae798633dc4a8c20867c.title: First basis vector \(e_1\)
bc4c86365d20bbca14a2ae798633dc4a8c20867c.body: Let \(e_1\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\) be the first canonical basis vector.

50a8c92697298a9ebd06983732c79ff208c77434.title: Local Kullback--Leibler radius \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\)
50a8c92697298a9ebd06983732c79ff208c77434.body:
Fix a local Kullback--Leibler radius constant \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) satisfying
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1.
\]

aab855cbd9443ce32e7996e509d7bf4c725bdba6.title: Observed-record space \(O_{d_x,d_z}\)
aab855cbd9443ce32e7996e509d7bf4c725bdba6.body:
Write \(O_{d_x,d_z}\) for the observed-record space of quadruples
\[
O=(T,X,Z,Y),
\]
where \(T\in\{0,1\}\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d_z}\), and \(Y\in\mathbb R\).

d8ab6d88360fdae0cf7fd55b9b4ac825fec387fa.title: Wasserstein distance \(W_1(\nu,\xi)\)
d8ab6d88360fdae0cf7fd55b9b4ac825fec387fa.body:
For represented atomic laws
\[
\nu=\sum_i p_i\delta_{x_i},
\qquad
\xi=\sum_j q_j\delta_{y_j},
\]
define \(W_1(\nu,\xi)\) by
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
=
\min_{\gamma_{ij}\ge 0}
\sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij}|x_i-y_j|,
\]
where the minimum is over all nonnegative couplings \((\gamma_{ij})_{i,j}\) whose marginals are the represented masses:
\[
\sum_j \gamma_{ij}=p_i
\quad\text{for every }i,
\qquad
\sum_i \gamma_{ij}=q_j
\quad\text{for every }j.
\]

704aad7562b001a55c2ee1c98c9cd1956a60a194.title: Observed-data marginal \(P_O\)
704aad7562b001a55c2ee1c98c9cd1956a60a194.body:
For a full-data probability law \(P\), let
\[
O=(T,X,Z,Y)
\]
be the observed record. The observed-data marginal of \(P\) is
\[
P_O:=P\circ O^{-1}.
\]

d9f4900895304aad8c62be45f1f39c229d4bc9be.title: Latent-class mass \(p_u\)
d9f4900895304aad8c62be45f1f39c229d4bc9be.body:
For each latent class \(u\), its latent-class mass is
\[
p_u:=P(U=u).
\]

152679b491d9f42ff90e7eff2944456039d1f8b6.title: Latent conditional mean \(\mu_{tu}\)
152679b491d9f42ff90e7eff2944456039d1f8b6.body:
For treatment arm \(t\) and latent class \(u\), the latent conditional potential-outcome mean is
\[
\mu_{tu}:=E_P\!\left[Y(t)\mid U=u\right].
\]

c46d41a4ddcc724af344542a70968064ed268dfc.title: Latent-class effect \(\tau_u\)
c46d41a4ddcc724af344542a70968064ed268dfc.body:
For each latent class \(u\), its latent-class treatment effect is
\[
\tau_u:=\mu_{1u}-\mu_{0u}.
\]

ec7b8f61e878295f14ef8f03a323ca912e1ba646.title: Reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\)
ec7b8f61e878295f14ef8f03a323ca912e1ba646.body:
For treatment arm \(t\), the reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\in\mathbb R^{d_z\times k}\) is defined entrywise by
\[
A_t(i,u):=E_P\!\left[Z_i\mid U=u,T=t\right].
\]

493badcef001a79f94be999a884d24fa4401267d.title: Target-proxy feature matrix \(B\)
493badcef001a79f94be999a884d24fa4401267d.body:
The target-proxy feature matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) is defined entrywise by
\[
B(i,u):=E_P\!\left[X_i\mid U=u\right].
\]

d3c5ea02ddca9cbd31368905ab5b4fd32854298b.title: Effect-support radius \(L_\tau\)
d3c5ea02ddca9cbd31368905ab5b4fd32854298b.body:
The derived effect-support radius is
\[
L_\tau := \frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]

31d4164f50cc5113501a60c9bf8332bd69beaf4b.title: Effect gap \(\delta(P)\)
31d4164f50cc5113501a60c9bf8332bd69beaf4b.body:
The effect gap of \(P\) is
\[
\delta(P)
:=
\min\bigl\{|\tau_u-\tau_v|:\ p_u>0,\ p_v>0,\ \tau_u\ne\tau_v\bigr\},
\]
with the convention \(\delta(P)=+\infty\) when the quotient law has a single distinct support point.

b609c24598f7fa6f3a61732ba3e25a5d55c98ef5.title: Observable population moments \(M_t(P)\), \(N_t(P)\), and \(m_X(P)\)
b609c24598f7fa6f3a61732ba3e25a5d55c98ef5.body:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise population moments and target-proxy population mean are
\[
M_t(P) := E_P[ZX^\top\mid T=t],
\qquad
N_t(P) := E_P[YZX^\top\mid T=t],
\qquad
m_X(P) := E_P[X].
\]

ce5b52d57d5edf3017b6c26775a6d7d6bffed737.title: Summary radius \(r_{n,\alpha}\)
ce5b52d57d5edf3017b6c26775a6d7d6bffed737.body:
For \(n\ge 1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the simultaneous concentration radius is
\[
r_{n,\alpha}
:=
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]

004797928c25a2e6a7f5d269eda0a0ba85071460.title: Atomic law classes \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) and \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\)
004797928c25a2e6a7f5d269eda0a0ba85071460.body: The class \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), also written \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), consists of probability laws on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\) with at most \(k\) distinct atoms. Repeated slots and zero-weight slots represent the same law. For a represented atomic law \(\xi\), \(\nu_\xi\) denotes the probability law obtained by aggregating all slots at the same atom location.

a5347bed95fa3eba62999f129ccfd863adc1abef.title: Ordered mass target \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\)
a5347bed95fa3eba62999f129ccfd863adc1abef.body:
When the \(k\) latent effects are distinct, \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\) is the vector of latent-class masses ordered by increasing effect. Otherwise,
\[
p^{\uparrow}(P) := (1/k,\ldots,1/k).
\]

f66a61b8b4e66aa788614c63d7c36c9625d4e39a.title: Path law \(P_{g,h}\)
f66a61b8b4e66aa788614c63d7c36c9625d4e39a.body: For a gap \(g\) and displacement \(h\), \(P_{g,h}\) is the explicit two-class factorization-preserving path law obtained by perturbing the latent weights while preserving the stated proxy factorizations.

4d331a96de979dcab41e2c22bb186f611ddcaba8.title: Atom floor \(\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m,\xi)\)
4d331a96de979dcab41e2c22bb186f611ddcaba8.body: For a probability law \(\xi\), \(\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m,\xi)\) is the condition that every distinct support atom of \(\xi\) has aggregate mass at least \(m\).

6d18f06ec3fa619567070103661fc55b86103f65.title: Structured-lattice constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\)
6d18f06ec3fa619567070103661fc55b86103f65.body:
The structured-lattice constant is
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
C_{\mathrm{lat}}(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0),
\]
the explicit prescribed constant given by the maximum of the threshold-stability constants and the grid-approximation constants displayed in the structured-lattice construction.

ee54c3e0765c351faac03beccd6b798e06046a93.title: Structured-lattice program \(\widehat\lambda_n\)
ee54c3e0765c351faac03beccd6b798e06046a93.body:
The inputs are the sample size \(n\), the empirical five-block summary \(s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\), and the fixed constants \(k,d_x,L_\tau,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the lattice scale, mesh width, and singular-value threshold by
\[
H_n
:=
\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,
\qquad
q_n:=H_n^{-1},
\qquad
s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2.
\]

\item For matrices \(M_0,M_1\), define vertical stacking by
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0,M_1):=[M_0^\top,M_1^\top]^\top.
\]

\item Define the thresholded empirical compressed operator at summary \(s\) by
\[
\widehat D_n(s)
:=
M_1^\dagger{}_{\ge s_0/2}N_1
-
M_0^\dagger{}_{\ge s_0/2}N_0.
\]

\item Let \(\mathcal V_n\) be the prescribed \(q_n\)-grid of polar factors, \(\mathcal R_n\) the \(q_n\)-grid of invertible conditioning matrices with singular value at least \(\sigma_0/2\), \(\mathcal P_n\) the \(H_n^{-1}\)-simplex grid with every coordinate at least \(\pi_0\), and \(\mathcal T_n\) the clipped \(q_n\)-effect grid in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]^k\). Define the candidate set by
\[
\mathcal A_n
:=
\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n,
\]
ordered lexicographically.

\item For each \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal A_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta
:=
VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\qquad
m_\vartheta
:=
VR^\top p,
\qquad
b_\vartheta
:=
RV^\top e_1,
\]
and
\[
\lambda_\vartheta
:=
\sum_u p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.
\]

\item Define the criterion
\[
J_n(\vartheta;s)
:=
\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n(s)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert m_\vartheta-m_X\rVert_2
+
\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf1_k\rVert_2.
\]

\item Let \(\widehat\vartheta_n(s)\) be the first lexicographic minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;s)\) over \(\mathcal A_n\). The structured-lattice quotient-law estimator is
\[
\widehat\lambda_n
:=
\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n(\widehat S_n)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

8038504430bd7dc4fe47f78b9d2afdd1b0394b75.title: Finite-net program \(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\)
8038504430bd7dc4fe47f78b9d2afdd1b0394b75.body:
The inputs are a stored representative library \(A=(A_i)_i\) and an observed sample \(\omega\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each representative \(A_i\), let \(S_i=(M_{0,i},M_{1,i},N_{0,i},N_{1,i},m_{X,i})\) be its stored five-block summary, and let
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)
\]
be its position in the fixed lexicographic library order.

\item Define the spectral law attached to representative \(A_i\) by
\[
\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_i),
\]
the real atomic effect law returned by the thresholded exact-real spectral run for \(A_i\).

\item For the empirical five-block summary
\[
\widehat S_n(\omega)
=
(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n}),
\]
define the comparison criterion
\[
\Delta_i(\omega)
:=
\lVert M_{0,i}-\widehat M_{0,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert M_{1,i}-\widehat M_{1,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert N_{0,i}-\widehat N_{0,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert N_{1,i}-\widehat N_{1,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert m_{X,i}-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2.
\]

\item If the library is nonempty, define the selected representative index by
\[
\widehat i(\omega)
\in
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{i}
\bigl(\Delta_i(\omega),\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)\bigr),
\]
with the minimum taken in lexicographic order.

\item The finite-library spectral program returns the selected representative and its spectral law,
\[
\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)
:=
\bigl(A_{\widehat i(\omega)},\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_{\widehat i(\omega)})\bigr),
\]
when the library is nonempty, and returns the canonical zero law when the library is empty. Its returned effect-law component is
\[
\operatorname{law}(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)).
\]
\end{enumerate}

1ab7fc7572fa037619045c8ed9484b8e3b58cf4b.title: Published VMW scope handle
1ab7fc7572fa037619045c8ed9484b8e3b58cf4b.body:
The published VMW scope handle is the cited-publication interface for the proxy-model parameter class and recovery regime. For fixed latent cardinality \(k\), target-proxy dimension \(d_x\), reference-proxy dimension \(d_z\), and full-data law \(P\) on \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), it records three law-level predicates:
\[
\mathsf{Model}_{\mathrm{VMW}}(k,d_x,d_z,P),
\qquad
\mathsf{FiniteReg}_{\mathrm{VMW}}(k,d_x,d_z,P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Recover}_{\mathrm{VMW}}(k,d_x,d_z,P).
\]
These predicates are publication-level gates whose concrete interpretations enter through separate cited gates. The handle also includes the published estimator
\[
\widehat\Theta^{\mathrm{VMW}}_n:
(O_{d_x,d_z})^n
\to
\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\times\mathbb R^k,
\]
which maps an observed sample of size \(n\) from records \((T,X,Z,Y)\) to a triple consisting of treatment effects, an anchor-normalized target-proxy feature matrix, and real-valued weight coordinates.

6eb11d829e9d0f6834b4d52d6f058aa01c4d8735.title: Target-proxy separation
6eb11d829e9d0f6834b4d52d6f058aa01c4d8735.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
X\perp (Y,T)\mid U.
\]

5e33ac25bb7de27c840a7caf97ed0181509f406e.title: Observed-outcome consistency
5e33ac25bb7de27c840a7caf97ed0181509f406e.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
Y=Y(T)
\]
almost surely.

e1de5b6b9744c4e98ac107be3dad89f209072088.title: Latent ignorability
e1de5b6b9744c4e98ac107be3dad89f209072088.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Y(t)\perp T\mid U.
\]

a7f3c9beb0f8caf576dfb383d0d0942c5bd46fa0.title: Target-proxy anchor
a7f3c9beb0f8caf576dfb383d0d0942c5bd46fa0.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
X_1=1
\]
almost surely.

5e25915876790582ec291ede6f53570bb025ee81.title: Bounded target proxy
5e25915876790582ec291ede6f53570bb025ee81.body:
For the boundedness radius \(L\), under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
\lVert X\rVert_2\le L
\]
almost surely.

35be0e7571b5b64fb06cda1096e06709535e5787.title: Latent-arm positivity
35be0e7571b5b64fb06cda1096e06709535e5787.body:
The latent class and treatment arms satisfy
\[
\min_{1\le u\le k,\ t\in\{0,1\}} P(U=u,T=t)\ge \pi_0 .
\]

a7d531c37c09517875a818feb1a17aa5bdf6c92a.title: Proxy rank margin
a7d531c37c09517875a818feb1a17aa5bdf6c92a.body:
The reference- and target-proxy feature matrices satisfy
\[
\min\{\sigma_k(A_0),\sigma_k(A_1),\sigma_k(B)\}\ge \sigma_0 .
\]

13900507b83dcfc0a45332dc995e641e37e13e80.title: Effect gap window
13900507b83dcfc0a45332dc995e641e37e13e80.body:
The smallest positive effect gap satisfies
\[
g/2\le \delta(P)\le 2g .
\]

fa9a69b95d508c0d147e26f172a5371b86b456bc.title: Distinct latent effects
fa9a69b95d508c0d147e26f172a5371b86b456bc.body: The positive-mass latent effects \(\tau_u\) take exactly \(k\) distinct values.

c5ce1fcc157944ca154f5673bda2e005661cc2cd.title: Local quotient neighborhood
c5ce1fcc157944ca154f5673bda2e005661cc2cd.body:
The Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(P_O\), the observed-data marginal, to the observed margin of \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\), the two-class collision witness at perturbation zero, satisfies
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P_O\Vert (P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\bigr)\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]

d85171d1b57aa1b284d3a632c2884523a91b923b.title: Local weight neighborhood
d85171d1b57aa1b284d3a632c2884523a91b923b.body:
The Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(P_O\), the observed-data marginal, to the observed margin of the two-class witness at perturbation \(g/2\) satisfies
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P_O\Vert (P_{g/2}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\bigr)\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]

a86906e52775351f13c485dc71055a03210d2bf2.title: Model class \(\mathcal M\)

2e547866236e46b7605b6cc59cb1a1725b4aa2f8.title: Observable summary \(S(P)\) and metric \(d_S\)
2e547866236e46b7605b6cc59cb1a1725b4aa2f8.body:
The observable conditional moment summary is
\[
S(P):=\bigl(M_0(P),M_1(P),N_0(P),N_1(P),m_X(P)\bigr).
\]
For summaries \(s\) and \(s'\), the summary metric is
\[
d_S(s,s')
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{4}\lVert s_j-s'_j\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert s_5-s'_5\rVert_2.
\]

89a46ac946a0010086865ab8d914547444d82b8e.title: Empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\)
89a46ac946a0010086865ab8d914547444d82b8e.body:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let
\[
N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat M_{t,n}
:=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Z_iX_i^\top}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}},
\qquad
\widehat N_{t,n}
:=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Y_iZ_iX_i^\top}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}},
\]
and
\[
\widehat m_{X,n}:=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i.
\]
The empirical five-block observable summary is
\[
\widehat S_n
:=
\bigl(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},
\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n}\bigr).
\]
On the event \(\{N_{t,n}=0\}\), the corresponding armwise matrices \(\widehat M_{t,n}\) and \(\widehat N_{t,n}\) are the zero matrix, so \(\widehat S_n\) is a total Borel function of the sample.

7f0eeb830181b9ff6910dbd2577295d7c4033199.title: Compressed operator \(\Delta Q(P)\)
7f0eeb830181b9ff6910dbd2577295d7c4033199.body:
Choose any matrix \(V(P)\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) with orthonormal columns spanning the row space of the vertically stacked matrix \(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(P),M_1(P))\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_x}\). Define
\[
\Delta Q(P)
:=
\{M_1(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_1(P)V(P)
-
\{M_0(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_0(P)V(P),
\]
with spectral anchors
\[
a(P)^\top:=m_X(P)^\top V(P),
\qquad
c(P):=V(P)^\top e_1.
\]

5f360d9cc99ab3e23d3f3c7fe28b8587db21fd46.title: Quotient law \(\nu_P\)
5f360d9cc99ab3e23d3f3c7fe28b8587db21fd46.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), the quotient latent-effect law is
\[
\nu_P:=\sum_{u=1}^{k}p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.
\]
It is interpreted as a probability measure on the latent treatment effects, with coincident values of \(\tau_u\) carrying their aggregate mass.

d251cbf5a6f9edc974bfc1ec528613effcace089.title: Gap stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\)
d251cbf5a6f9edc974bfc1ec528613effcace089.body:
For the model class \(\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) and the effect-gap conditions in \(\cref{obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}\), the gap-local stratum is
\[
\mathcal M(g):=\{P\in\mathcal M: P \text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}\}.
\]

a817f48f3f9495a1486303edf209b1fec12c63ab.title: Sample experiment \(\mathcal E_n\)
a817f48f3f9495a1486303edf209b1fec12c63ab.body:
The observed i.i.d. proxy experiment at sample size \(n\) is
\[
\mathcal E_n:=\{Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}:P\in\mathcal M\}.
\]

a3bffffa2a5b584fe23f015de867ccf48a603e1c.title: Summary closure \(\mathcal K\)
a3bffffa2a5b584fe23f015de867ccf48a603e1c.body:
The admissible summary image, its closure, and the summary-to-quotient-law map are
\[
\mathscr S:=S(\mathcal M)=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\},\qquad
\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}^{\,d_S},
\]
and
\[
F:\mathscr S\to\mathcal P_k([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]),\qquad
F(S(P)):=\nu_P.
\]
The map \(F\) is well defined by Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu (2026, Theorem 5.4), which gives
\[
\int x^j\,d\nu_P(x)=a(P)^\top\Delta Q(P)^jc(P),
\qquad j=0,\ldots,2k-1.
\]
Under homogeneous effects, Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu (2026, Proposition 6.2) gives
\[
\Delta Q(P)=\tau_\star I_k,\qquad \nu_P=\delta_{\tau_\star}.
\]

e850bd3cbe7962e69f42e0ca96bc226794a9ebdf.title: Summary-space repair \(\widehat\nu_n\)
e850bd3cbe7962e69f42e0ca96bc226794a9ebdf.body:
The inputs are the closure \(\mathcal K\), the functional \(F\), the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), and the ambient summary space.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), let \(\overline F:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}])\) be the unique continuous extension of \(F\), and choose a Borel nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\) satisfying
\[
\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathcal K} d_S(q,s).
\]
\item If \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), set
\[
\Pi(s):=0.
\]
\item Define the repaired estimator by
\[
\widehat\nu_n:=
\begin{cases}
\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n)),&\mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\delta_0,&\mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Then \(\Pi\) and \(\widehat\nu_n\) are total Borel maps for every choice of the fixed class constants.
\end{enumerate}

6146cb2dd598f022a2849a6fc3a11b1af9b56e4b.title: Wasserstein confidence set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\)
6146cb2dd598f022a2849a6fc3a11b1af9b56e4b.body:
The inputs are fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\), constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0,\alpha,C_0,C_{\mathrm{lat}}\in\mathbb R\), an observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) with empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\) on \(\mathcal K\), and a prescribed structured-lattice estimator.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The fixed constants satisfy
\[
0<k,\qquad 0<n,\qquad 1\le L,\qquad
0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1},\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac12,\qquad
1\le C_0,\qquad 0<C_{\mathrm{lat}}.
\]
Define the effect-support radius and assume its nonnegativity:
\[
L_\tau:=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},\qquad 0\le L_\tau.
\]
\item Define the simultaneous concentration radius by
\[
r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]
\item The repair data satisfy: \(\overline F\) is continuous on \(\mathcal K\) and extends the summary-to-quotient-law map on model summaries; \(\Pi\) is measurable; if \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), then
\[
\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathcal K}d_S(q,s);
\]
if \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), then
\[
\Pi(s)=0;
\]
and the induced repaired estimator is measurable.
\item Let \(\widehat\lambda_n\) be the valid \(k\)-atomic law returned at \(\omega\) by the measurable prescribed structured-lattice estimator at support radius \(L_\tau\), generated by an exhaustive duplicate-free lexicographically ordered list of well-formed \(H_n,q_n\) lattice candidates and the first lexicographic minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\) with threshold
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}.
\]
\item Define the original summary-inversion confidence set by
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=
\begin{cases}
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\},&\mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\{\delta_0\},&\mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Define the atom-floor constant and computable radius by
\[
m_\star:=\pi_0,\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+(\sqrt n)^{-1}\right).
\]
\item Define the atom-floor subclass by
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi)\}.
\]
\item Output the computable Wasserstein confidence set
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi),\
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

f30878791c18eced7e6dd98e2af6704c19f6787b.title: Cluster report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\)
f30878791c18eced7e6dd98e2af6704c19f6787b.body:
The cluster report is computed from \(\widehat S_n\), \(S(P)\), \(r_{n,\alpha}\), \(R_{n,\alpha}\), \(m_\star\), \(\widehat\lambda_n\), and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the simultaneous concentration event and association radius by
\[
E_P:=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\},
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}:=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{m_\star}.
\]
\item Merge repeated atoms of \(\widehat\lambda_n\). Join two distinct support points whenever their distance is at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\), and define
\[
\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}
\]
as the set of connected components of the resulting graph.
\item For each \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define the associated true and candidate support sets by
\[
K_C(P):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\},
\qquad
K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
\item Define the mass interval by
\[
I_C:=\left[
\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi)),
\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi))
\right].
\]
In the ordered-support and transport-plan representation of \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), each endpoint is the value of a finite union of fixed-dimensional mixed-integer constrained programs. For each \(1\le r\le k\), introduce binary variables
\[
z_a\in\{0,1\},\qquad 1\le a\le r,
\]
with
\[
z_a=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \min_{c\in C}|x_a-c|\le\rho_{n,\alpha},
\]
and minimize or maximize
\[
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a z_a
\]
subject to the ordered-support, atom-floor, simplex, and transport constraints defining \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\).
\item Output the report
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}
:=
\left\{
\left(
C,\,
[\min C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\max C+\rho_{n,\alpha}],\,
I_C
\right):
C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For each component \(C\), define the external true-support gap by
\[
\Delta_C(P):=\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)=\emptyset\).
\end{enumerate}

2eeb9dc58be4007cd55307899f3242fc3d59fdf3.title: Labeled-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\)
2eeb9dc58be4007cd55307899f3242fc3d59fdf3.body:
The labeled-weight estimator is computed from \(\widehat\nu_n\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Write the positive law estimator uniquely as
\[
\widehat\nu_n=\sum_{\ell=1}^{\widehat s_n}\widehat w_{\ell,n}\delta_{\widehat\tau_{\ell,n}},
\]
where
\[
\widehat\tau_{1,n}<\cdots<\widehat\tau_{\widehat s_n,n},
\qquad
\widehat w_{\ell,n}>0\quad\text{for every }1\le \ell\le \widehat s_n.
\]
\item Define
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:=
\begin{cases}
(\widehat w_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat w_{k,n}), & \widehat s_n=k,\\
(1/k,\ldots,1/k), & \widehat s_n<k.
\end{cases}
\]
\item The ordering of finitely many support points and extraction of their jump sizes define a total Borel map into \(\Delta^{k-1}\).
\end{enumerate}

c66d3d30b2f15f6ff6d7717be37614babf6c91b9.title: Two-class witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\)
c66d3d30b2f15f6ff6d7717be37614babf6c91b9.body:
For \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), the two-class witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) is the law specified by
\[
P(U=1)=0.4,\qquad P(U=2)=0.6,
\]
\[
P(T=1\mid U=1)=0.4,\qquad P(T=1\mid U=2)=0.6,
\]
\[
X=(1,X_2)^\top,\qquad Z=(1,Z_2)^\top,
\]
\[
B=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.2&0.8\end{psmallmatrix},
\qquad
A_0=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.3&0.7\end{psmallmatrix},
\qquad
A_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.35&0.75\end{psmallmatrix},
\]
\[
E[Y(0)\mid U]=(0.25,0.25),
\qquad
E[Y(1)\mid U]=(0.5-\varepsilon,0.5+\varepsilon).
\]
Conditional on \(U\), the variables \(X_2\), \(Y(0)\), \(Y(1)\), and \(T\) are mutually independent Bernoulli variables with the displayed conditional means. Conditional on \(U\) and \(T\), the variable \(Z_2\) is independent of \((X_2,Y(0),Y(1))\) and has conditional mean given by \(A_T\). The observed outcome is
\[
Y=Y(T).
\]

6bd8dd3035cda4d19f05fff1c9bfda0908b4d62a.title: Local quotient experiment \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\)
6bd8dd3035cda4d19f05fff1c9bfda0908b4d62a.body:
The local quotient-law KL experiment is
\[
\mathcal L_n^\nu
:=
\{P\in\mathcal M:P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:local-quotient-neighborhood}\},
\]
where \(\mathcal M\) is the model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).

861857c43835f1fe6e8f0481023b9bb9cf2fac4f.title: Local weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\)
861857c43835f1fe6e8f0481023b9bb9cf2fac4f.body:
The local labeled-weight KL experiment is
\[
\mathcal L_{n,g}^p
:=
\{P\in\mathcal M(g):P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood}\},
\]
where \(\mathcal M(g)\) is the gap-local stratum in \(\cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}\).

49e1c701710474faf1c10aa47733c43109393834.title: Constructive repair handle \(m\)
49e1c701710474faf1c10aa47733c43109393834.body:
The constructive repair handle is defined for laws in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item At the realized empirical summary, define the first \(2k\) spectral moments by
\[
m=(m_j)_{0\le j<2k}.
\]
\item Among all valid positive \(k\)-atomic laws \(\sum_i w_i\delta_{x_i}\), choose a minimizer of
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{2k-1}\left|m_j-\sum_i w_i x_i^j\right|.
\]
\item Extract the repaired real probability measure from the minimizing positive \(k\)-atomic law, transporting aggregate projector mass across each cluster diameter after replacing individual eigenvectors inside overlapping localization discs by Kato contour projectors.
\item For the labeled-weight converse, differentiate the Bernoulli factorization of \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and solve the linear score-cancellation equations for the proxy and treatment primitives so that a weight displacement \(h\) preserves the factorization and the observed score has order \(g h\).
\end{enumerate}

74aecb014687885d539a95b05e54453269ac53a9.title: Finite-net estimator \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\)
74aecb014687885d539a95b05e54453269ac53a9.body:
The input is the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\); the tuning constants are
\[
D:=4d_zd_x+d_x,\qquad
b:=4\sqrt{d_zd_x}+\sqrt{d_x},\qquad
\epsilon_n:=n^{-1/2}.
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item Partition the coordinate box \([-L,L]^D\) into a deterministic lexicographically ordered grid of half-open cubes whose side length is at most
\[
\epsilon_n/b.
\]

\item If \(\mathscr S=\varnothing\), set
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}:=\delta_0
\]
and stop.

\item For each grid cube that intersects \(\mathscr S\), choose one representative
\[
q_{n,\ell}\in\mathscr S.
\]
Let \(\widehat q_n\) be the smallest-index minimizer
\[
\widehat q_n
\in
\arg\min_{\ell} d_S(q_{n,\ell},\widehat S_n).
\]

\item At \(\widehat q_n\), form the vertically stacked proxy moment and retain the \(k\) right singular directions whose singular values exceed \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\). Denote the resulting orthonormal basis by
\[
V.
\]
Using this basis, form the compressed effect operator, left anchor, and right anchor
\[
\Delta,\qquad a,\qquad c
\]
from the compressed-operator formulas.

\item For each distinct eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\Delta\), define the spectral projector
\[
E_\lambda
:=
\prod_{\gamma\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta):\,\gamma\ne\lambda}
\frac{\Delta-\gamma I_k}{\lambda-\gamma},
\]
with the empty product equal to \(I_k\).

\item Output the atomic law
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}
:=
\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta)}
a^\top E_\lambda c\,\delta_\lambda .
\]
\end{enumerate}

6eb4125ac68d07e99522764a239d33db81e9fc7f.title: Sharp summary-inversion computation
6eb4125ac68d07e99522764a239d33db81e9fc7f.body:
It remains open whether, in the fixed-dimensional exact-real model, one can compute exactly and in time polynomial in \(n\) the sharp summary-inversion image
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
=
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le 2r_{n,\alpha}\}
\]
together with its exact support-dependent cluster extrema, using neither compact nearest-summary optimization nor black-box evaluation of \(\overline F\). The positive real law estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\), the honest outer set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), and every interval in the report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) have explicit fixed-dimensional constrained representations, including cases in which the raw empirical operator has nonreal eigenpairs. The question concerns a sharp polynomial-time algorithm for the original summary-inversion image and its extrema.

3115a5cd740590469b5372481e4e153f375075ff.title: One-Wasserstein transport cost
3115a5cd740590469b5372481e4e153f375075ff.body:
For fixed \(k\) and radius, let \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) be represented atomic laws with labelled weights and locations \((p_i,x_i)_{i=1}^k\) and \((q_j,y_j)_{j=1}^k\). Define
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
=
\inf\left\{
\sum_{i=1}^k\sum_{j=1}^k \gamma_{ij}|x_i-y_j|:
\gamma_{ij}\ge 0,\ 
\sum_{j=1}^k\gamma_{ij}=p_i\ \text{for every }i,\ 
\sum_{i=1}^k\gamma_{ij}=q_j\ \text{for every }j
\right\}.
\]

6890a549f531ec71c0bf9f3ebad45d13232d9f4a.title: Labelled atomic laws
6890a549f531ec71c0bf9f3ebad45d13232d9f4a.body:
For \(k\in\mathbb N\) and radius \(L_\tau\in\mathbb R\), an element
\(\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), also written
\(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), is a labelled list of \(k\) real weights and
\(k\) real atom locations,
\[
  \xi=\bigl((w_i(\xi))_{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}},(a_i(\xi))_{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}}\bigr),
  \qquad
  w_i(\xi),a_i(\xi)\in\mathbb R .
\]
The associated measure \(\nu_\xi\) on \(\mathbb R\) is
\[
  \nu_\xi
  =
  \sum_{i=1}^k \max\{w_i(\xi),0\}\,\delta_{a_i(\xi)} .
\]
Repeated atom locations contribute additively through this sum. The topology on
\(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) is the topology induced by the coordinate
map \(\xi\mapsto ((w_i(\xi))_i,(a_i(\xi))_i)\), and its measurable structure is
the corresponding pullback Borel structure.

15c3f8d240439b6ab147cfc10163e56903c89263.title: Model class

25e9cb89cdf13d61814d0d6e84cb9c6ddc5f9bd7.title: Prescribed structured lattice
25e9cb89cdf13d61814d0d6e84cb9c6ddc5f9bd7.body:
For \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), set \(L_\tau:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\). A structured-lattice estimator \(A\) with sample size \(n\), effect radius \(L_\tau\), candidate count \(A_{\mathrm{count}}\), and estimate map \(\widehat\lambda_A\) is prescribed when there exist a candidate enumeration
\[
\vartheta:\{0,\ldots,A_{\mathrm{count}}-1\}\to
\{\text{structured lattice points with }k\text{ atoms, }d_x\text{ target coordinates, and radius }L_\tau\}
\]
and a sample-dependent selected index
\[
i_\star:(O_{d_x,d_z})^n\to \{0,\ldots,A_{\mathrm{count}}-1\}
\]
such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Feasibility.)} Every enumerated candidate \(\vartheta_i\) is well formed for the parameters \(n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).
\item \textbf{(Exhaustiveness.)} For every well-formed structured lattice point \(\theta\) with the same parameters \(n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), some enumerated candidate \(\vartheta_i\) has the same \(V\), \(R\), weights, and effects as \(\theta\).
\item \textbf{(No duplicates.)} If two enumerated candidates \(\vartheta_i\) and \(\vartheta_j\) have the same \(V\), \(R\), weights, and effects, then \(i=j\).
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} For all \(i,j\), \(i\le j\) exactly when \(\vartheta_i\) is lexicographically no larger than \(\vartheta_j\).
\item \textbf{(Empirical minimization.)} For every sample \(\omega\in(O_{d_x,d_z})^n\) and every candidate index \(i\),
\[
J(\vartheta_{i_\star(\omega)};\widehat S_n(\omega))
\le
J(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega)),
\]
where
\[
J(\theta;s)
:=
\left\|\operatorname{matrixCLM}\!\left(
\operatorname{Op}(\theta)-\operatorname{EmpOp}\!\left(\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2},s\right)
\right)\right\|
+
\sqrt{\sum_a\left(\sum_u V_{a u}\sum_v R_{v u}p_v-s.m_X(a)\right)^2}
+
\sqrt{\sum_u\left(\sum_v R_{u v}\sum_a V_{a v}e_1(a)-1\right)^2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(First tie.)} For every sample \(\omega\) and candidate index \(i\), equality in the preceding display implies \(i_\star(\omega)\le i\).
\item \textbf{(Returned law.)} The estimator returns the atomic effect law of this selected candidate:
\[
\widehat\lambda_A(\omega)=\lambda_{\vartheta_{i_\star(\omega)}}\qquad\text{for every sample }\omega\in(O_{d_x,d_z})^n .
\]
\end{itemize}

6a61865c3b3353f56dc259268c26197bed085c29.title: Empirical observable summary
6a61865c3b3353f56dc259268c26197bed085c29.body:
For \(n,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and observed records
\(O_i=(T_i,X_i,Z_i,Y_i)\), \(i\in \operatorname{Fin}(n)\), with
\(T_i\in\{0,1\}\), \(X_i\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), \(Z_i\in\mathbb R^{d_z}\),
and \(Y_i\in\mathbb R\), define, for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i\in \operatorname{Fin}(n)} \mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}.
\]
The empirical armwise matrices are the \(d_z\times d_x\) matrices
\[
\widehat M_{t,n}(a,b)
:=
\bigl(\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\bigr)^{-1}
\sum_{i\in \operatorname{Fin}(n)}
\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}\,Z_i(a)X_i(b),
\]
and
\[
\widehat N_{t,n}(a,b)
:=
\bigl(\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\bigr)^{-1}
\sum_{i\in \operatorname{Fin}(n)}
\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}\,Y_iZ_i(a)X_i(b).
\]
The empirical target-proxy mean is
\[
\widehat m_{X,n}(b):=
(n)^{-1}\sum_{i\in \operatorname{Fin}(n)}X_i(b),
\]
where the inverse is the real-field inverse. The empirical five-block observable summary is
\[
\widehat S_n
:=
\bigl(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},
\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n}\bigr).
\]

58bf1a1bd386e5c69fc77f5ebf6eba156e18d95c.title: Gap-local model stratum
58bf1a1bd386e5c69fc77f5ebf6eba156e18d95c.body:
For fixed dimensions \(k,d_x,d_z\), envelope \(L\), positivity margin \(\pi_0\), rank margin \(\sigma_0\), and gap scale \(g\), the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) consists of exactly those full-data probability laws \(P\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\), as defined in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} \(0<g\) and \(g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Gap window.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:gap-window}.
\item \textbf{(Distinct effects.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:distinct-effects}.
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal M(g)
=
\{P\in\mathcal M: 0<g,\ g\le 1/4,\ P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}\}.
\]

3e6f0354a6c2a946aa0dce566fcbc9c5793ca664.title: Summary closure data
3e6f0354a6c2a946aa0dce566fcbc9c5793ca664.body:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), the summary-closure data consists of
\[
\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}^{\,d_S}
=\overline{S(\mathcal M)}^{\,d_S},
\]
together with the functional
\[
F:\mathscr S\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
defined as follows: for an admissible summary \(q\in\mathscr S\), choose an admissible model law \(Q\) realizing \(q\), and set
\[
F(q)=\nu_Q.
\]
The package also includes the spectral moment identity
\[
\int x^j\,d\nu_P(x)=a(P)^\top\Delta Q(P)^j c(P),
\qquad j=0,\ldots,2k-1,
\]
and the homogeneous-effect specialization
\[
\Delta Q(P)=\tau_\star I_k,
\qquad
\nu_P=\delta_{\tau_\star}.
\]

8b0b43e9faec111e54d611bacb24b59667b6cabb.title: Summary-space repair
8b0b43e9faec111e54d611bacb24b59667b6cabb.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), and
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal K=\operatorname{cl}(\mathscr S)
\]
be the \(d_S\)-closure of the admissible summary image at these constants. A summary-space repair datum consists of \(0<k\), \(0\le L_\tau\), a continuous map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]),
\]
which agrees with the model quotient law at every admissible model summary, and a Borel map
\[
\Pi:\text{summary space}\to \text{summary space}
\]
such that, for every summary \(s\), if \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), then
\[
\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K,
\qquad
d_S(\Pi(s),s)\le d_S(q,s)\quad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K,
\]
while if \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), then \(\Pi(s)=0\).

For a sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), with empirical five-block summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), the repaired estimator determined by this datum is the total Borel map
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\varnothing,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,
\end{cases}
\]
as an element of \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), where \(\delta_0\) is the unit point mass at zero represented in the \(k\)-atomic quotient class.

943e5258f331497896e90ee970f90df72c73e65d.title: Ordered weight estimator
943e5258f331497896e90ee970f90df72c73e65d.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Let \(R\) be repair data with \(k>0\), \(L_\tau\ge 0\), a continuous map \(\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), and a measurable selector \(\Pi\) on summary space such that \(\overline F(S(Q))=\nu_Q\) for every model law \(Q\), \(\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K\) minimizes \(d_S(q,s)\) over \(q\in\mathcal K\) whenever \(\mathcal K\neq\emptyset\), \(\Pi(s)=0\) for every \(s\) whenever \(\mathcal K=\emptyset\), and the resulting repaired quotient law is measurable in the sample.

For an observed sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\), with \(O_i\in O_{d_x,d_z}\), define the repaired law by
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\emptyset,\\
\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))), & \mathcal K\neq\emptyset.
\end{cases}
\]
Choose its fixed quotient representative \(\xi(\omega)\), with labelled weights \(\xi_w(i)\) and labelled atoms \(\xi_\tau(i)\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\). The labelled-weight estimator is the map
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega):=(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)_j)_{j=1}^k,
\]
where, if every labelled weight is positive and the labelled atom map is injective,
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)_j
=
\sum_{i=1}^k
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\ell:\xi_\tau(\ell)<\xi_\tau(i)\}=j-1
\right\}\xi_w(i),
\qquad j=1,\ldots,k,
\]
and otherwise
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)_j=\frac1k,
\qquad j=1,\ldots,k.
\]

c4f62290717c1f8ebba65f7c5f37f810fd440d42.title: Observed proxy moment factorization
c4f62290717c1f8ebba65f7c5f37f810fd440d42.body:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), with fixed target- and reference-proxy dimensions \(d_x,d_z\), in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} The number \(k\) of latent classes satisfies \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Target dimension.)} The target-proxy dimension satisfies \(k\le d_x\).
\item \textbf{(Boundedness radius.)} The uniform boundedness radius satisfies \(1\le L\), with the bounded-target-proxy condition as in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}.
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} The latent-arm positivity margin satisfies \(\pi_0>0\), with latent-arm positivity as in \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}.
\item \textbf{(Proxy separation.)} The reference- and target-proxy separation conditions hold as in \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation}.
\end{itemize}
Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise proxy moment \(M_t(P)\) from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments} factors as
\[
M_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_t B^\top,
\]
where \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix of \cref{obj:def:reference-feature}, \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix of \cref{obj:def:target-feature}, and
\[
\Gamma_t
=
\operatorname{diag}\left\{
\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k
\right\}.
\]

24890ed0c580c536b4bdd8e039800198adc9432d.title: Cluster report construction
24890ed0c580c536b4bdd8e039800198adc9432d.body:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), repair data \(R\), a structured-lattice estimator \(A\) at radius
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0,
\]
a sample \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\), and constants \(\alpha,C_0,C_{\mathrm{lat}}\), the cluster report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) is defined under the conditions
\[
0<n,\quad 0<\alpha<\frac12,\quad 1\le C_0,\quad 1\le L,\quad
0<\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k},\quad 0<C_{\mathrm{lat}},
\]
with \(R\) supplying the continuous summary repair and \(A\) supplied by the prescribed structured-lattice program.

Let
\[
r_{n,\alpha}=r_{n,\alpha}(n,\alpha,C_0,L),\qquad
\widehat\lambda_n=A((O_i)_{i=1}^n),
\]
and define
\[
R_{n,\alpha}
=
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}\right),
\qquad
m_\star=\pi_0,
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{m_\star}.
\]
The computable confidence class is
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
=
\left\{
\xi:
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and}\
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For every summary \(s\), the report stores the event
\[
E_P(s)=
\left\{
(O_i')_{i=1}^n:
d_S(\widehat S_n((O_i')_{i=1}^n),s)\le r_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
It stores \(\rho_{n,\alpha}>0\), the connected components
\[
\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}
=
\operatorname{components}_{\rho_{n,\alpha}}(\widehat\lambda_n),
\]
and, for any represented atomic law \(\nu\) and finite component \(C\),
\[
K_C(\nu)
=
\left\{
x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu):
\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le \rho_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For each component \(C\), its support interval is
\[
\left[\inf C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\ \sup C+\rho_{n,\alpha}\right],
\]
and its mass interval is
\[
I_C
=
\left[
\inf\left\{m:\exists \xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha},\
m=\xi(K_C(\xi))\right\},
\sup\left\{m:\exists \xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha},\
m=\xi(K_C(\xi))\right\}
\right].
\]
These intervals satisfy
\[
0\le I_C^-\le I_C^+\le 1.
\]
The endpoint predicate recorded in the report is the constrained endpoint-feasibility predicate for \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) centered at \(\widehat\lambda_n\), and the stored endpoint identity is
\[
I_C
=
\left[
\inf\{m:\operatorname{endpointFeasible}(C,m)\},
\sup\{m:\operatorname{endpointFeasible}(C,m)\}
\right].
\]
Finally, for any represented atomic law \(\nu\), the report stores
\[
\Delta_C(\nu)=
\operatorname{clusterExternalGap}_{\rho_{n,\alpha}}(\nu,C),
\]
with the range guarantee that, whenever \(\nu\) is valid,
\[
\Delta_C(\nu)=+\infty
\quad\text{or}\quad
0\le \Delta_C(\nu)\le 2L_\tau .
\]

1c12df2e97328d6fb4304ab8fec0c35aa1752372.title: Published VMW transfer
1c12df2e97328d6fb4304ab8fec0c35aa1752372.body:
Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).  There exist constants \(a,c\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<a\le \frac18,
\qquad
0<c .
\]
For every \(n\ge 1\), the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Quotient witness pair.)} The two laws \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness} belong to the published VMW model and satisfy the law-level finite-regularity condition consisting of positive dimensions, finite positive envelopes for \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\), positive treatment-arm probabilities, and a positive singular-value margin for the stacked proxy moment and each armwise projected proxy moment.  The collision law \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) is outside the published separated recovery regime.
\item \textbf{(Quotient lower bound.)} For every class \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) of full-data probability laws such that every \(P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu\) belongs to the published VMW model and satisfies the same law-level finite-regularity condition, if \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) contains laws equal to \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\), then every estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) of the quotient effect law with support radius \(80\sqrt2\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\ge \frac{c}{\sqrt n}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Separated labeled path.)} For every \(g\in\mathbb R\) with
\[
0<g\le \frac14,
\]
define the calibrated labeled-path displacement by
\[
h(n,g):=a\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}.
\]
Then \(h(n,g)\) lies in the tangent-amplitude domain, and the endpoint laws \(P_{g,0}\) and \(P_{g,h(n,g)}\) both belong to the published VMW model, satisfy the same law-level finite-regularity condition, and have spectrally separated latent effects.
\item \textbf{(Labeled-weight lower bound.)} For every \(g\in\mathbb R\) with \(0<g\le 1/4\) and every class \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) of full-data probability laws such that every \(P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) belongs to the published VMW model and satisfies the same law-level finite-regularity condition, if \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) contains laws equal to \(P_{g,0}\) and \(P_{g,h(n,g)}\), then every estimator \(\widetilde p_n\) of the ordered latent weights satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^p}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\left\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1
\right]
\ge
c\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

95494861ff3d76f3f38eb683df5f717d530f2ef7.title: Coordinate envelope bounds
95494861ff3d76f3f38eb683df5f717d530f2ef7.body:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), with \(\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Target-proxy dimension.)} \(k\le d_x\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope conditions.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product}.
\item \textbf{(Anchor normalization.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:anchor}.
\end{itemize}
Then the model envelope \(L\) bounds the target proxy, the reference proxy, and the outcome--reference-proxy products \(P\)-almost surely:
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|X_i|\le L\text{ for every }1\le i\le d_x\,\}=1,
\]
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|Z_j|\le L\text{ for every }1\le j\le d_z\,\}=1,
\]
and
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|Y Z_j|\le L\text{ for every }1\le j\le d_z\,\}=1.
\]

124812c49e7e0723d3bab4dcf1288263cb47259d.title: Latent effect envelope
124812c49e7e0723d3bab4dcf1288263cb47259d.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), let \(P\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), and fix a latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with the bounded-proxy, latent-arm-positivity, and proxy-rank-margin components recorded in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}
Then the latent-class treatment effect \(\tau_u\), formed from the latent means in \cref{obj:def:latent-mean,obj:def:latent-effect}, satisfies
\[
|\tau_u|\le L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
where \(L_\tau\) is the derived effect-support radius in \cref{obj:def:effect-radius}.

8a3593248ce7df8cb40566c202450a9bd5d5d3a2.title: Path stratum membership
8a3593248ce7df8cb40566c202450a9bd5d5d3a2.body:
For real numbers \(g\) and \(h\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} The path displacement satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Model constants.)} The constants in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin,obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects} are \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}. In particular, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M\), the scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\), its smallest positive effect gap \(\delta(P_{g,h})\) from \cref{obj:def:effect-gap} obeys
\[
\frac{g}{2}\le \delta(P_{g,h})\le 2g,
\]
and the two latent effects of \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} are distinct.

5ee4510d7ab2967d3fa256ef378bcb1590c312f5.title: Latent mean envelope
5ee4510d7ab2967d3fa256ef378bcb1590c312f5.body:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Model constants.)} \(1\le L\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model components.)} The model class includes the bounded target-proxy condition of \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}, the latent-arm positivity condition of \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}, and the proxy-rank margin condition of \cref{obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}
Then, for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and every treatment state \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the latent conditional potential-outcome mean \(\mu_{tu}\) of \cref{obj:def:latent-mean} satisfies
\[
|\mu_{tu}|\le \frac{L_\tau}{2},
\]
where \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) is the derived effect-support radius from \cref{obj:def:effect-radius}.

181af1bd117b733ec60aa84fbbf47e6ff25c0b73.title: Path local weight membership
181af1bd117b733ec60aa84fbbf47e6ff25c0b73.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in\mathbb R\) be the local Kullback--Leibler radius constant, and let \(g,h\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Local radius.)} \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1\), as in \cref{obj:def:local-kl-radius}.
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale \(g\) is in the gap window of \cref{obj:ass:gap-window}, with \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} The path displacement satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Observed KL calibration.)}
\[
16000\,g^2h^2\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) from \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) of \cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment} with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M(g)\) as in \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}, and its observed-data marginal from \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} obeys the neighborhood condition of \cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood}:
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\,\Vert\,(P_{g,0})_O\right)
\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n},
\qquad
P_{g,0}=P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}.
\]

683b2ccc72db32fcd55c5145e75be4e970ec2deb.title: Matching local lower bounds
683b2ccc72db32fcd55c5145e75be4e970ec2deb.body:
Fix \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in(0,1)\). There exist constants \(a,c,C\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<a\le \frac18,\qquad c>0,\qquad C>0,
\]
and, for every integer \(n\ge 1\), the following statements hold for the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Quotient-law risk.)} For every measurable quotient-law estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) with support radius
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
there is a law \(P\) in the local quotient-law experiment \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\) of \cref{obj:def:local-quotient-experiment} such that
\[
P=P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}
\quad\text{or}\quad
P=P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}},
\]
with \(P_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{wit}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}, and
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Ordered-weight risk.)} For every \(g\in(0,1/4]\) and every measurable ordered-weight estimator \(\widetilde p_n\) taking values in the simplex, there is a law \(P\) in the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\) of \cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment} such that
\[
P=P_{g,0}
\quad\text{or}\quad
P=P_{g,h(n,g)},
\qquad
h(n,g)=a\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\},
\]
and
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\|_1\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Quotient-law certificate.)} The laws \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) belong to the corresponding local quotient-law experiments, and their observed-data marginals and quotient laws satisfy
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\Vert (P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\right)
\le
\frac{C}{n},
\qquad
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
W_1\!\left(\nu_{P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}},\nu_{P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}}\right).
\]

\item \textbf{(Labeled-path certificate.)} For every \(g\in(0,1/4]\), with
\[
h=h(n,g)=a\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\},
\]
the displacement \(h\) lies in the tangent-amplitude domain, the laws \(P_{g,h}\) and \(P_{g,0}\) belong to the corresponding local labeled-weight experiments, and
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\Vert (P_{g,0})_O\right)
\le
C g^2h^2,
\qquad
\sum_i\left|p_i^{\uparrow}(P_{g,h})-p_i^{\uparrow}(P_{g,0})\right|
=
2|h|.
\]
\end{itemize}

b10f08c04b2eeecc5c4fde2c0285392c3c23cf83.title: Gap-local model stratum
