b10f08c04b2eeecc5c4fde2c0285392c3c23cf83.body: For the local effect-gap scale \(g\), the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) consists exactly of the full-data laws \(P\in\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class} satisfying \(0<g\le 1/4\), the gap-window condition in \cref{obj:ass:gap-window}, and the distinct-effects condition in \cref{obj:ass:distinct-effects}.

88a4277b74fe3515eb34c82f079556fdcd85e797.title: Model class
88a4277b74fe3515eb34c82f079556fdcd85e797.body:
The uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) consists of all full-data probability laws \(P\) for which:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Parameter domain.)} The fixed latent cardinality \(k\), target- and reference-proxy dimensions \(d_x,d_z\), uniform boundedness radius \(L\), latent-arm positivity margin \(\pi_0\), and proxy-rank singular-value margin \(\sigma_0\) satisfy
\[
2\le k,\quad k\le d_x,\quad k\le d_z,\quad 1\le L,\quad
0<\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k},\quad 0<\sigma_0\le 1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Full-data record.)} \(P\) is carried by records \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) with \(U\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(T\in\{0,1\}\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d_z}\), and \(Y(0),Y(1),Y\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Model restrictions.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:latent-ignorability,obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}\).
\end{itemize}

80fac5001c221b1d10d64386bbc14cb2b55be13e.title: Labelled atomic laws
80fac5001c221b1d10d64386bbc14cb2b55be13e.body:
For a slot count \(k\) and radius parameter \(L_\tau\), the represented atomic-law space \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), also abbreviated \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), is the labelled coordinate space of pairs
\[
\xi=(w,a),\qquad w:\{1,\ldots,k\}\to\mathbb R,\qquad a:\{1,\ldots,k\}\to\mathbb R .
\]
For \(\xi=(w,a)\), write \(\nu_\xi\) for the finite measure
\[
\nu_\xi=\sum_{i=1}^k (w_i)_+\,\delta_{a_i},
\]
where repeated locations contribute through the same Dirac mass. The topology is the one induced by the coordinate map \(\xi\mapsto(w,a)\), and the measurable structure is the corresponding pullback Borel structure from the two real coordinate vectors.

560f74192ad68bc9dda6b016f4d68678bdbf1251.title: Structured lattice program
560f74192ad68bc9dda6b016f4d68678bdbf1251.body:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), set
\[
L_\tau:=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
A structured-lattice estimator \(A\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) is prescribed when there exist an indexed candidate list
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),
\qquad
i\in\{1,\ldots,A.\mathrm{candidateCount}\},
\]
and, for every sample \(\omega=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), a selected index \(i_\star(\omega)\), such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Admissible candidates.)} Every \(\vartheta_i\) is a well-formed structured lattice point for \((n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), including the prescribed constraints on \(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i\) and the conditioning-matrix bound
\[
\|R_i\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 2\sqrt{k}\,L.
\]
\item \textbf{(Exhaustive list.)} For every well-formed structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\) with effect radius \(L_\tau\), there is an index \(i\) such that
\[
V_i=V,\qquad R_i=R,\qquad p_i=p,\qquad \tau_i=\tau.
\]
\item \textbf{(Unique representation.)} If two listed candidates agree in all four coordinates,
\[
V_i=V_j,\qquad R_i=R_j,\qquad p_i=p_j,\qquad \tau_i=\tau_j,
\]
then \(i=j\).
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} The index order is exactly the lexicographic order on structured lattice points:
\[
i\le j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\vartheta_i\preceq_{\mathrm{lex}}\vartheta_j.
\]
\item \textbf{(First minimizer.)} For every sample \(\omega\), with empirical summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), the selected candidate minimizes
\[
J(\vartheta;\widehat S_n(\omega))
:=
\operatorname{structuredLatticeCriterion}\!\left(\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2},\widehat S_n(\omega),\vartheta\right)
\]
over the listed candidates:
\[
J(\vartheta_{i_\star(\omega)};\widehat S_n(\omega))
\le
J(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\qquad\text{for every }i.
\]
Whenever another listed candidate ties this minimum,
\[
J(\vartheta_{i_\star(\omega)};\widehat S_n(\omega))
=
J(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega)),
\]
the selected index is lexicographically first, \(i_\star(\omega)\le i\).
\end{itemize}
The estimator returned by \(A\) is exactly the atomic effect law attached to this first minimizing candidate:
\[
A.\mathrm{estimate}(\omega)
=
\lambda_{\vartheta_{i_\star(\omega)}}.
\]

b941d09249457d569d705dab3b9f6d7d86fdb435.title: Closed summary data
b941d09249457d569d705dab3b9f6d7d86fdb435.body:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), the closed-summary data consist of the admissible summary image
\[
\mathscr S:=S(\mathcal M)=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\},
\]
its \(d_S\)-closure
\[
\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}^{\,d_S},
\]
and a quotient-law selector
\[
F:\mathscr S\to\mathcal P_k([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]).
\]
For each admissible summary, \(F\) selects a realizing model law \(P\) and returns its quotient latent-effect law \(\nu_P\). The data also record the moment identity
\[
\int x^j\,d\nu_P(x)=a(P)^\top\Delta Q(P)^jc(P),
\qquad j=0,\ldots,2k-1,
\]
and the homogeneous-effect specialization
\[
\Delta Q(P)=\tau_\star I_k,\qquad \nu_P=\delta_{\tau_\star}.
\]

8f4ceec4071b8bec60956ce023b8611a647412e2.title: Summary-space repair map
8f4ceec4071b8bec60956ce023b8611a647412e2.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Let
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\qquad
\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\subseteq \mathscr S_{d_x,d_z}.
\]
A summary-space repair datum consists of the following objects:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(0<k\) and \(0\le L_\tau\).
\item \textbf{(Extension.)} A continuous map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
whose value at every model summary \(S(Q)\) agrees with the quotient law induced by \(Q\).
\item \textbf{(Selector.)} A Borel map \(\Pi:\mathscr S_{d_x,d_z}\to\mathscr S_{d_x,d_z}\) such that, whenever \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\),
\[
\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K,
\qquad
d_S(\Pi(s),s)\le d_S(q,s)\quad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K.
\]
If \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), the same datum sets \(\Pi(s)=0\) for every \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Repair measurability.)} The sample-to-law map defined below is Borel measurable.
\end{itemize}
For a sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), let \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\) be the empirical five-block observable summary.  The repaired estimator is
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr),& \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\delta_0,& \mathcal K=\varnothing,
\end{cases}
\]
as an element of \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\).

8d2fa1b9d39ee0dfa9fe1277795af7f4d5edb02e.title: Ordered labeled weights
8d2fa1b9d39ee0dfa9fe1277795af7f4d5edb02e.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Let \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) be the effect-support radius, and let \(\mathcal K\) be the closure of the admissible summary image. A repair datum \(R\) supplies \(k>0\), \(L_\tau\ge 0\), a continuous extension
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]),
\]
a Borel selector \(\Pi\) from summary space to summary space which selects a \(d_S\)-nearest point of \(\mathcal K\) when \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty and equals \(0\) when \(\mathcal K\) is empty, agrees with the model quotient law on admissible model summaries, and makes the resulting repaired law estimator Borel.

For an observed sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), define the repaired quotient-law estimator by
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\emptyset,\\
\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))), & \mathcal K\ne\emptyset.
\end{cases}
\]
Choose the representative of \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\) with labelled weights \(w_i\) and labelled atoms \(\tau_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,k\). The ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)\in\mathbb R^k\) is the total map with \(j\)th coordinate
\[
\widehat p_{n,j}^{\uparrow}(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^k w_i\,\mathbf 1\!\left\{\#\{\ell:\tau_\ell<\tau_i\}=j-1\right\},
& \text{if }w_i>0\text{ for every }i\text{ and the labelled atoms }\tau_i\text{ are pairwise distinct},\\[1.2em]
1/k, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
for \(j=1,\ldots,k\).

0c3f80cbfecb4d2a56fbb0f4612f7d3e3fdeaab0.title: Cluster report construction
0c3f80cbfecb4d2a56fbb0f4612f7d3e3fdeaab0.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and set \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\).  The cluster report
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}
\]
is defined from the following inputs:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Repair data.)} Summary repair data \(R\) at \((k,d_x,d_z,n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), carrying \(k>0\), \(L_\tau\ge 0\), a continuous extension \(\overline F\) on \(\mathcal K\), and a measurable nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\) with its empty-set fallback.
\item \textbf{(Lattice estimator.)} A measurable lattice estimator \(A\) with effect radius \(L_\tau\), whose estimate is the empirical-summary rule and whose output satisfies its atom-floor certificate.
\item \textbf{(Prescribed lattice.)} The estimator \(A\) is the prescribed structured-lattice estimator: its finite candidate list is exhaustive over well-formed structured-lattice points, has no duplicate represented point, is lexicographically ordered, and selects the first minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\).
\item \textbf{(Sample and constants.)} A sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) and constants \(\alpha,C_0,C_{\mathrm{lat}}\) satisfy
\[
0<n,\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac12,\qquad
1\le C_0,\qquad
1\le L,\qquad
0<\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k},\qquad
0<C_{\mathrm{lat}}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Let
\[
r_{n,\alpha}:=\operatorname{summaryRadius}(n,\alpha,C_0,L),
\qquad
\widehat\lambda_n:=A(\omega),
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}\right),
\qquad
m_\star:=\pi_0,
\]
and
\[
\rho_{n,\alpha}:=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{m_\star}.
\]
The event map in the report is
\[
E_P(s):=\left\{\omega'\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n:
d_S(\widehat S_n(\omega'),s)\le r_{n,\alpha}\right\}.
\]
The empirical components \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) are the connected components of the represented support of \(\widehat\lambda_n\) at association radius \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  For any represented atomic law \(\nu\) and finite set \(C\subset\mathbb R\), both the true-association and candidate-association maps are
\[
K_C(\nu):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le \rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
For every finite \(C\subset\mathbb R\), the support interval is
\[
\left[\inf C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\ \sup C+\rho_{n,\alpha}\right],
\]
and the mass interval is
\[
I_C:=
\left[
\inf\left\{m:\exists \xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha},\
m=\xi\bigl(K_C(\xi)\bigr)\right\},
\sup\left\{m:\exists \xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha},\
m=\xi\bigl(K_C(\xi)\bigr)\right\}
\right],
\]
where
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
=
\left\{\xi:
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and}\
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
The interval satisfies, for every \(C\),
\[
0\le I_C^{\mathrm{lo}}\le I_C^{\mathrm{hi}}\le 1,
\]
and it is represented by the endpoint-feasibility extrema
\[
I_C
=
\left[
\inf\{m:\operatorname{EndpointFeasible}(C,m)\},
\sup\{m:\operatorname{EndpointFeasible}(C,m)\}
\right].
\]
Finally, for every represented atomic law \(\nu\) and finite set \(C\), the external gap recorded in the report is
\[
\Delta_C(\nu)
=
\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(\nu),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu)\setminus K_C(\nu)\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when the second set is empty; whenever \(\nu\) is valid,
\[
\Delta_C(\nu)=+\infty
\quad\text{or}\quad
0\le \Delta_C(\nu)\le 2L_\tau .
\]

af94bba903b0687f8d076f359f332b8c04f497d5.title: Path stratum membership

0d7f1565e02737f6b71bec173e09da7107e6fb29.title: Path local weight membership
0d7f1565e02737f6b71bec173e09da7107e6fb29.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) and let \(c_{\mathrm{loc}},g,h\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Local radius.)} \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1\).
\item \textbf{(Gap window.)} \(0<g\le 1/4\), as in \cref{obj:ass:gap-window}.
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Observed KL calibration.)}
\[
16000\,g^2h^2\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) from \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) of \cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment} with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M(g)\) as in \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}, and its observed-data marginal satisfies the neighborhood condition of \cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood} relative to the witness law \(P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}\) of \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}:
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\,\Vert\,(P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2})_O\right)
\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]

0dff125ecf385677262dfc505f97553c05fb551b.title: Cluster report data
0dff125ecf385677262dfc505f97553c05fb551b.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and set
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
The cluster report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) is defined from the following data:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Repair data.)} Summary repair data \(R\) at \((k,d_x,d_z,n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), carrying \(k>0\), \(L_\tau\ge 0\), a continuous extension \(\overline F\) on \(\mathcal K\), and a measurable nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\) with its fallback value when \(\mathcal K\) is empty.
\item \textbf{(Lattice estimator.)} A measurable lattice estimator \(A\) with effect radius \(L_\tau\), whose estimate is the empirical-summary rule and whose output carries its atom-floor certificate.
\item \textbf{(Prescribed lattice.)} The estimator \(A\) is the prescribed structured-lattice estimator: its finite candidate list is exhaustive over well-formed structured-lattice points, has unique represented candidates, is lexicographically ordered, and selects the first minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\).
\item \textbf{(Sample and constants.)} A sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) and constants \(\alpha,C_0,C_{\mathrm{lat}}\) satisfy
\[
0<n,\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac12,\qquad
1\le C_0,\qquad
1\le L,\qquad
0<\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k},\qquad
0<C_{\mathrm{lat}}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Let
\[
r_{n,\alpha}:=\operatorname{summaryRadius}(n,\alpha,C_0,L),
\qquad
\widehat\lambda_n:=A(\omega),
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}\right),
\qquad
m_\star:=\pi_0,
\]
and
\[
\rho_{n,\alpha}:=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{m_\star}.
\]
The event map in \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) is
\[
E_P(s):=\left\{\omega'\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n:
d_S(\widehat S_n(\omega'),s)\le r_{n,\alpha}\right\}.
\]
The empirical components \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) are the connected components of the represented support of \(\widehat\lambda_n\) under the graph that joins two support points when their distance is at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  For any represented atomic law \(\nu\) and finite set \(C\subset\mathbb R\), both association maps recorded by the report are
\[
K_C(\nu):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le \rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
For every finite \(C\subset\mathbb R\), the support interval is
\[
\left[\inf C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\ \sup C+\rho_{n,\alpha}\right],
\]
and the mass interval is
\[
I_C:=
\left[
\inf\left\{m:\exists \xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha},\
m=\xi\bigl(K_C(\xi)\bigr)\right\},
\sup\left\{m:\exists \xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha},\
m=\xi\bigl(K_C(\xi)\bigr)\right\}
\right],
\]
where
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
=
\left\{\xi:
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and}\
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
The interval satisfies, for every \(C\),
\[
0\le I_C^{\mathrm{lo}}\le I_C^{\mathrm{hi}}\le 1,
\]
and the endpoint-feasibility predicate in the report represents the same extrema:
\[
I_C
=
\left[
\inf\{m:\operatorname{EndpointFeasible}(C,m)\},
\sup\{m:\operatorname{EndpointFeasible}(C,m)\}
\right].
\]
Finally, for every represented atomic law \(\nu\) and finite set \(C\), the external gap recorded in the report is
\[
\Delta_C(\nu)
=
\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(\nu),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu)\setminus K_C(\nu)\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when the second set is empty.  Whenever \(\nu\) is valid,
\[
\Delta_C(\nu)=+\infty
\quad\text{or}\quad
0\le \Delta_C(\nu)\le 2L_\tau .
\]

b24e570b7a2a239b813f140cb824e52156d1c341.title: Cluster-adaptive lattice report
b24e570b7a2a239b813f140cb824e52156d1c341.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(\pi_0\in\mathbb R\), and \(\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Latent mass.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), if
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
and
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
      +\frac{2\sqrt{k}L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}Lc_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}Lc_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
\end{gathered}
\]
then
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\,
(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\}
\]
is positive.  For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a measurable structured-lattice estimator
\(\widehat\lambda_n\) with effect radius \(L_\tau\) and repair data consisting of the continuous extension \(\overline F\), the Borel nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\), and the empty-closure zero-law fallback, such that \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is obtained from an exhaustive lexicographically ordered finite list of well-formed structured-lattice candidates by choosing the first minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\).

For every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the estimator has atom floor
\[
m_\star=\pi_0.
\]
Moreover, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class} and every sample \(\omega\),
\[
W_1\!\left(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega),\nu_P\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
\left\{
d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P)\right)+\frac{1}{\sqrt n}
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
r_{n,\alpha}
=
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}},
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}
=
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\right),
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\pi_0},
\]
with \(\widehat S_n\) as in \cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}, and set
\[
E_P=\left\{\omega:
d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P)\right)\le r_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge 1-\alpha .
\]

For every sample \(\omega\in E_P\), let \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) be the empirical support components of the representative of \(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)\) using linking radius \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  For an atomic law \(\nu\) and a component \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define
\[
K_C(\nu)
=
\left\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu):
\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le \rho_{n,\alpha}
\right\},
\]
and define
\[
\Delta_C(\nu)
=
\begin{cases}
\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(\nu),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu)\setminus K_C(\nu)\},
& \operatorname{supp}(\nu)\setminus K_C(\nu)\ne\varnothing,\\
+\infty,
& \operatorname{supp}(\nu)\setminus K_C(\nu)=\varnothing .
\end{cases}
\]
The cluster report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) centered at \(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)\) satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Partition.)} For every \(x\in\mathbb R\),
\[
x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists!\,C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\ \text{such that}\ x\in K_C(\nu_P).
\]
\item \textbf{(Association.)} For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), the set \(K_C(\nu_P)\) is nonempty and is contained in \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\).
\item \textbf{(Support interval.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(x\in K_C(\nu_P)\), then \(x\) lies in the reported support interval for \(C\).
\item \textbf{(Mass interval.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), then the reported mass interval \(I_C\) contains \(\nu_P(K_C(\nu_P))\).
\item \textbf{(Singleton width.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(K_C(\nu_P)\) is a singleton, then the reported support interval for \(C\) has length at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\), and
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\delta(P)}\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(External-gap width.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\Delta_C(\nu_P)=+\infty\), then \(\operatorname{length}(I_C)=0\).  For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\),
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\Delta_C(\nu_P)}\right\},
\]
with the displayed right side read as zero when \(\Delta_C(\nu_P)=+\infty\).
\item \textbf{(Constrained representation.)} The computable class
\(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) has the finite constrained-program representation
\[
\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and}\ 
\exists\gamma\ \text{with transport cost at most } R_{n,\alpha}
\text{ from }\xi\text{ to }\widehat\lambda_n(\omega).
\]
\end{itemize}

eace12e665bdc0909412540dd18a77821ff29df6.title: Uniform proxy model class
eace12e665bdc0909412540dd18a77821ff29df6.body:
The uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) consists of full-data probability laws \(P\) on records \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) with the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Record space.)} \(U\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(T\in\{0,1\}\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d_z}\), and \(Y(0),Y(1),Y\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Core parameter domain.)} The fixed parameters satisfy
\[
2\le k,\qquad k\le d_x,\qquad k\le d_z,\qquad 1\le L,\qquad 0<\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k},\qquad 0<\sigma_0\le 1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Model conditions.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:latent-ignorability,obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}\).
\end{itemize}

6d9469034e2c2b0d9f8a37ef0053aa2676447173.title: Labelled atomic laws
6d9469034e2c2b0d9f8a37ef0053aa2676447173.body:
For \(k\in\mathbb N\) and \(L_\tau\in\mathbb R\), \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), also written \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), denotes the labelled \(k\)-slot atomic-law coordinate space. An element \(\xi\) consists exactly of two coordinate maps,
\[
w_\xi:\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\to\mathbb R,
\qquad
a_\xi:\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\to\mathbb R .
\]
The topology is the topology induced by the coordinate map \(\xi\mapsto (w_\xi,a_\xi)\), and the measurable structure is the corresponding coordinate pullback of the Borel structure on the two real coordinate vectors. The represented measure associated with \(\xi\) is
\[
\nu_\xi
=
\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\max\{w_\xi(i),0\}\,\delta_{a_\xi(i)} .
\]
Coincident atom locations contribute additively through this displayed sum.

fba20364a9bcf48b67035b5902ab7e44df79fa61.title: Gap-local model stratum
fba20364a9bcf48b67035b5902ab7e44df79fa61.body:
For a real local effect-gap scale \(g\), the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) consists of the full-data probability laws \(P\) such that
\[
P\in\mathcal M(g).
\]
Equivalently, membership means that the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(P\) belongs to the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Gap and distinct effects.)} \(P\) satisfies the gap-window and distinct-effect conditions in \cref{obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}.
\end{itemize}

de6c4c239401e00483c3700625781ce1a1d4e9c1.title: Prescribed structured lattice
de6c4c239401e00483c3700625781ce1a1d4e9c1.body:
For \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), set
\[
L_\tau:=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
A structured-lattice estimator \(A\) with radius \(L_\tau\) is prescribed when there are an enumeration
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),
\qquad i=0,\ldots,A.\mathrm{candidateCount}-1,
\]
of structured lattice points and a sample-indexed selector
\[
\iota(\omega)\in\{0,\ldots,A.\mathrm{candidateCount}-1\},
\qquad
\omega:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to O_{d_x,d_z},
\]
such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Admissibility.)} Every \(\vartheta_i\) is well formed for \(n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), including the conditioning-matrix bound \(\|R_i\|\le 2\sqrt{k}\,L\).
\item \textbf{(Exhaustion.)} For every well-formed structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\) with radius \(L_\tau\), there is an index \(i\) such that
\[
V_i=V,\qquad R_i=R,\qquad p_i=p,\qquad \tau_i=\tau.
\]
\item \textbf{(No duplicates.)} If two enumerated candidates have the same four displayed components, then their indices are equal.
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} For all indices \(i,j\),
\[
i\le j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\vartheta_i\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\vartheta_j.
\]
\item \textbf{(First minimizer.)} For every sample \(\omega\), the selected index \(\iota(\omega)\) minimizes
\[
J(\vartheta;\omega)
:=
\left\|
\operatorname{matrixCLM}\!\left(
\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta)
-
\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}\!\left(\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2},\widehat S_n(\omega)\right)
\right)
\right\|
+
\left(\sum_a
\left[
\sum_u V_{a u}\Bigl(\sum_v R_{v u}p_v\Bigr)
-\widehat m_{X,n,a}(\omega)
\right]^2
\right)^{1/2}
+
\left(\sum_u
\left[
\sum_v R_{u v}\Bigl(\sum_a V_{a v}e_{1,a}\Bigr)-1
\right]^2
\right)^{1/2}
\]
over the enumerated candidates, and it is the first such minimizer in the enumeration: whenever
\[
J(\vartheta_{\iota(\omega)};\omega)=J(\vartheta_i;\omega),
\]
one has \(\iota(\omega)\le i\).
\end{itemize}
For every sample \(\omega\), the estimator returns the effect law of the selected candidate:
\[
A.\mathrm{estimate}(\omega)=\lambda_{\vartheta_{\iota(\omega)}}.
\]

2073b7cf919c69b8a31e280352800063913aa24c.title: Summary closure data
2073b7cf919c69b8a31e280352800063913aa24c.body:
For \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), the summary-closure data consist of
\[
\mathcal K
=
\overline{\mathscr S}^{\,d_S},
\qquad
\mathscr S=S(\mathcal M),
\]
together with the functional
\[
F:\mathscr S\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]).
\]
For \(q\in\mathscr S\), fix a model law \(P_q\in\mathcal M\) whose observable summary is \(q\), and set
\[
F(q)=\nu_{P_q}.
\]
The data also include the spectral moment identity
\[
\int x^j\,d\nu_{P_q}(x)
=
a(P_q)^\top\Delta Q(P_q)^j c(P_q),
\qquad
j=0,\ldots,2k-1,
\]
and the homogeneous-effect specialization
\[
\Delta Q(P_q)=\tau_\star I_k,
\qquad
\nu_{P_q}=\delta_{\tau_\star}.
\]

eb6533cea039ea6238da99d750e0f97c7c8ec359.title: Ordered weight estimator
eb6533cea039ea6238da99d750e0f97c7c8ec359.body:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), let \(R\) consist of the following repair data:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Size and radius.)} \(0<k\) and
\[
0\le L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Closed-summary repair.)} With
\[
\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S},
\]
\(R\) supplies a continuous map \(\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) that agrees with the model quotient law on model-generated summaries.
\item \textbf{(Nearest selector.)} \(R\) supplies a measurable selector \(\Pi\) on summary space such that, when \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty, \(\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K\) and minimizes \(d_S(q,s)\) over \(q\in\mathcal K\); when \(\mathcal K\) is empty, \(\Pi(s)=0\).
\item \textbf{(Sample repair.)} The repaired quotient law is the measurable rule
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\emptyset,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\emptyset.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{itemize}
For an observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), choose the quotient representative of \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\) and write its labelled masses and atoms as \((w_i(\omega),\tau_i(\omega))_{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}}\). The ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)\in\mathbb R^k\) is the vector whose \(j\)th coordinate is
\[
\widehat p_{n,j}^{\uparrow}(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\ell:\tau_\ell(\omega)<\tau_i(\omega)\}=j-1
\right\}w_i(\omega),
&
\text{if } w_i(\omega)>0\text{ for every }i
\text{ and }i\mapsto \tau_i(\omega)\text{ is injective},\\[1.2em]
1/k, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

eb35d1a9d0c55c487b7d2e7fd7a1a846b91d6b05.title: Summary-space repair map
eb35d1a9d0c55c487b7d2e7fd7a1a846b91d6b05.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Set
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}
\]
and let \(\mathcal K\) be the \(d_S\)-closure of the admissible summary image in the five-block summary space.

A summary-space repair datum \(R\) consists of the following objects and conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Support radius.)} \(0<k\) and \(0\le L_\tau\).
\item \textbf{(Extension on the closure.)} A continuous map
\[
\overline F:\{q:q\in\mathcal K\}\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
such that, for every model law \(Q\) in the uniformly conditioned class with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), \(\overline F(S(Q))\) is the quotient latent-effect law induced by \(Q\).
\item \textbf{(Nearest-summary selector.)} A Borel map \(\Pi\) from the summary space to itself such that, when \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\),
\[
\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K,
\qquad
d_S(\Pi(s),s)\le d_S(q,s)\quad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K,
\]
and, when \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), \(\Pi(s)=0\) for every summary \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Measurable repaired map.)} The sample-to-law map defined below is Borel measurable.
\end{itemize}

For a sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\) of observed records \(O_i=(T_i,X_i,Z_i,Y_i)\), define the repaired estimator
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\varnothing,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\delta_0\) is the quotient law of the unit point mass at zero in \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\).

5c15373a1da657a5f4feb7170fb29ecaf41476d8.title: Path stratum membership
5c15373a1da657a5f4feb7170fb29ecaf41476d8.body:
For real numbers \(g\) and \(h\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} The path displacement satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum constants.)} The constants in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:def:gap-stratum,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin,obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}\) are \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:path-law-family}\) belongs to the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}\). Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M\), the scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\), the smallest positive effect gap \(\delta(P_{g,h})\) from \(\cref{obj:def:effect-gap}\) obeys the gap window from \(\cref{obj:ass:gap-window}\),
\[
\frac{g}{2}\le \delta(P_{g,h})\le 2g,
\]
and the two latent effects of \(\cref{obj:def:latent-effect}\) are distinct as in \(\cref{obj:ass:distinct-effects}\).

9e37febfbae9675eca4657747eb3746e87107761.title: Path local-weight membership
9e37febfbae9675eca4657747eb3746e87107761.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) and let \(c_{\mathrm{loc}},g,h\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Local radius.)} The local Kullback--Leibler radius constant satisfies \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1\).
\item \textbf{(Gap window.)} The local effect-gap scale \(g\) lies in the window of \cref{obj:ass:gap-window}, with
\[
0<g\le \frac14 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} The path displacement satisfies
\[
|h|\le \frac1{100}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed KL calibration.)} The calibration inequality holds:
\[
16000\,g^2h^2\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) from \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) of \cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment} with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). In particular, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M(g)\) as in \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}, and its observed-data marginal satisfies the neighborhood condition of \cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood}:
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\,\Vert\,(P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2})_O\right)
\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]

bd24a84deb675ae13be331cef945fa420579b5e2.title: Atomic law coordinates
bd24a84deb675ae13be331cef945fa420579b5e2.body:
For \(k\in\mathbb N\) and real radius \(L_\tau\), the class \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), also abbreviated \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), denotes the labelled \(k\)-slot atomic-law coordinate space. An element \(\xi\) consists exactly of two real coordinate maps,
\[
w_\xi:\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\to\mathbb R,
\qquad
a_\xi:\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\to\mathbb R .
\]
The topology is induced by the coordinate map \(\xi\mapsto (w_\xi,a_\xi)\), and the measurable structure is the coordinate pullback of the Borel structure on the two real coordinate vectors. The represented measure associated with \(\xi\) is
\[
\nu_\xi
=
\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\max\{w_\xi(i),0\}\,\delta_{a_\xi(i)} .
\]
Coincident atom locations contribute additively through this displayed sum.

395fea64098295fc71e05e737423243aaa105d12.title: Collision-uniform root rate
395fea64098295fc71e05e737423243aaa105d12.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform bounds.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) taking values in \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), with
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0,
\]
and a nearest-summary repair estimator \(\widehat\nu_n\) of the form described in \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\).  The estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the first lexicographic minimizer over a finite exhaustive structured lattice of well-formed candidates \(\vartheta\) for the criterion \(J_n(\vartheta)\), with tie-breaking by the lattice order and output \(\lambda_\vartheta\); it also carries a samplewise aggregate distinct-atom mass floor.  Both \(\widehat\lambda_n\) and \(\widehat\nu_n\) are Borel sample maps.

For every \(\eta\) satisfying \(0<\eta<1/2\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\), and the \(n\)-sample observed experiment \(Q_P^{(n)}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
\max\!\left\{
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P),
W_1(\widehat\nu_n,\nu_P)
\right\}
>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}\le \eta .
\]
Moreover, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\{N_{t,n}=0\}\le (1-k\pi_0)^n .
\]

fb3d367dcf12650b500e097c6f91f93ed9727901.title: Cluster report validity
fb3d367dcf12650b500e097c6f91f93ed9727901.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Atom floor.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), the following statement holds.  Put
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\qquad
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\]
and define
\[
\begin{gathered}
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}\,L L_\tau}{\sigma_0},\qquad
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\\
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}\,L L_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
     +\frac{2\sqrt{k}\,L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}\,L c_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}\,L c_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
\end{gathered}
\]
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\,
\left(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f\right)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\}.
\]
Then \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}>0\).  For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a measurable lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) with support radius \(L_\tau\), summary-repair data consisting of a continuous extension on \(\mathcal K\) and a Borel nearest-summary selector, and a finite structured-lattice candidate list with actual candidate count such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exhaustive lattice.)} The list consists exactly of the well-formed structured-lattice candidates, with no duplicates in \((V,R,p,\tau)\).
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} Candidate indices agree with the lexicographic order on structured-lattice candidates.
\item \textbf{(First minimizer.)} For each sample \(\omega\), \(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)\) is the effect law of the first candidate minimizing \(J_n(\vartheta)\), the structured-lattice criterion at empirical summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\) with threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).
\end{itemize}
For every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the estimator has atom floor \(\pi_0\).  Moreover, for every full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:model-class} and every sample \(\omega\),
\[
W_1\!\left(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega),\nu_P\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
\left\{
d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P)\right)+n^{-1/2}
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
r_{n,\alpha}
=
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}},
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}
=
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+n^{-1/2}\right),
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\pi_0},
\]
with \(\widehat S_n\) as in \cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}, and set
\[
E_P
=
\left\{
\omega:
d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P)\right)\le r_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge 1-\alpha.
\]
For every \(\omega\in E_P\), form the computable confidence set
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
=
\left\{
\xi:
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and}\
W_1\!\left(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)\right)\le R_{n,\alpha}
\right\},
\]
and let the cluster report centered at \(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)\) have empirical components
\(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), association radius \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\), associated true sets
\(K_C(P)\), support intervals, mass intervals \(I_C\), and external gaps \(\Delta_C(P)\).  Then, for the representative atomic law \(\nu_P\), the following properties hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Partition.)} For every \(x\),
\[
x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists!\,C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\ \text{such that }x\in K_C(P).
\]
\item \textbf{(Nonempty associated support.)} For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), the set \(K_C(P)\) is nonempty and satisfies \(K_C(P)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\).
\item \textbf{(Support interval.)} For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and every \(x\in K_C(P)\), \(x\) lies in the reported support interval for \(C\).
\item \textbf{(Mass interval.)} For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\),
\[
\nu_P(K_C(P))\in I_C.
\]
\item \textbf{(Singleton width.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(K_C(P)\) is a singleton, then the reported support interval for \(C\) has length at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\), and
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\delta(P)}\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(External-gap width.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\), then \(\operatorname{length}(I_C)=0\).  For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\),
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\Delta_C(P)}\right\},
\]
with the displayed right side read as zero when \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\).
\item \textbf{(Constrained representation.)} The set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) has the finite transport-plan representation
\[
\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and there exists a finite transport plan from }\xi\text{ to }\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)
\text{ with cost at most }R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
\end{itemize}

df52a63f22ec36a6f6b3ef08ff9a6812a0ee8acb.title: Separated recovery regime
df52a63f22ec36a6f6b3ef08ff9a6812a0ee8acb.body:
A full-data law \(P\) lies in the separated recovery regime when it satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} The published VMW structural model conditions.
\item \textbf{(Anchor normalization.)} The first target-proxy coordinate satisfies \(X_1=1\) almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Finite regularity.)} The published VMW finite-regularity condition.
\item \textbf{(Spectral separation.)} The latent-class treatment effects satisfy \(\tau_u\ne\tau_v\) whenever \(u\ne v\).
\end{itemize}
In this regime, the separated-recovery estimator analyzed by \citet{VirkMazaheriWu2026} is evaluated under its stated sample-size and radius conditions and returns simultaneous high-probability bounds for the treatment effects, the anchor-normalized feature matrix, and the simplex-projected mixture weights.

d97382c8b1076eddc73a29a54da776924270a001.title: Ordered masses are invariant
d97382c8b1076eddc73a29a54da776924270a001.body:
Let \(\xi\) and \(\xi'\) be valid labelled representatives in \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), as in \cref{obj:def:atomic-law-class,obj:def:effect-radius}.  If they represent the same aggregated probability law, \(\nu_\xi=\nu_{\xi'}\), then their ordered-mass maps from \cref{obj:def:ordered-mass-target} agree:
\[
\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi)=\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi').
\]
Thus the ordered aggregate masses are determined by the represented probability law, independently of the labelled finite representative.

1d15c963061a3d7afaca14728dd07778675f8435.title: Ordered masses are invariant
1d15c963061a3d7afaca14728dd07778675f8435.body:
Let \(\xi\) and \(\xi'\) be valid labelled representatives in \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:atomic-law-class,obj:def:effect-radius}\).  If they represent the same aggregated probability law, \(\nu_\xi=\nu_{\xi'}\), then the ordered-mass maps defined in \(\cref{obj:synth_26}\) agree:
\[
\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi)=\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi').
\]
Thus the ordered aggregate masses are determined by the represented probability law.

b6b894c73d0abd95cab4b779ddd25725425cd779.title: Gap-local stratum
b6b894c73d0abd95cab4b779ddd25725425cd779.body: For a local effect-gap scale \(g\) satisfying \(0<g\le 1/4\), the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) is the class of full-data laws \(P\) in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class} that satisfy \cref{obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}.

1b102465a81d406de486763296f38a4084a3f3e6.title: Uniform proxy model class
1b102465a81d406de486763296f38a4084a3f3e6.body:
The uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) is the class of full-data probability laws \(P\) for records \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Record space.)} \(U\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(T\in\{0,1\}\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d_z}\), and \(Y(0),Y(1),Y\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Parameter domain.)} The dimensions and constants obey
\[
2\le k,\qquad k\le d_x,\qquad k\le d_z,\qquad 1\le L,\qquad 0<\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k},\qquad 0<\sigma_0\le 1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Model restrictions.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:latent-ignorability,obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}

8cc9c34ee644d5f77c99e2d06f88f41efaa2be32.title: Atomic law coordinates
8cc9c34ee644d5f77c99e2d06f88f41efaa2be32.body:
For \(k\in\mathbb N\) and radius parameter \(L_\tau\in\mathbb R\), a represented atomic law
\[
\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
is a labelled coordinate record
\[
\xi=\bigl((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k}\bigr),
\qquad
w_i\in\mathbb R,\quad a_i\in\mathbb R .
\]
The abbreviation \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) denotes the same represented space. The associated measure on \(\mathbb R\) is
\[
\nu_\xi=\sum_{i<k}\operatorname{ofReal}(w_i)\,\delta_{a_i},
\]
so coincident labelled locations contribute additively at that location. The topology on this represented space is the topology induced by the coordinate map
\[
\xi\mapsto \bigl((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k}\bigr),
\]
and its measurable structure is the corresponding pullback Borel structure from the two real coordinate vectors.

dee8e0e12f81af3c2fe38c5bfde96b9dbb85f43e.title: Structured lattice program
dee8e0e12f81af3c2fe38c5bfde96b9dbb85f43e.body:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), let
\[
L_\tau:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0 .
\]
A structured-lattice estimator \(A\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) is prescribed when there are an enumeration
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),\qquad i=1,\ldots,A.\mathrm{candidateCount},
\]
of structured lattice points and, for every sample \(\omega=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a selected index \(i_\omega\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Well-formed exhaustive list.)} Each \(\vartheta_i\) is well formed for the parameters \((n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), including the conditioning-matrix bound
\[
\|R_i\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 2\sqrt{k}\,L,
\]
and every well-formed structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) appears in the list through an index \(i\) satisfying
\[
V_i=V,\qquad R_i=R,\qquad p_i=p,\qquad \tau_i=\tau .
\]
\item \textbf{(No duplicates.)} If two listed candidates agree in all four displayed coordinates,
\[
V_i=V_j,\qquad R_i=R_j,\qquad p_i=p_j,\qquad \tau_i=\tau_j,
\]
then \(i=j\).
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} The index order agrees exactly with the lexicographic order on candidates:
\[
i\le j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\vartheta_i\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\vartheta_j .
\]
\item \textbf{(First minimizer.)} For the empirical five-block summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), define
\[
J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n(\omega))
:=
\Bigl\|
D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n(\widehat S_n(\omega))
\Bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\left(
\sum_{a=1}^{d_x}
\left[
\sum_{u=1}^k V_{a u}\sum_{v=1}^k R_{v u}p_v
-\widehat m_{X,n,a}(\omega)
\right]^2
\right)^{1/2}
+
\left(
\sum_{u=1}^k
\left[
\sum_{v=1}^k R_{u v}\sum_{a=1}^{d_x}V_{a v}e_{1,a}
-1
\right]^2
\right)^{1/2},
\]
where the threshold in \(\widehat D_n\) is \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\). The selected index \(i_\omega\) satisfies
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
\le
J_n(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\qquad\text{for every }i,
\]
and any tie is resolved by the first lexicographic index:
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
=
J_n(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
i_\omega\le i .
\]
\item \textbf{(Returned law.)} The estimator returns the atomic effect law attached to the selected candidate:
\[
A(\omega)=\lambda_{\vartheta_{i_\omega}} .
\]
\end{itemize}

948ace5ed5a6d29e9742f8fad133dea7905397aa.title: Summary closure data
948ace5ed5a6d29e9742f8fad133dea7905397aa.body:
For \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), the summary-closure data consists of the closed feasible-summary set
\[
\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}^{\,d_S},
\qquad
\mathscr S:=S(\mathcal M)=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\},
\]
together with a quotient-law functional
\[
F:\mathscr S\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]).
\]
For each admissible summary \(q\in\mathscr S\), \(F(q)\) is the quotient latent-effect law \(\nu_{P_q}\) of a selected model representative \(P_q\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(S(P_q)=q\). The data also records the published spectral moment identity
\[
\int x^j\,d\nu_{P_q}(x)
=
a(P_q)^\top\Delta Q(P_q)^j c(P_q),
\qquad j=0,\ldots,2k-1,
\]
and, in the homogeneous-effect specialization with common effect \(\tau_\star\),
\[
\Delta Q(P_q)=\tau_\star I_k,
\qquad
\nu_{P_q}=\delta_{\tau_\star}.
\]

e6b32a3ca37bd3c54e59b68946ffaee86ab4fa6f.title: Summary-space repair map
e6b32a3ca37bd3c54e59b68946ffaee86ab4fa6f.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Let
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\qquad
\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S},
\]
where \(\mathscr S\) is the admissible image in the five-block summary space. A summary-space repair datum consists of \(k>0\), \(L_\tau\ge 0\), and maps
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]),
\qquad
\Pi:\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\to \mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}},
\]
with the following certified properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Extension.)} The map \(\overline F\) is continuous and, for every full-data law \(P\) in the uniformly conditioned model class, sends its observable summary \(S(P)\in\mathcal K\) to the quotient latent-effect law \(\nu_P\).
\item \textbf{(Nearest selector.)} The map \(\Pi\) is Borel measurable and, whenever \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\),
\[
\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K,
\qquad
d_S(\Pi(s),s)\le d_S(q,s)\quad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K .
\]
\item \textbf{(Fallback.)} Whenever \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), the selector satisfies
\[
\Pi(s)=0
\]
in the ambient five-block summary space for every \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Repair measurability.)} The sample-to-law map defined below is Borel measurable.
\end{itemize}
For an observed sample \(\omega:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to O_{d_x,d_z}\) with empirical five-block summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), the repaired estimator is the total map
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\varnothing,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\varnothing .
\end{cases}
\]

4ba01fd9fae256d2e4d4b17a4ae36dac31d6da5a.title: Ordered weight estimator
4ba01fd9fae256d2e4d4b17a4ae36dac31d6da5a.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and set
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\qquad
\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}.
\]
A repair input \(R\) consists of \(0<k\), \(0\le L_\tau\), a continuous map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]),
\]
a measurable selector \(\Pi\) from observable summaries to observable summaries, and the following repair properties: \(\overline F\) agrees with the model quotient law on every admissible model summary; when \(\mathcal K\ne\emptyset\), \(\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K\) and minimizes \(d_S(q,s)\) over \(q\in\mathcal K\); when \(\mathcal K=\emptyset\), \(\Pi(s)=0\); and the resulting repaired quotient-law estimator is measurable.

For an observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), define
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\emptyset,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\emptyset.
\end{cases}
\]
Let \(\xi(\omega)\) be the representative atomic law selected from the quotient class \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\), with labelled weights \(\xi_w(i)\) and labelled atoms \(\xi_\tau(i)\) for \(i\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\). The ordered-weight estimator is the function
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega):\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\to\mathbb R
\]
defined by
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)(j)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\,\ell:\xi_\tau(\ell)<\xi_\tau(i)\,\}=j
\right\}\xi_w(i),
&
\text{if }\xi_w(i)>0\text{ for every }i
\text{ and }i\mapsto\xi_\tau(i)\text{ is injective},\\[1.2em]
1/k, & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

3a1193fd8f620389bbbecdd9e968fa1209f91341.title: Path stratum membership
3a1193fd8f620389bbbecdd9e968fa1209f91341.body:
For real numbers \(g\) and \(h\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} The path displacement satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}, with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M\) as specified by \cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}, its smallest positive effect gap \(\delta(P_{g,h})\) from \cref{obj:def:effect-gap} satisfies the gap window of \cref{obj:ass:gap-window},
\[
\frac{g}{2}\le \delta(P_{g,h})\le 2g,
\]
and its latent effects from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} are distinct as in \cref{obj:ass:distinct-effects}.

e01abebb0e935f7c6b5e09dd2ec6fe0bbc982a7a.title: Atomic law coordinates
e01abebb0e935f7c6b5e09dd2ec6fe0bbc982a7a.body:
For \(k\in\mathbb N\) and radius parameter \(L_\tau\in\mathbb R\), the represented atomic-law class
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
is the labelled coordinate space whose element \(\xi\) consists of two real coordinate vectors,
\[
\xi=\bigl((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k}\bigr),
\qquad
w_i\in\mathbb R,\quad a_i\in\mathbb R .
\]
The abbreviation \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) denotes the same represented space. The associated measure on \(\mathbb R\) is
\[
\nu_\xi=\sum_{i<k} \max\{w_i,0\}\,\delta_{a_i},
\]
so coincident labelled locations contribute additively at that location. The topology on this represented space is induced by the coordinate map
\[
\xi\mapsto \bigl((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k}\bigr),
\]
and its measurable structure is the pullback of the measurable structure on the two real coordinate vectors under the same map.

52499a3df37fe850973e535d60b01fa5f2e2f89e.title: Attaining KR potential

d328fc720c3c1a72daa6dcb31401b6946dbfa26f.title: Latent-arm weight injectivity

f663124a88169886dead83c67ca7f1ad3976cd40.title: Moore--Penrose product cancellation
f663124a88169886dead83c67ca7f1ad3976cd40.body:
Let \(C\in\mathbb R^{\mathrm{rows}\times r}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{\mathrm{cols}\times r}\), and \(\mu\in\mathbb R^r\). Suppose that the linear maps represented by \(C\) and by \(B\), each with domain \(\mathbb R^r\), are injective. Then
\[
(CB^\top)^\dagger\bigl(C\operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top\bigr)
=
(B^\dagger)^\top \operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top .
\]

08c286645dc57b59036e2d40e3c2564f4bf3c3b3.title: Outcome proxy moment factorization
08c286645dc57b59036e2d40e3c2564f4bf3c3b3.body:
Let \(P\), a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), belong to the model class \(\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\). Suppose that \(2\le k\) and that the latent-arm positivity margin satisfies \(\pi_0>0\). Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
N_t(P)
=
A_t\,\Gamma_t\,\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}:1\le u\le k\}\,B^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma_t
=
\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\}.
\]
Here \(N_t(P)\) is the observable armwise \(YZX^\top\) population moment in \(\cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}\), \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix in \(\cref{obj:def:reference-feature}\), \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix in \(\cref{obj:def:target-feature}\), and \(\mu_{tu}\) is the latent conditional potential-outcome mean in \(\cref{obj:def:latent-mean}\).

092396b671333e05c9f26f2c894f1160c9fcfa8d.title: Summary metric continuity
092396b671333e05c9f26f2c894f1160c9fcfa8d.body:
For fixed target- and reference-proxy dimensions \(d_x,d_z\), let \(d_S\) be the summary metric on observable moment summaries from \(\cref{obj:def:observable-summary}\). The map
\[
(s,q)\longmapsto d_S(s,q)
\]
from the product of the five-block summary space with itself to \(\mathbb R\) is continuous.

96a16b237481be6621fe49bb70e2bc0ed99e83ad.title: Coordinate metric comparison
96a16b237481be6621fe49bb70e2bc0ed99e83ad.body:
Let \(d_x\) and \(d_z\) be fixed target- and reference-proxy dimensions, and let \(s,s'\) be elements of the five-block observable summary space in \cref{obj:def:observable-summary}. Equip this space with its coordinate Euclidean distance \(\rho_{\mathrm{sum}}\). Then
\[
d_S(s,s')
\le
\bigl(4\operatorname{Ent}_{d_z,d_x}+d_x\bigr)\rho_{\mathrm{sum}}(s,s'),
\]
where
\[
\operatorname{Ent}_{r,c}
:=
c\,r\,\|J_c\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and \(J_c:\mathbb R^c\to(\{1,\ldots,c\}\to\mathbb R)\) is the canonical coordinate identification.

8c692da326d52d78dc7a0d50ad238dccf0736d18.title: Stacked proxy signal margin
8c692da326d52d78dc7a0d50ad238dccf0736d18.body:
Let \(P\), a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), belong to the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\le d_x\), where \(k\) is the number of latent classes and \(d_x\) is the target-proxy dimension.
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(\pi_0>0\) and \(\sigma_0>0\), with the latent-arm positivity and proxy-rank margin conditions in \(\cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}\).
\end{itemize}
Then the vertically stacked observable proxy moment satisfies
\[
\pi_0\sigma_0^2
\le
\sigma_{k-1}\!\left\{\operatorname{stack}\bigl(M_0(P),M_1(P)\bigr)\right\},
\]
where \(\sigma_{k-1}\) uses zero-based singular-value indexing and \(M_0(P),M_1(P)\) are the armwise \(ZX^\top\) population moments from \(\cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}\).

3f5eb5e28c1e3f36bb25fe174d9a9fe86a3117a5.title: Compressed spectral certificate
3f5eb5e28c1e3f36bb25fe174d9a9fe86a3117a5.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(Q\in\mathcal M\) be a model law as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with observable summary \(S(Q)\) as in \cref{obj:def:observable-summary}.  Then there exist a signal basis \(V\) for \(S(Q)\) and a real diagonalization of the compressed effect operator \(\Delta Q(Q)\) from \cref{obj:def:compressed-operator} such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(V\) spans the signal row space of \(S(Q)\).
\item For each arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the compressed map
\[
x\longmapsto M_t(S(Q))Vx
\]
is injective, where \(M_t\) is the observable armwise \(ZX^\top\) moment from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}.
\item With \(G=\operatorname{stack}(M_0(S(Q)),M_1(S(Q)))\), one has
\[
\operatorname{rank}(G)=k.
\]
\item For every index \(j\),
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j(G)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j<k.
\]
\item The eigenvalues of the diagonalization are exactly the latent-class treatment effects \(\tau_u(Q)\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect}.
\item The left spectral anchor \(a(Q)^\top\) has coordinates given by the latent-class masses \(p_u(Q)\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-mass}, and the right spectral anchor \(c(Q)\) is carried to \(\mathbf 1_k\).
\end{enumerate}

d622cdda4bc0c2dd0f06a90463af97cc4fedcaf8.title: Attaining KR potential
d622cdda4bc0c2dd0f06a90463af97cc4fedcaf8.body:
Let \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) be represented atomic laws, with finite labelled slots, whose weights are nonnegative and sum to one and whose atoms lie in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\).  Let \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) be the Kantorovich--Rubinstein potential selected for the pair \((\nu,\xi)\).  Then \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) is one-Lipschitz, is normalized by
\[
\varphi_{\nu,\xi}(0)=0,
\]
and attains the Wasserstein distance of \(\cref{obj:def:wasserstein-distance}\):
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
=
\left|
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\xi
\right|.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), if every one-Lipschitz function \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) with \(\varphi(0)=0\) satisfies
\[
\left|
  \int \varphi\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi\,d\xi
\right|
\le \epsilon,
\]
then
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)\le \epsilon.
\]

2427f60100385b9f58fe5fc4fa090e5a46ec72f9.title: Matrix continuous linear map
2427f60100385b9f58fe5fc4fa090e5a46ec72f9.body:
For natural numbers \(r\) and \(c\) and any real \(r\times c\) matrix \(A\), \(\operatorname{matrixCLM}(A)\) is the continuous linear map from \(\mathbb R^c\) to \(\mathbb R^r\) induced by the usual Euclidean matrix action of \(A\):
\[
\operatorname{matrixCLM}(A)
=
\operatorname{toContinuousLinearMap}\bigl(\operatorname{toEuclideanLin}(A)\bigr).
\]

6bc7f86430d7694166bd40164ade836956187774.title: Calibrated path displacement
6bc7f86430d7694166bd40164ade836956187774.body:
For \(a,g\in\mathbb R\) and \(n\in\mathbb N\), define
\[
\operatorname{calibratedDisplacement}(a,n,g)
=
a\,\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}.
\]

57d45b49adae9ce7475eb794db6eef9d39555a5f.title: Stacked proxy signal margin
57d45b49adae9ce7475eb794db6eef9d39555a5f.body:
Let \(P\), a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), belong to the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\le d_x\), where \(k\) is the number of latent classes and \(d_x\) is the target-proxy dimension.
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge 1\), with the bounded target-proxy condition in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}.
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(\pi_0>0\) and \(\sigma_0>0\), with the latent-arm positivity and proxy-rank margin conditions in \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}
Then the vertically stacked observable proxy moment satisfies
\[
\pi_0\sigma_0^2
\le
\sigma_{k-1}\!\left\{\operatorname{stack}\bigl(M_0(P),M_1(P)\bigr)\right\},
\]
where \(\sigma_{k-1}\) uses zero-based singular-value indexing and \(M_0(P),M_1(P)\) are the armwise \(ZX^\top\) population moments from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}.

816bc17c7eff6cb4b778ff6118149cd2622bc798.title: Attaining transport potential
816bc17c7eff6cb4b778ff6118149cd2622bc798.body:
Let \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) be valid represented atomic laws on \(\mathbb R\) with finite labelled slot sets: their labelled weights are nonnegative and each labelled weight vector sums to one.  Let \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) be the Kantorovich--Rubinstein potential selected for the pair \((\nu,\xi)\).  Then \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) is one-Lipschitz, is normalized by
\[
\varphi_{\nu,\xi}(0)=0,
\]
and attains the minimum transport cost \(W_1(\nu,\xi)\) of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-distance}:
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
=
\left|
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\xi
\right|.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), if every one-Lipschitz function \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) with \(\varphi(0)=0\) satisfies
\[
\left|
  \int \varphi\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi\,d\xi
\right|
\le \epsilon,
\]
then
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)\le \epsilon.
\]

bfa9fbf6c19608055979ccb262eb821c71e05771.title: Outcome proxy moment factorization
bfa9fbf6c19608055979ccb262eb821c71e05771.body:
Let \(P\), a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), belong to the model class \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent classes.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Positivity margin.)} The latent-arm positivity margin satisfies \(\pi_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model conditions.)} The reference- and target-proxy separation, consistency, latent ignorability, latent-arm positivity, bounded outcome-proxy product, and bounded target-proxy conditions in \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:latent-ignorability,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-x} hold.
\end{itemize}
Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
N_t(P)
=
A_t\,\Gamma_t\,\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}:1\le u\le k\}\,B^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma_t
=
\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\}.
\]
Here \(N_t(P)\) is the observable armwise \(YZX^\top\) population moment in \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}, \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix in \cref{obj:def:reference-feature}, \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix in \cref{obj:def:target-feature}, and \(\mu_{tu}\) is the latent conditional potential-outcome mean in \cref{obj:def:latent-mean}.

37cac42d79b8e94edfcafff482196cd4c15b6066.title: Ordered weight estimator
37cac42d79b8e94edfcafff482196cd4c15b6066.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Let
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0
\]
be the effect-support radius, and let \(\mathcal K\) be the closure of the admissible summary image.  A repair datum \(R\) consists of \(0<k\), \(0\le L_\tau\), a continuous map \(\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), and a measurable selector \(\Pi\) on summary space such that \(\overline F\) agrees with the model quotient law on admissible model summaries, \(\Pi(s)\) is a nearest point of \(\mathcal K\) to \(s\) when \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty, \(\Pi(s)=0\) when \(\mathcal K\) is empty, and the resulting repaired quotient-law map is measurable.

For an observed sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), define
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\emptyset,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\emptyset.
\end{cases}
\]
Choose the quotient representative used by the construction and write its labelled atoms as \((w_i,\tau_i)_{i=1}^k\).  The ordered-weight estimator is the vector \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)\in\mathbb R^k\) with coordinates
\[
\widehat p_{n,j}^{\uparrow}(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k
\mathbf 1\!\left\{\#\{\ell:\tau_\ell<\tau_i\}=j-1\right\}w_i,
& \text{if }w_i>0\text{ for every }i\text{ and the }\tau_i\text{ are pairwise distinct},\\[1.2em]
1/k, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad j=1,\ldots,k .
\]
Equivalently, \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) is the total map \(O_{d_x,d_z}^n\to\mathbb R^k\) obtained by applying this ordering rule to the representative of the repaired quotient law \(\widehat\nu_n\).

1d057d74ab9bffb524e6638d84b5eef9ef10170a.title: Compressed spectral certificate
1d057d74ab9bffb524e6638d84b5eef9ef10170a.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(Q\) be a full-data model law in \(\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, satisfying the anchor, proxy-rank-margin, and latent-arm-positivity conditions in \cref{obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}.  Write \(S(Q)\) for its observable summary as in \cref{obj:def:observable-summary}.  Then there exist a signal basis \(V\) for \(S(Q)\) and a real diagonalization of the compressed effect operator \(\Delta Q(Q)\) from \cref{obj:def:compressed-operator} such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(V\) spans the signal row space of \(S(Q)\).
\item For each arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the compressed map
\[
x\longmapsto M_t(S(Q))Vx
\]
is injective, where \(M_t\) is the observable armwise \(ZX^\top\) moment from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}.
\item With \(G=\operatorname{stack}(M_0(S(Q)),M_1(S(Q)))\), one has
\[
\operatorname{rank}(G)=k.
\]
\item For every index \(j\),
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j(G)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j<k.
\]
\item The eigenvalue vector of the diagonalization is the latent-effect vector \((\tau_u(Q))_u\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect}.
\item Writing \(R^{-1}\) for the inverse diagonalizing basis matrix, the left and right spectral anchors satisfy
\[
a(Q)^\top=p(Q)^\top R^{-1},
\qquad
R^{-1}c(Q)=\mathbf 1_k,
\]
where \(p(Q)=(p_u(Q))_u\) is the latent-mass vector from \cref{obj:def:latent-mass}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

069c1ca0c9cad19c73b87967f78594d303899ad6.title: Attaining KR potential
069c1ca0c9cad19c73b87967f78594d303899ad6.body:
Let \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) be valid represented atomic laws with finite labelled slot sets: their weights are nonnegative and sum to one.  Let \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) be the cumulative-distribution-gap sign Kantorovich--Rubinstein potential selected for the pair \((\nu,\xi)\).  Then \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) is one-Lipschitz, is normalized by
\[
\varphi_{\nu,\xi}(0)=0,
\]
and attains the Wasserstein distance of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-distance}:
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
=
\left|
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\xi
\right|.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), if every one-Lipschitz function \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\varphi(0)=0\) obeys
\[
\left|
  \int \varphi\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi\,d\xi
\right|
\le \epsilon,
\]
then
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)\le \epsilon.
\]

a87115c8f1712f843fef47a138d6d9711c09b86a.title: Ordered labelled weights
a87115c8f1712f843fef47a138d6d9711c09b86a.body:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), let \(R\) be summary-repair data consisting of \(0<k\), \(0\le L_\tau\), a continuous extension \(\overline F\) on
\[
\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S},
\]
a measurable selector \(\Pi\), the model-extension identity for \(\overline F\), the nearest-summary property of \(\Pi\) on nonempty \(\mathcal K\), the zero fallback for \(\Pi\) when \(\mathcal K=\emptyset\), and measurability of the repaired quotient-law map below.  Given an observed sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\) with \(O_i\in O_{d_x,d_z}\), define
\[
\widetilde\nu_R(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\emptyset,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\emptyset.
\end{cases}
\]
Let \(\xi_R(\omega)\) be the chosen finite labelled representative of \(\widetilde\nu_R(\omega)\), with labelled masses and locations \((w_i(\omega),\tau_i(\omega))_{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}}\).  The ordered labelled-weight estimator is the vector \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)\in\mathbb R^k\) whose \(j\)th coordinate is
\[
\widehat p_{n,j}^{\uparrow}(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\ell:\tau_\ell(\omega)<\tau_i(\omega)\}=j-1
\right\}w_i(\omega),
&
\text{if } w_i(\omega)>0 \text{ for all }i
\text{ and } i\mapsto \tau_i(\omega) \text{ is injective},\\[1.1em]
1/k, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

4e802b12e10fc4fdd4149ac1afefb1f1e1f43263.title: Ordered weight estimator
4e802b12e10fc4fdd4149ac1afefb1f1e1f43263.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(R\) be summary-repair data at these parameters. Thus \(R\) supplies \(0<k\), \(0\le L_\tau\) with \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), a continuous extension \(\overline F\) on \(\mathcal K\), and a Borel nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\) with the prescribed empty-closure fallback and measurable repaired-law map. For an observed sample \(\omega:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to O_{d_x,d_z}\), define the repaired quotient law
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\varnothing,\\
\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))), & \mathcal K\ne\varnothing,
\end{cases}
\]
where in the second case \(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\in\mathcal K\). Choose the quotient representative
\[
\xi(\omega)=\bigl((w_i(\omega))_{i<k},(\tau_i(\omega))_{i<k}\bigr)
\]
of \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\). The ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)\in\mathbb R^k\) is the vector whose \(j\)th coordinate, for \(j=0,\ldots,k-1\), is
\[
\widehat p_{n,j}^{\uparrow}(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i<k}
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\ell<k:\tau_\ell(\omega)<\tau_i(\omega)\}=j
\right\}w_i(\omega),
&
\text{if }w_i(\omega)>0\text{ for every }i<k
\text{ and }i\mapsto\tau_i(\omega)\text{ is injective},\\[1.2em]
1/k, & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]
Equivalently, \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) is the map
\[
\omega\longmapsto
\operatorname{orderedMasses}\!\left(
\operatorname{representative}(\widehat\nu_n(\omega))
\right).
\]

2e0964fe3463ec527c30991514ee0efac9d42a3f.title: Representative quotient law
2e0964fe3463ec527c30991514ee0efac9d42a3f.body:
For \(k\in\mathbb N\), radius \(r\in\mathbb R\), and an extensional atomic law \(\nu\) in the quotient \(\operatorname{LawModulo}(k,r)\) of valid labelled laws by equality of their induced measures, define the noncomputable representative
\[
\operatorname{representative}(\nu)
:=
\operatorname{Quotient.out}(\nu)
\in \operatorname{ProbabilityLaw}(k,r),
\]
where \(\operatorname{ProbabilityLaw}(k,r)\) is the subtype of valid at-most-\(k\) atomic laws supported in the radius-\(r\) interval. The topology on \(\operatorname{LawModulo}(k,r)\) is the topology coinduced by the quotient map from \(\operatorname{ProbabilityLaw}(k,r)\), the measurable space is the mapped measurable space along the same quotient map, and \(\operatorname{LawModulo}(k,r)\) is compact in this coinduced topology.

68db8bf78504fe4b9767742f9cc686014e3609d2.title: Diagonalization condition number
68db8bf78504fe4b9767742f9cc686014e3609d2.body:
Work under the notation and conventions of \cref{obj:def:observed-record-space,obj:def:target-feature,obj:def:latent-effect,obj:def:compressed-operator,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin,obj:lem:summary-metric-coordinate-comparison,obj:lem:moore-penrose-product-cancellation}.  Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(d_x\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Signal factorization.)} The target-proxy feature matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) admits a thin signal factorization \(B=V\Upsilon\), where \(V^\top V=I_k\) and \(\Upsilon\) is invertible.
\item \textbf{(Latent effects.)} \(\tau\in\mathbb R^k\) is a vector of latent-class treatment effects.
\item \textbf{(Entry bounds.)} For constants \(L\ge 0\) and \(\sigma_0>0\),
\[
|B_{iu}|\le L,
\qquad
|(\Upsilon^{-1})_{ru}|\le \sigma_0^{-1}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
K_{\mathrm{forw}}
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\sigma_0^{-1}
+
\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}
+\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\]
\[
K_{\mathrm{back}}
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}(d_xL)
+
\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}
+\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\]
and
\[
\kappa_\star
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}^{\,2}K_{\mathrm{forw}}K_{\mathrm{back}},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Ent}_{r,c}\) is the entrywise-to-operator norm constant from \cref{obj:lem:summary-metric-coordinate-comparison}.  Set
\[
\mathcal A
:=
V(\Upsilon^{-1})^\top V^\top+(I_{d_x}-VV^\top),
\qquad
\mathcal A^{-1}
=
V\Upsilon^\top V^\top+(I_{d_x}-VV^\top).
\]
Then
\[
\|\mathcal A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_{\mathrm{forw}},
\qquad
\|\mathcal A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_{\mathrm{back}}.
\]
Moreover, for any orthonormal extension \((u_j)_{j=1}^{d_x}\) of the columns of \(V\), the real diagonalization of
\[
(B^\dagger)^\top\operatorname{diag}(\tau)B^\top
\]
whose eigenbasis matrix \(R\) has columns \(\mathcal A u_j\) satisfies
\[
\|R\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,\|R^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa_\star .
\]

a5b65697c8c53493246b179ec0f862c3257d684a.title: Diagonalization condition bound
a5b65697c8c53493246b179ec0f862c3257d684a.body:
Let \(d_x\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 1\).  Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\), and let \(F\) be a thin signal factorization of \(B\), written \(B=V\Upsilon\), with coordinate inverse \(\Upsilon^{-1}\).  Let \(\tau\in\mathbb R^k\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Feature bound.)} There is a constant \(L\ge 0\) such that \(|B_{iu}|\le L\) for every row \(i\) and latent index \(u\).
\item \textbf{(Coordinate-inverse bound.)} There is a constant \(\sigma_0>0\) such that \(|(\Upsilon^{-1})_{ru}|\le \sigma_0^{-1}\) for every pair of coordinate indices \(r,u\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
K_{\mathrm{forw}}
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\sigma_0^{-1}
+
\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}
+
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\]
\[
K_{\mathrm{back}}
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}(d_xL)
+
\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}
+
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\]
and
\[
\kappa_\star
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}^{\,2}K_{\mathrm{forw}}K_{\mathrm{back}},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Ent}_{r,c}\) is the entrywise-to-operator norm constant of \cref{obj:lem:summary-metric-coordinate-comparison}.  Then the real diagonalization associated with \(F\) and \(\tau\) has condition number at most \(\kappa_\star\).

1baa4f73467af94b9e5110f49bed3515f164720e.title: Matrix action operator
1baa4f73467af94b9e5110f49bed3515f164720e.body:
For \(r,c\in\mathbb N\) and any real \(r\times c\) matrix \(A\), the associated continuous linear operator from \(\mathbb R^c\) to \(\mathbb R^r\) is the ordinary finite-dimensional matrix action:
\[
x\longmapsto Ax .
\]

18153a0897bd039ee7e4f97105e4d10528aeefa2.title: Quotient atomic law structure
18153a0897bd039ee7e4f97105e4d10528aeefa2.body:
For every \(k\in\mathbb N\) and \(r\in\mathbb R\), consider the quotient of valid labelled at-most-\(k\)-atomic probability laws supported in the radius-\(r\) interval by equality of their induced measures.  For a quotient law \(
u\) in this space, \(\operatorname{representative}(
u)\) is the noncomputably chosen valid labelled representative of the equivalence class \(
u\).

The topology on this quotient space is the topology coinduced by the canonical quotient map from valid labelled laws to their induced-measure equivalence classes.  Its measurable structure is the mapped measurable structure along the same quotient map.  With this coinduced topology, the quotient space is compact.

842ad4583b3890e8dc110cc10f45176604c9c10e.title: Ordered weight estimator
842ad4583b3890e8dc110cc10f45176604c9c10e.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), and a repair datum \(R\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\), with effect radius \(L_\tau\) from \(\cref{obj:def:effect-radius}\). For an observed sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\) in the sample space of \(\cref{obj:def:observed-record-space}\), let \(\xi_n(\omega)\) be the labelled atomic representative selected from the repaired quotient law \(\widehat\nu_n=\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\) constructed by \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\). Thus \(\xi_n(\omega)\) has labelled weights \(a_i(\omega)\) and labelled atom locations \(t_i(\omega)\), \(1\le i\le k\).

The ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)=(\widehat p_{1,n}^{\uparrow}(\omega),\ldots,\widehat p_{k,n}^{\uparrow}(\omega))\) is the vector in \(\mathbb R^k\) defined by
\[
\widehat p_{\ell,n}^{\uparrow}(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k a_i(\omega)\,
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{r: t_r(\omega)<t_i(\omega)\}=\ell-1
\right\},
&
\text{if } a_i(\omega)>0 \text{ for every }i
\text{ and } i\mapsto t_i(\omega)\text{ is injective},\\[1.2em]
1/k,
&
\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]
Equivalently, \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) is the map
\[
\omega\longmapsto
\operatorname{orderedMasses}\!\left(\xi_n(\omega)\right),
\]
where the first branch orders the \(k\) labelled atoms increasingly by location and records their labelled masses, and the fallback branch is the uniform vector \((1/k,\ldots,1/k)\).

16d50ad2dc6c10bbf0b4772707ba7a2376a0d345.title: Structured lattice program
16d50ad2dc6c10bbf0b4772707ba7a2376a0d345.body:
For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), let \(L_\tau\), the effect-support radius, be as in \(\cref{obj:def:effect-radius}\). A structured-lattice estimator \(A\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) is prescribed when there are a finite candidate cardinality \(N\), a candidate enumeration
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),\qquad i\in\{1,\ldots,N\},
\]
