of structured lattice points with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\), and, for every sample \(\omega=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), a selected index \(i_\omega\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Well-formed exhaustive list.)} Each \(\vartheta_i\) is well formed for the parameters \((n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), and every well-formed structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\) with effect-support radius \(L_\tau\) appears in the list through an index \(i\) satisfying
\[
V_i=V,\qquad R_i=R,\qquad p_i=p,\qquad \tau_i=\tau .
\]
\item \textbf{(No duplicates.)} If two listed candidates agree in all four displayed coordinates,
\[
V_i=V_j,\qquad R_i=R_j,\qquad p_i=p_j,\qquad \tau_i=\tau_j,
\]
then \(i=j\).
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} The index order agrees exactly with the lexicographic order on candidates:
\[
i\le j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\vartheta_i\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\vartheta_j .
\]
\item \textbf{(First minimizer.)} For the empirical five-block summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-summary-primitives}\), define
\[
J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n(\omega))
=
\left\|
\operatorname{CLM}\!\left(
\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta)
-
\operatorname{Op}_{\mathrm{emp}}\!\left(\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2},\widehat S_n(\omega)\right)
\right)
\right\|
+
\left(
\sum_{a=1}^{d_x}
\left[
\sum_{u=1}^k V_{a u}\sum_{v=1}^k R_{v u}p_v
-\widehat m_{X,n,a}(\omega)
\right]^2
\right)^{1/2}
+
\left(
\sum_{u=1}^k
\left[
\sum_{v=1}^k R_{u v}\sum_{a=1}^{d_x}V_{a v}e_{1,a}
-1
\right]^2
\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The selected index \(i_\omega\) satisfies
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
\le
J_n(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\qquad\text{for every }i,
\]
and ties are resolved by the first lexicographic index:
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
=
J_n(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
i_\omega\le i .
\]
\item \textbf{(Returned law.)} The estimator returns the atomic effect law attached to the selected candidate:
\[
\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)=\lambda_{\vartheta_{i_\omega}} .
\]
\end{itemize}

ee58013cd9fac79b87d95a54fb4058aa10c2aea2.title: Ordered masses are representative-invariant
ee58013cd9fac79b87d95a54fb4058aa10c2aea2.body:
Fix \(k\in\mathbb N\) and a real support radius.  Let \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) be valid labelled atomic representatives with \(k\) slots in the corresponding compact interval, as in \cref{obj:def:atomic-law-class}.  If \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) represent the same aggregated probability measure, then their ordered-mass vectors coincide:
\[
\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\nu)=\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi).
\]

6d06922a900034007c150aa2f1469d97d88a2f68.title: Compact summary closure
6d06922a900034007c150aa2f1469d97d88a2f68.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Let \(\mathscr S:=S(\mathcal M)\) and \(\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}\) be the admissible summary image and its summary-space closure from \(\cref{obj:def:summary-closure}\), for the model class \(\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\). For summaries \(s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\) and \(q=(M_0',M_1',N_0',N_1',m_X')\), use the summary metric from \(\cref{obj:def:observable-summary}\),
\[
d_S(s,q)
=
\|M_0-M_0'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|M_1-M_1'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|N_0-N_0'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|N_1-N_1'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\Bigl(\sum_i (m_X(i)-m_X'(i))^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Boundedness radius.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy-rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists \(B\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
d_S(s,0)\le B
\qquad
\text{for every }s\in\mathscr S.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal K\) is compact, and
\[
\mathcal K\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\ne\varnothing .
\]

a0a5377184f7212a6d48ada9ea92d8924950ff53.title: Diagonalization condition bound
a0a5377184f7212a6d48ada9ea92d8924950ff53.body:
Let \(d_x\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 1\).  Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\), and let \(F\) be a thin signal factorization of \(B\), written \(B=V\Upsilon\), with coordinate inverse \(\Upsilon^{-1}\).  Let \(\tau\in\mathbb R^k\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Feature bound.)} For a constant \(L\ge 0\) as in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}, \(|B_{iu}|\le L\) for every row \(i\) and latent index \(u\).
\item \textbf{(Coordinate-inverse bound.)} For a constant \(\sigma_0>0\) as in \cref{obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}, \(|(\Upsilon^{-1})_{ru}|\le \sigma_0^{-1}\) for every pair of coordinate indices \(r,u\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
K_{\mathrm{forw}}
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\sigma_0^{-1}
+
\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}
+
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\]
\[
K_{\mathrm{back}}
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}(d_xL)
+
\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}
+
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\]
and
\[
\kappa_\star
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}^{\,2}K_{\mathrm{forw}}K_{\mathrm{back}},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Ent}_{r,c}\) is the entrywise-to-operator norm constant of \cref{obj:lem:summary-metric-coordinate-comparison}.  Then the real diagonalization associated with \(F\) and \(\tau\) has condition number at most \(\kappa_\star\).

7c758f70989e19833acdff0f8e8d1048ed8841d3.title: Summary radius \(r_{n,\alpha}\)
7c758f70989e19833acdff0f8e8d1048ed8841d3.body:
For sample size \(n\), miscoverage level \(\alpha\), concentration constant \(C_0\), and envelope constant \(L\), the simultaneous summary radius is
\[
r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]
This is the radius used in the event \(E_P=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\}\).

38004c1a38535eb4f1e3124565e1384c6a23710e.title: Structured comparison operator
38004c1a38535eb4f1e3124565e1384c6a23710e.body:
For a structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\), define the structured comparison operator by
\[
\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta):=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top .
\]
For an empirical summary \(s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\) and threshold \(s_0/2=\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\), define the empirical comparison operator by
\[
\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(s):=M_{1,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}N_1-M_{0,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}N_0,
\]
where \(M_{t,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}\) is the singular-value-thresholded pseudoinverse retaining singular directions with singular value at least \(s_0/2\). In the lattice criterion, these operators are compared through
\[
\|\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta)-\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(\widehat S_n)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

b6d0bffff48e9aae6e9ca013c2299f279d3aff15.title: Atomic measure \(\nu_\xi\)
b6d0bffff48e9aae6e9ca013c2299f279d3aff15.body:
For a represented atomic record \(\xi=((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k})\), define
\[
\nu_\xi=\sum_{i<k}\max\{w_i,0\}\,\delta_{a_i}.
\]
Repeated labelled locations contribute additively through the nonnegative masses \(\max\{w_i,0\}\).

19fa506098786835b51d51a27961cbda3d109351.title: Candidate count \(N_A\)
19fa506098786835b51d51a27961cbda3d109351.body:
For a prescribed structured-lattice estimator \(A\), let
\[
N_A\in\mathbb N
\]
be the cardinality of its finite exhaustive candidate list. The listed candidates are indexed as
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,N_A,
\]
and this enumeration is the duplicate-free lexicographically ordered list of all well-formed structured lattice points at the stated sample size, conditioning constants, and effect-support radius.

7c28e2276029a370b0995547216593a8787d691c.title: Matrix operator norm \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\)
7c28e2276029a370b0995547216593a8787d691c.body:
For natural numbers \(r\) and \(c\) and a real \(r\times c\) matrix \(A\), \(A\) acts as the ordinary finite-dimensional linear map
\[
x\mapsto Ax,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^c.
\]
Its Euclidean operator norm is
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup_{\|x\|_2\le 1}\|Ax\|_2.
\]
Thus comparisons of matrix-valued operators use the ordinary matrix operator norm, for example
\[
\|\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta)-\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(\widehat S_n)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

93a54833d6aef397ab2375d60ea3b5b53396d694.title: Ordered weight estimator
93a54833d6aef397ab2375d60ea3b5b53396d694.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and a repair datum \(R\) with \(0<k\), \(0\le 4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), a continuous extension \(\overline F\) on \(\mathcal K\), and a measurable nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\) with its empty-set fallback.  For an observed sample \(\omega\), let \(\xi_n^R(\omega)\) be the labelled representative of the repaired quotient law obtained from \(R\).

The ordered-weight estimator is the map
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow,R}(\omega)
=
\operatorname{orderedMasses}\!\left(\xi_n^R(\omega)\right),
\]
equivalently, writing the labelled weights and atom locations of \(\xi_n^R(\omega)\) as \(a_i(\omega)\) and \(t_i(\omega)\), \(1\le i\le k\),
\[
\widehat p_{\ell,n}^{\uparrow,R}(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k a_i(\omega)\,
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{r: t_r(\omega)<t_i(\omega)\}=\ell-1
\right\},
&
\text{if } a_i(\omega)>0 \text{ for every }i
\text{ and } i\mapsto t_i(\omega)\text{ is injective},\\[1.2em]
1/k,
&
\text{otherwise,}
\end{cases}
\]
for \(\ell=1,\ldots,k\).

c842ed59ad22ce1d16b654922576bdcc16ae7712.title: Compact summary closure
c842ed59ad22ce1d16b654922576bdcc16ae7712.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Let \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) be the class of full-data probability laws satisfying the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model restrictions with boundedness radius \(L\), latent-arm positivity margin \(\pi_0\), and proxy-rank margin \(\sigma_0\). Define the admissible summary image and its closure by
\[
\mathscr S:=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\},
\qquad
\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}.
\]
For summaries \(s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\) and \(q=(M_0',M_1',N_0',N_1',m_X')\), write
\[
d_S(s,q)
=
\|M_0-M_0'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|M_1-M_1'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|N_0-N_0'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|N_1-N_1'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\Bigl(\sum_i (m_X(i)-m_X'(i))^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Boundedness radius.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy-rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists \(B\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
d_S(s,0)\le B
\]
for every \(s\in\mathscr S\). Moreover, \(\mathcal K\) is compact, and
\[
\mathcal K\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\ne\varnothing .
\]

6f7f28c855339220b57ce159ed622fe5742bacd4.title: Structured lattice program
6f7f28c855339220b57ce159ed622fe5742bacd4.body:
For integers \(k,d_x,d_z,n\), constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), and \(L_\tau:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), the effect-support radius, a lattice estimator \(A\) with radius \(L_\tau\) is prescribed when there exist a candidate enumeration
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),\qquad i\in\{1,\ldots,A.\operatorname{candidateCount}\},
\]
of structured lattice points with radius \(L_\tau\), and, for every sample \(\omega=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a selected index
\[
i_\omega\in\{1,\ldots,A.\operatorname{candidateCount}\},
\]
such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Well-formed exhaustive list.)} Each listed candidate \(\vartheta_i\) is well formed for the parameters \((n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\). Conversely, every well-formed structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\) with radius \(L_\tau\) appears in the list through some index \(i\) satisfying
\[
V_i=V,\qquad R_i=R,\qquad p_i=p,\qquad \tau_i=\tau .
\]
\item \textbf{(No duplicates.)} If two listed candidates agree in all four displayed coordinates,
\[
V_i=V_j,\qquad R_i=R_j,\qquad p_i=p_j,\qquad \tau_i=\tau_j,
\]
then \(i=j\).
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} The index order agrees exactly with the lexicographic order on structured lattice points:
\[
i\le j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\vartheta_i\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\vartheta_j .
\]
\item \textbf{(First minimizer.)} For the empirical summary \(s=\widehat S_n(\omega)\), the criterion is
\[
J_n(\vartheta;s)
=
\left\|
D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n(s)
\right\|
+
\left(
\sum_{a=1}^{d_x}
\left[
\sum_{u=1}^k V_{a u}\sum_{v=1}^k R_{v u}p_v
-s.m_X(a)
\right]^2
\right)^{1/2}
+
\left(
\sum_{u=1}^k
\left[
\sum_{v=1}^k R_{u v}\sum_{a=1}^{d_x}V_{a v}e_{1,a}
-1
\right]^2
\right)^{1/2},
\]
where the empirical comparison operator uses the threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\). The selected index satisfies
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
\le
J_n(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\qquad\text{for every }i,
\]
and ties are resolved by the first lexicographic index:
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
=
J_n(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
i_\omega\le i .
\]
\item \textbf{(Returned law.)} The estimator returns the atomic effect law attached to the selected candidate:
\[
A.\operatorname{estimate}(\omega)=\lambda_{\vartheta_{i_\omega}} .
\]
\end{itemize}

237b8bc10b2dee94e0f6b5ad8258ac461d5b9cb2.title: Ordered weight estimator
237b8bc10b2dee94e0f6b5ad8258ac461d5b9cb2.body:
Given \(k,d_x,d_z,n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\) and a repair datum \(R\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\), let \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\) be the repaired quotient law returned from the observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) by \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\). Choose the construction's representative
\[
\xi_n(\omega)=\bigl((w_i(\omega))_{i=1}^k,(\tau_i(\omega))_{i=1}^k\bigr)
\]
of \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\). The ordered-weight estimator is the vector
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)_j
:=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\ell:\tau_\ell(\omega)<\tau_i(\omega)\}=j-1
\right\} w_i(\omega),
&
\text{if }w_i(\omega)>0\text{ for every }i
\text{ and the }\tau_i(\omega)\text{ are pairwise distinct},\\[1.2em]
1/k,
&
\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad j=1,\ldots,k .
\]
Equivalently, \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) is the total map \(O_{d_x,d_z}^n\to\mathbb R^k\) obtained by applying this ordered-mass rule to the representative of the repaired quotient law \(\widehat\nu_n\).

00d240fddc61841a1f58c8faa08ffe449fa6e048.title: Structured lattice program
00d240fddc61841a1f58c8faa08ffe449fa6e048.body:

\[

\]
and, for every sample \(\omega=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a selected index
\[
i_\omega\in\{1,\ldots,N_A\},
\]
such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Well-formed exhaustive list.)} Each candidate \(\vartheta_i\) is well formed for the parameters \((n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\). Conversely, every well-formed structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\) with radius \(L_\tau\) appears at some index \(i\) with
\[
V_i=V,\qquad R_i=R,\qquad p_i=p,\qquad \tau_i=\tau .
\]
\item \textbf{(No duplicates.)} If two listed candidates agree in all four displayed coordinates,
\[
V_i=V_j,\qquad R_i=R_j,\qquad p_i=p_j,\qquad \tau_i=\tau_j,
\]
then \(i=j\).
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} The index order agrees exactly with the lexicographic order on structured lattice points:
\[
i\le j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\vartheta_i\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\vartheta_j .
\]
\item \textbf{(First minimizer.)} For the empirical summary \(s=\widehat S_n(\omega)\), the selected index minimizes the criterion \(J_n\) computed with threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\):
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
\le

\qquad\text{for every }i=1,\ldots,N_A .

Ties are resolved by the first lexicographic index:

\end{itemize}

b7015b4afd5e05788e1cdb8ec391d92f8188b465.title: Witness latent masses
b7015b4afd5e05788e1cdb8ec391d92f8188b465.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\) with \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\), let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) be the two-class witness law of \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}.  The latent-class masses \(p_u:=P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(U=u)\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-mass} are
\[
p_1=\frac25,
\qquad
p_2=\frac35 .
\]
Equivalently, these masses are constant in \(\varepsilon\) over this range and are distinct.

d7b0617a56114ec75b022adca54d3f670e86d543.title: Ordered weight estimator
d7b0617a56114ec75b022adca54d3f670e86d543.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and put \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), the effect-support radius.  A repair datum \(R\) supplies \(0<k\), \(0\le L_\tau\), a continuous map \(\overline F:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), and a measurable selector \(\Pi\) from observable summaries to their nearest point in \(\mathcal K\), with the zero-summary fallback when \(\mathcal K=\emptyset\), such that \(\overline F\) agrees with the quotient law on every model summary and the resulting repaired-law map is measurable.

\widehat\nu_n(\omega)

\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\emptyset,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\delta_0\) is the zero atomic law with \(k\) labelled slots at radius \(L_\tau\).  Choose the construction's representative
\[
\xi_n(\omega)=\bigl((w_i(\omega))_{i=1}^k,(\tau_i(\omega))_{i=1}^k\bigr)

of \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\).  The ordered-weight estimator is the total map
\(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:O_{d_x,d_z}^n\to\mathbb R^k\) given, for \(j=1,\ldots,k\), by

\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)_j
=

\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k

\right\} w_i(\omega),
&
\text{if every }w_i(\omega)>0\text{ and the }\tau_i(\omega)\text{ are pairwise distinct},\\[1.2em]
1/k,
&

\]

5dc8c1513071c4bd1878f83e3fd4717c2a57627e.title: Structured lattice program
5dc8c1513071c4bd1878f83e3fd4717c2a57627e.body:

\[
L_\tau:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0,

i_\omega\in\{1,\ldots,N_A\},

such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Well-formed exhaustive list.)} Each listed candidate \(\vartheta_i\) is well formed for the parameters \((n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\). Conversely, every well-formed structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\) at radius \(L_\tau\) appears at some listed index \(i\) with
\[
V_i=V,\qquad R_i=R,\qquad p_i=p,\qquad \tau_i=\tau .
\]
\item \textbf{(No duplicates.)} If two listed candidates agree in all four displayed coordinates,

9e91be3981985f91297d183437f1ffe74e329c0a.title: Ordered weight estimator
9e91be3981985f91297d183437f1ffe74e329c0a.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and put \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), the effect-support radius.  A repair datum \(R\) consists of \(0<k\), \(0\le L_\tau\), a continuous extension \(\overline F\) on \(\mathcal K\), and a measurable nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\) as in \cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}, with \(\overline F\) agreeing with the quotient law on each model summary and with the repaired-law map measurable.

For a sample \(\omega\), let \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\) be the repaired quotient law
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\emptyset,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\emptyset,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\delta_0\) is the zero atomic law with \(k\) labelled slots at radius \(L_\tau\).  Choose the construction's representative
\[
\xi_n(\omega)=\bigl((w_i(\omega))_{i=1}^k,(\tau_i(\omega))_{i=1}^k\bigr)
\]
of \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\).  The ordered-weight estimator associated with \(R\) is the total map
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)_j
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\ell:\tau_\ell(\omega)<\tau_i(\omega)\}=j-1
\right\} w_i(\omega),
&
\text{if every }w_i(\omega)>0\text{ and the }\tau_i(\omega)\text{ are pairwise distinct},\\[1.2em]
1/k,
&
\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
for \(j=1,\ldots,k\).

564074999d360292ae1fe882eebdfa6a4703262c.title: Ordered weight estimator
564074999d360292ae1fe882eebdfa6a4703262c.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and set
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0 .
\]
A repair datum \(R\) consists of \(0<k\), \(0\le L_\tau\), a continuous map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]),
\]
a measurable selector \(\Pi\) on observable summaries, agreement of \(\overline F\) with the quotient law at every model summary, nearest-point selection in \(\mathcal K\) when \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty, fallback \(\Pi(s)=0\) when \(\mathcal K=\emptyset\), and measurability of the repaired-law map below.

For an observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), define
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\emptyset,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\emptyset,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\delta_0\) is the zero atomic law with \(k\) labelled slots and radius \(L_\tau\).  Let
\[
\xi_n(\omega)=\bigl((w_i(\omega))_{i=1}^k,(\tau_i(\omega))_{i=1}^k\bigr)
\]
be the construction's quotient representative of \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\).  The ordered-weight estimator associated with \(R\) is the total map \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:O_{d_x,d_z}^n\to\mathbb R^k\) defined by
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)_j
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\ell:\tau_\ell(\omega)<\tau_i(\omega)\}=j-1
\right\} w_i(\omega),
&
\text{if every }w_i(\omega)>0\text{ and the }\tau_i(\omega)\text{ are pairwise distinct},\\[1.2em]
1/k,
&
\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
for \(j=1,\ldots,k\).

28ea51d48844462ae7a4c78579ff17ece9d73125.title: Ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\)
28ea51d48844462ae7a4c78579ff17ece9d73125.body:
The input is the positive estimated atomic law \(\widehat\nu_n\) on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item Write \(\widehat\nu_n\) uniquely in increasing support order as
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^{\widehat s_n}
\widehat w_{\ell,n}\delta_{\widehat\tau_{\ell,n}},
\qquad
\widehat\tau_{1,n}<\cdots<\widehat\tau_{\widehat s_n,n},
\qquad
\widehat w_{\ell,n}>0 .
\]

\item Output the ordered-weight estimator
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}
=
\begin{cases}
(\widehat w_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat w_{k,n}), & \widehat s_n=k,\\[2mm]
(1/k,\ldots,1/k), & \widehat s_n<k .
\end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}

Ordering the finitely many support points and extracting their jump sizes are Borel operations, so \(\widehat\nu_n\mapsto\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) is a total Borel map into \(\Delta^{k-1}\).

7503215216e2802eceea57fa0670c2ef5eeaf3fc.title: Ordered weight estimator
7503215216e2802eceea57fa0670c2ef5eeaf3fc.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\), \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), and repair data \(R\) carrying the continuous extension \(\overline F\), nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\), fallback law, and measurability certificate specified in \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\). For an observed sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), let \(\widehat\nu_n\) be the repaired quotient law returned by that construction at \(\omega\), and let \(\xi_n=(w_i,\tau_i)_{i=1}^k\) be its chosen labelled representative.

The labelled ordered-weight estimator is the vector
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\left(
\displaystyle\sum_{i:\#\{l:\tau_l<\tau_i\}=0} w_i,\ldots,
\displaystyle\sum_{i:\#\{l:\tau_l<\tau_i\}=k-1} w_i
\right),
&
\text{if } w_i>0 \text{ for every } i \text{ and the } \tau_i\text{ are pairwise distinct},\\[3mm]
(k^{-1},\ldots,k^{-1}),
&
\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]
Equivalently, its \(j\)th coordinate, for \(j=0,\ldots,k-1\), sums the weights of the labelled atoms whose location has exactly \(j\) labelled locations below it, with the uniform vector used in the fallback case.

085325e95ca4b594403af9bd439d68542bfa51ad.title: Compressed spectral certificate
085325e95ca4b594403af9bd439d68542bfa51ad.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(Q\) be a full-data probability law in the uniformly conditioned model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  Write \(S(Q)\) for its observable summary as in \cref{obj:def:observable-summary}, let \(M_t^Q\) denote the \(t\)-arm \(ZX^\top\) moment block of this summary, and set
\[
G:=\operatorname{stack}(M_0^Q,M_1^Q).
\]
Then there exist a signal basis \(V\) and a real diagonalization of the compressed effect operator \(\Delta Q(Q)\) from \cref{obj:def:compressed-operator} such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(V\) spans the signal row space of \(S(Q)\).
\item For each arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the compressed map
\[
x\longmapsto M_t^Q Vx
\]
is injective.
\item The stacked proxy moment has rank
\[
\operatorname{rank}(G)=k.
\]
\item For every index \(j\),
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j(G)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j<k.
\]
\item The eigenvalue vector of the diagonalization is the latent-effect vector \((\tau_u(Q))_u\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect}.
\item Writing \(R^{-1}\) for the inverse diagonalizing basis matrix, the left and right spectral anchors satisfy
\[
a(Q)^\top=p(Q)^\top R^{-1},
\qquad
R^{-1}c(Q)=\mathbf 1_k,
\]
where \(p(Q)=(p_u(Q))_u\) is the latent-mass vector from \cref{obj:def:latent-mass}.
\end{enumerate}

5a231fb571df6a037b421d03d23c075c497fe46d.title: Gap-free modulus extension
5a231fb571df6a037b421d03d23c075c497fe46d.body:
Fix natural numbers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and real constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent dimension.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Bound and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), and let \(\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\) be the summary closure from \(\cref{obj:def:summary-closure}\).  For two summaries
\[
s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X),
\qquad
q=(M'_0,M'_1,N'_0,N'_1,m'_X),
\]
write
\[
d_S(s,q)
=
\|M_0-M'_0\|+\|M_1-M'_1\|
+\|N_0-N'_0\|+\|N_1-N'_1\|
+\Bigl(\sum_i (m_X(i)-m'_X(i))^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
There exists a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) such that, for every pair of full-data laws \(P,Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
W_1(\nu_P,\nu_Q)\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(S(P),S(Q)).
\]
Moreover, there is a map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
such that \(\overline F\) is continuous and Borel measurable,
\[
W_1(\overline F(q),\overline F(q'))
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q')
\qquad\text{for all }q,q'\in\mathcal K,
\]
and
\[
\overline F(S(Q))=\nu_Q
\qquad\text{for every }Q\in\mathcal M.
\]
This map is unique among continuous maps \(G:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) that obey
\[
W_1(G(q),G(q'))
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q')
\qquad\text{for all }q,q'\in\mathcal K
\]
and satisfy \(G(S(Q))=\nu_Q\) for every \(Q\in\mathcal M\): every such \(G\) satisfies \(G(q)=\overline F(q)\) for all \(q\in\mathcal K\).

4e98ea9c93b842ad415c47899e1c7668983326fd.title: Compressed spectral certificate
4e98ea9c93b842ad415c47899e1c7668983326fd.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(Q\) be a full-data probability law in the uniformly conditioned model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with observable summary \(S(Q)\) as in \cref{obj:def:observable-summary}. Assume that \(Q\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}. Let \(M_t(S(Q))\) be the \(t\)-arm \(ZX^\top\) moment block from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}, and set
\[
G:=\operatorname{stack}(M_0(S(Q)),M_1(S(Q))).
\]
Then there exist a signal basis \(V\) spanning the signal row space of \(S(Q)\) and a real diagonalization of the compressed effect operator \(\Delta Q(Q)\) from \cref{obj:def:compressed-operator} such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for each arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the compressed map
\[
x\longmapsto M_t(S(Q))Vx
\]
is injective;
\item the stacked proxy moment has rank
\[
\operatorname{rank}(G)=k;
\]
\item for every index \(j\),
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j(G)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j<k;
\]
\item the eigenvalue vector of the diagonalization is the latent-effect vector \((\tau_u(Q))_u\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect};
\item writing \(R\) for the diagonalizing basis matrix, the left and right spectral anchors satisfy
\[
a(Q)=R^{-\top}p(Q),
\qquad
R^{-1}c(Q)=\mathbf 1_k,
\]
where \(p(Q)=(p_u(Q))_u\) is the latent-mass vector from \cref{obj:def:latent-mass}.
\end{enumerate}

d8b02a317b376ad42219bca5240f8a008364892b.title: Ordered repair weights
d8b02a317b376ad42219bca5240f8a008364892b.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Given the repair handle \(R\) of \(\cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}\), define the ordered-weight estimator as the total map
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}:(O_{d_x,d_z})^n\to\mathbb R^k
\]
that sends an observed sample \(\omega=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\), with \(O_i=(T_i,X_i,Z_i,Y_i)\), to the ordered masses of any representative atomic law of the repaired quotient-law estimate \(\widehat\nu_n(\omega)\).  Concretely, if that representative has labelled weights \(w_i\) and labelled atom locations \(\tau_i\), then for \(j=1,\ldots,k\),
\[
\widehat p_{n,j}^{\uparrow}(\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{i=1}^k
\mathbf 1\!\left\{
\#\{\ell:\tau_\ell<\tau_i\}=j-1
\right\}w_i,
&
\text{if }w_i>0\text{ for every }i\text{ and }i\mapsto\tau_i\text{ is injective},\\[3mm]
1/k,
&
\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

groups.title: Vertical matrix stacking
groups.body: For matrices \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times d}\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{s\times d}\) with the same number of columns, define \(\operatorname{stack}(A,B)\in\mathbb R^{(r+s)\times d}\) by vertical concatenation,\[\operatorname{stack}(A,B):=\begin{bmatrix}A\\ B\end{bmatrix}.\] Its row space is regarded as a subspace of \(\mathbb R^d\).

groups.title: Ordered aggregate mass map
groups.body:
For a labelled representative \(\xi=\sum_{i=1}^k w_i\delta_{x_i}\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), define \(\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi)\in\mathbb R^k\) as follows. If every labelled weight is positive and the labelled atoms are distinct, then its \(j\)th coordinate is the mass of the atom whose support rank is \(j\):
\[
\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi)_j
:=\sum_{i=1}^k w_i\mathbf 1\!\left\{\#\{\ell:x_\ell<x_i\}=j\right\},
\qquad j=0,\ldots,k-1.
\]
If some labelled weight is zero or two labelled atoms coincide, set \(\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi):=(1/k,\ldots,1/k)\).

groups.title: Ambient summary space
groups.body:
For fixed proxy dimensions \(d_x\) and \(d_z\), the ambient five-block observable-summary space is
\[
\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}
:=
(\mathbb R^{d_z\times d_x})^4\times\mathbb R^{d_x}.
\]
A point \(s\in\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\) is written \(s=(s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,s_5)\), with four matrix blocks and one target-proxy mean block, and the summary metric is
\[
d_S(s,s'):=\sum_{j=1}^{4}\|s_j-s'_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|s_5-s'_5\|_2 .
\]
The admissible image \(\mathscr S\) and its closure \(\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\) are subsets of \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\), and the repair selector \(\Pi\) is a total Borel map from \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\) to \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\).

groups.title: Real-weight embedding
groups.body:
For a real number \(w\), define
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}(w):=\max\{w,0\}
\]
as the associated nonnegative extended-real scalar used to weight a positive measure. Thus a represented atomic record \(\xi=((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k})\) induces the measure
\[
\nu_\xi=\sum_{i<k}\operatorname{ofReal}(w_i)\,\delta_{a_i},
\]
with repeated labelled locations contributing additively through their embedded nonnegative weights.

groups.title: Structured-lattice candidate count
groups.body:
For a prescribed structured-lattice estimator \(A\), the integer
\[
A.\mathrm{candidateCount}\in\mathbb N
\]
is the cardinality of its finite exhaustive candidate enumeration. The listed candidates are indexed as
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,A.\mathrm{candidateCount},
\]
and this enumeration is the duplicate-free lexicographically ordered list of all well-formed structured lattice points at the stated sample size, conditioning constants, and effect-support radius.

groups.title: Structured lattice candidate spaces
groups.body: Put \(m_\star:=\pi_0\), \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\), \[H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,\qquad q_n:=H_n^{-1},\] and \(\ell_n:=\lceil m_\star H_n\rceil\). Let \(\mathcal V_n\) consist of the polar factors \(G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}\) of all \(G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k}\) satisfying \(|G_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sigma_k(G)\ge1/2\). Let \(\mathcal R_n\) consist of all \(R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}\) satisfying \(\sigma_k(R)\ge\sigma_0/2\) and \(\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt{k}L\). Define \[\mathcal P_n:=\left\{H_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:a_u\in\{\ell_n,\ldots,H_n\},\ \sum_{u=1}^k a_u=H_n\right\},\] and let \(\mathcal T_n\) be the \(k\)-fold product of the clipped \(q_n\)-lattice in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\).

groups.title: Thresholded empirical compressed operator
groups.body: For a rectangular matrix \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define the thresholded pseudoinverse \[G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top.\] The empirical compressed operator is \[\widehat D_n:=(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}-(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.\]

groups.title: Lattice-implied operator and quotient law
groups.body: For \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\), define \[D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,\qquad m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,\qquad b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,\] and define the associated quotient law by \[\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^k p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.\]

groups.title: Euclidean matrix action as a continuous linear map
groups.body: For natural numbers \(r\) and \(c\) and a real \(r\times c\) matrix \(A\), let \(\operatorname{toEuclideanLin}(A):\mathbb R^c\to\mathbb R^r\) denote the linear map given by the usual Euclidean matrix action, \(x\mapsto Ax\). For any linear map \(L:\mathbb R^c\to\mathbb R^r\), let \(\operatorname{toContinuousLinearMap}(L)\) denote the same map bundled as a continuous linear map between finite-dimensional Euclidean normed spaces. Thus \(\operatorname{matrixCLM}(A):=\operatorname{toContinuousLinearMap}(\operatorname{toEuclideanLin}(A))\).

groups.title: Structured-lattice objective $J_n(\vartheta;s)$
groups.body:
Put $s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2$. For a summary $s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\in(\mathbb R^{d_z\times d_x})^4\times\mathbb R^{d_x}$, define the thresholded pseudoinverse by writing a rectangular matrix $G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top$ and setting $G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top$. Set $\widehat D(s):=M_1^\dagger{}_{\ge s_0/2}N_1-M_0^\dagger{}_{\ge s_0/2}N_0$. For $\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n$, with $V\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}$, $R\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}$ invertible on $\mathcal R_n$, $p\in\Delta^{k-1}$, and $\tau\in[-L_\tau,L_\tau]^k$, define $D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top$, $m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p$, $b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1$, and $\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^kp_u\delta_{\tau_u}$. The structured-lattice criterion at summary $s$ is 
\[
J_n(\vartheta;s):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D(s)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}+\lVert m_\vartheta-m_X\rVert_2+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2.
\]
For the empirical summary $\widehat S_n$, write $J_n(\vartheta):=J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)$.

synth_1.title: Ambient Euclidean dimension
synth_1.body: Let \(d\in\mathbb N\) denote the finite ambient dimension of a Euclidean summary space \(\mathbb R^d\). In the nearest-summary selection statement, \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a compact feasible set and \(d_S:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is the continuous summary distance used to choose nearest feasible summaries.

synth_6.title: Kullback--Leibler divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}$
synth_6.body:
For probability laws $\mu$ and $
u$ on the same measurable space, define $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|
u):=\int \log(d\mu/d
u)\,d\mu$ when $\mu\ll
u$, and set $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|
u):=+\infty$ when $\mu
ot\ll
u$. In the local experiments this divergence is applied to one-record observed-data margins such as $P_O$ and $(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O$.

synth_7.title: All-ones vector $\mathbf 1_k$
synth_7.body: The vector $\mathbf 1_k\in\mathbb R^k$ is the all-ones vector, with coordinate $(\mathbf 1_k)_u=1$ for every latent-coordinate index $u=1,\ldots,k$.

synth_8.title: Thresholded armwise Moore--Penrose inverse
synth_8.body: Let \(s=(M_0(s),M_1(s),N_0(s),N_1(s),m_X(s))\) be an observable summary and put \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\). For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), write a real singular-value expansion \(M_t(s)=\sum_j \sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), with \(\sigma_j\ge0\). The thresholded Moore--Penrose inverse of the armwise proxy moment is\[ (M_t(s))^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top.\]

synth_9.title: Operation count for the structured-lattice estimator
synth_9.body: For the structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\), let \(\mathcal A_n:=\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\) denote its lexicographically ordered finite candidate list. In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost exact-real model, define\[\operatorname{ops}(\widehat\lambda_n):=n+\#\mathcal A_n.\]The term \(n\) counts formation of the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), and \(\#\mathcal A_n\) counts exhaustive evaluation of the fixed-dimensional objective \(J_n(\vartheta)\) once for each \(\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n\), including the fixed-size arithmetic, comparison, singular-value, polar-decomposition, and root-isolation operations used by that candidate evaluation.

synth_10.title: Finite transport-plan relation
synth_10.body: Let \(\nu=\sum_{a=1}^r w_a\delta_{x_a}\) and \(\widehat\lambda_n=\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\widehat w_b\delta_{\widehat x_b}\) be finite probability laws on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\). We write \(\gamma:\nu\leadsto\widehat\lambda_n\) when \(\gamma=(\gamma_{ab})_{1\le a\le r,\,1\le b\le\widehat r}\) is a finite transport plan with \(\gamma_{ab}\ge0\), \(\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}=w_a\) for every \(a\), and \(\sum_{a=1}^{r}\gamma_{ab}=\widehat w_b\) for every \(b\). Its absolute-distance transport cost is \(\sum_{a=1}^{r}\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\).

synth_11.title: Published VMW structural model
synth_11.body: Fix \(k,d_x,d_z\) with \(0<k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\). A one-unit full-data probability law \(P\) belongs to the published VMW structural model when it satisfies the published qualitative proxy model conditions: reference-proxy separation \(Z\perp (X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), target-proxy separation \(X\perp (Y,T)\mid U\), consistency \(Y=Y(T)\) almost surely, armwise latent ignorability \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\) for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), full column rank of \(A_0\), \(A_1\), and \(B\), and strict latent-arm positivity \(P(U=u,T=t)>0\) for every \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).

synth_12.title: Published VMW finite-regularity condition
synth_12.body: A law \(P\) satisfies the published VMW finite-regularity condition when \(0<k\), \(k\le d_x\), \(k\le d_z\), and there exist constants \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{YZX},\pi,\sigma>0\) such that \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le L_X\), \(\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{YZX}\) almost surely, \(P(T=t)\ge\pi\) for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and there is a top-\(k\) right singular basis \(V\) for the stacked proxy moment \([M_0(P);M_1(P)]\) satisfying \(\sigma_k([M_0(P);M_1(P)])\ge\sigma\) and \(\sigma_k(M_t(P)V)\ge\sigma\) for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\).

synth_13.title: Separated recovery regime
synth_13.body:
A full-data law \(P\) lies in the separated recovery regime when it satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} The published VMW structural model conditions.
\item \textbf{(Anchor normalization.)} The first target-proxy coordinate satisfies \(X_1=1\) almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Finite regularity.)} The published VMW finite-regularity condition.
\item \textbf{(Spectral separation.)} The latent-class treatment effects satisfy \(\tau_u\ne\tau_v\) whenever \(u\ne v\).
\end{itemize}
In this regime, the separated-recovery estimator analyzed by \citet{VirkMazaheriWu2026} is evaluated under its stated sample-size and radius conditions and returns simultaneous high-probability bounds for the treatment effects, the anchor-normalized feature matrix, and the simplex-projected mixture weights.

synth_14.title: Factorization-preserving two-class path law $P_{g,h}$
synth_14.body: For $0\le g\le 1/4$ and $|h|\le 1/100$, $P_{g,h}$ is the full-data law on $(U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)$ with $U\in\{1,2\}$, $T\in\{0,1\}$, $X=(1,X_2)^\top$, $Z=(1,Z_2)^\top$, $Y=Y(T)$, latent masses $P_{g,h}(U=1)=2/5+h$ and $P_{g,h}(U=2)=3/5-h$, and latent-arm weights\[\begin{array}{c|cc} & u=1 & u=2\\ \hline P_{g,h}(U=u,T=1) & 4/25+3h/5 & 9/25-3h/5\\ P_{g,h}(U=u,T=0) & 6/25+2h/5 & 6/25-2h/5 .\end{array}\] Thus $P_{g,h}(T=1\mid U=u)=P_{g,h}(U=u,T=1)/P_{g,h}(U=u)$. Conditional on $U$, the variables $T,X_2,Y(0),Y(1)$ are Bernoulli with the displayed treatment probability, with $E_{P_{g,h}}[X_2\mid U=1]=1/5$, $E_{P_{g,h}}[X_2\mid U=2]=(12/25-h/5)/(3/5-h)$, $E_{P_{g,h}}[Y(0)\mid U=u]=1/4$, $E_{P_{g,h}}[Y(1)\mid U=1]=1/2-g/2$, and $E_{P_{g,h}}[Y(1)\mid U=2]=1/2+g/2$. Conditional on $(U,T)$, $Z_2$ is Bernoulli and independent of $(X_2,Y(0),Y(1))$, with\[E_{P_{g,h}}[Z_2\mid U=1,T=1]=\frac{225h+28}{20(15h+4)},\quad E_{P_{g,h}}[Z_2\mid U=2,T=1]=\frac34,\]\[E_{P_{g,h}}[Z_2\mid U=1,T=0]=\frac{35h+9}{10(5h+3)},\quad E_{P_{g,h}}[Z_2\mid U=2,T=0]=\frac7{10}.\] With the induced feature matrices $A_t(h)$ and $B(h)$ and latent-arm weight vector $w_t(h)=(P_{g,h}(U=1,T=t),P_{g,h}(U=2,T=t))$, the path preserves the armwise proxy factorization $A_t(h)\operatorname{diag}(w_t(h))B(h)^\top=A_t(0)\operatorname{diag}(w_t(0))B(0)^\top$ for $t\in\{0,1\}$, and $P_{g,0}=P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}$.

synth_15.title: Kullback--Leibler divergence
synth_15.body:
For probability laws $\mu$ and $
u$ on the same measurable space, the Kullback--Leibler divergence from $
u$ to $\mu$ is
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|
u):=\int \log\!\left( rac{d\mu}{d
u}ight)\,d\mu
\]
when $\mu\ll
u$, and $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|
u):=+\infty$ when $\mu
ot\ll
u$. In the local experiments this divergence is applied to one-record observed-data margins, including $P_O$ and $(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O$.

synth_16.title: Structured-lattice work count
synth_16.body:
For the explicit structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\), let \(\operatorname{Work}_n\) denote the fixed-dimensional exact-real operation count for forming \(\widehat S_n\), enumerating the lexicographically ordered candidate lattice, evaluating the criterion \(J_n\), and returning the first minimizer \(\widehat\vartheta_n\). In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost exact-real model, \(\operatorname{Work}_n\) counts arithmetic, comparison, singular-value, and fixed-degree root-isolation operations and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Work}_n\le C\left\{n+n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\right\},
\]
for a finite constant \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\).

synth_18.title: VMW Assumption 4
synth_18.body:
For a one-unit full-data law \(P\), VMW Assumption 4 holds when \(0<k\), \(k\le d_x\), \(k\le d_z\), and there exist positive constants \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{YZX},\pi,\sigma\) such that \(\|X\|_2\le L_X\), \(\|ZX^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\|YZX^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{YZX}\) almost surely under \(P\), both treatment-arm probabilities satisfy \(P(T=t)\ge\pi\) for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and there is a population top-\(k\) right singular basis \(V\) of the stacked proxy moment \([M_0(P);M_1(P)]\) for which
\[
\sigma_k([M_0(P);M_1(P)])\ge\sigma,
\qquad
\sigma_k(M_t(P)V)\ge\sigma\quad\text{for }t\in\{0,1\}.
\]

synth_19.title: Summary radius \(r_{n,\alpha}\)
synth_19.body:
For sample size \(n\), miscoverage level \(\alpha\), concentration constant \(C_0\), and envelope constant \(L\), the simultaneous summary radius is
\[
r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]
This is the radius used in the event \(E_P=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\}\).

synth_21.title: Endpoint feasibility for cluster-mass extrema
synth_21.body: For confidence-set data with atom floor \(m_\star\), outer radius \(R_{n,\alpha}\), computed center \(\widehat\lambda_n\), association radius \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\), empirical component \(C\), and candidate endpoint value \(m\), say that \(\operatorname{EndpointFeasible}(C,m)\) holds when there exists a law \(\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) and a transport plan \(\gamma\) from \(\xi\) to \(\widehat\lambda_n\) such that \[ \sum_{a,b}\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\le R_{n,\alpha} \] and \[ m=\xi(K_C(\xi)),\qquad K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}. \] Thus the lower and upper endpoints of \(I_C\) are the infimum and supremum of feasible values \(m\) over the same ordered-support, atom-floor, simplex, and transport constraints.

synth_24.title: Structured comparison operator
synth_24.body:
For a structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\), define the structured comparison operator by
\[
\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta):=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top .
\]
For an empirical summary \(s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\) and threshold \(s_0/2=\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\), define the empirical comparison operator by
\[
\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(s):=M_{1,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}N_1-M_{0,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}N_0,
\]
where \(M_{t,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}\) is the singular-value-thresholded pseudoinverse retaining singular directions with singular value at least \(s_0/2\). In the lattice criterion, these operators are compared through
\[
\|\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta)-\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(\widehat S_n)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

synth_25.title: Vertical matrix stacking
synth_25.body: For matrices \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times d}\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{s\times d}\) with the same number of columns, define \(\operatorname{stack}(A,B)\in\mathbb R^{(r+s)\times d}\) by vertical concatenation,\[\operatorname{stack}(A,B):=\begin{bmatrix}A\\ B\end{bmatrix}.\] Its row space is regarded as a subspace of \(\mathbb R^d\).

synth_26.title: Ordered aggregate mass map
synth_26.body:
For a labelled representative \(\xi=\sum_{i=1}^k w_i\delta_{x_i}\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), define \(\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi)\in\mathbb R^k\) as follows. If every labelled weight is positive and the labelled atoms are distinct, then its \(j\)th coordinate is the mass of the atom whose support rank is \(j\):
\[
\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi)_j
:=\sum_{i=1}^k w_i\mathbf 1\!\left\{\#\{\ell:x_\ell<x_i\}=j\right\},
\qquad j=0,\ldots,k-1.
\]
If some labelled weight is zero or two labelled atoms coincide, set \(\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi):=(1/k,\ldots,1/k)\).

synth_27.title: Ambient summary space
synth_27.body:
For fixed proxy dimensions \(d_x\) and \(d_z\), the ambient five-block observable-summary space is
\[
\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}
:=
(\mathbb R^{d_z\times d_x})^4\times\mathbb R^{d_x}.
\]
A point \(s\in\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\) is written \(s=(s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,s_5)\), with four matrix blocks and one target-proxy mean block, and the summary metric is
\[
d_S(s,s'):=\sum_{j=1}^{4}\|s_j-s'_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|s_5-s'_5\|_2 .
\]
The admissible image \(\mathscr S\) and its closure \(\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\) are subsets of \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\), and the repair selector \(\Pi\) is a total Borel map from \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\) to \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\).

synth_28.title: Atomic measure \(\nu_\xi\)
synth_28.body:
For a represented atomic record \(\xi=((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k})\), define
\[
\nu_\xi=\sum_{i<k}\max\{w_i,0\}\,\delta_{a_i}.
\]
Repeated labelled locations contribute additively through the nonnegative masses \(\max\{w_i,0\}\).

synth_29.title: Candidate count \(N_A\)
synth_29.body:
For a prescribed structured-lattice estimator \(A\), let
\[
N_A\in\mathbb N
\]
be the cardinality of its finite exhaustive candidate list. The listed candidates are indexed as
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,N_A,
\]
and this enumeration is the duplicate-free lexicographically ordered list of all well-formed structured lattice points at the stated sample size, conditioning constants, and effect-support radius.

synth_30.title: Matrix action operator
synth_30.body:
For \(r,c\in\mathbb N\) and any real \(r\times c\) matrix \(A\), the associated continuous linear operator from \(\mathbb R^c\) to \(\mathbb R^r\) is the ordinary finite-dimensional matrix action:
\[
x\longmapsto Ax .
\]

synth_31.title: Calibrated path displacement
synth_31.body:
For \(a,g\in\mathbb R\) and \(n\in\mathbb N\), define
\[
\operatorname{calibratedDisplacement}(a,n,g)
=
a\,\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}.
\]

synth_32.title: Structured lattice candidate spaces
synth_32.body: Put \(m_\star:=\pi_0\), \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\), \[H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,\qquad q_n:=H_n^{-1},\] and \(\ell_n:=\lceil m_\star H_n\rceil\). Let \(\mathcal V_n\) consist of the polar factors \(G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}\) of all \(G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k}\) satisfying \(|G_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sigma_k(G)\ge1/2\). Let \(\mathcal R_n\) consist of all \(R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}\) satisfying \(\sigma_k(R)\ge\sigma_0/2\) and \(\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt{k}L\). Define \[\mathcal P_n:=\left\{H_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:a_u\in\{\ell_n,\ldots,H_n\},\ \sum_{u=1}^k a_u=H_n\right\},\] and let \(\mathcal T_n\) be the \(k\)-fold product of the clipped \(q_n\)-lattice in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\).

synth_33.title: Thresholded empirical compressed operator
synth_33.body: For a rectangular matrix \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define the thresholded pseudoinverse \[G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top.\] The empirical compressed operator is \[\widehat D_n:=(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}-(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.\]

synth_34.title: Lattice-implied operator and quotient law
synth_34.body: For \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\), define \[D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,\qquad m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,\qquad b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,\] and define the associated quotient law by \[\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^k p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.\]

synth_35.title: Matrix operator norm \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\)
synth_35.body:
For natural numbers \(r\) and \(c\) and a real \(r\times c\) matrix \(A\), \(A\) acts as the ordinary finite-dimensional linear map
\[
x\mapsto Ax,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^c.
\]
Its Euclidean operator norm is
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup_{\|x\|_2\le 1}\|Ax\|_2.
\]
Thus comparisons of matrix-valued operators use the ordinary matrix operator norm, for example
\[
\|\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta)-\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(\widehat S_n)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

synth_36.title: Quotient atomic law structure
synth_36.body:
For every \(k\in\mathbb N\) and \(r\in\mathbb R\), consider the quotient of valid labelled at-most-\(k\)-atomic probability laws supported in the radius-\(r\) interval by equality of their induced measures.  For a quotient law \(
u\) in this space, \(\operatorname{representative}(
u)\) is the noncomputably chosen valid labelled representative of the equivalence class \(
u\).

The topology on this quotient space is the topology coinduced by the canonical quotient map from valid labelled laws to their induced-measure equivalence classes.  Its measurable structure is the mapped measurable structure along the same quotient map.  With this coinduced topology, the quotient space is compact.

synth_37.title: Structured-lattice objective $J_n(\vartheta;s)$
synth_37.body:
Put $s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2$. For a summary $s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\in(\mathbb R^{d_z\times d_x})^4\times\mathbb R^{d_x}$, define the thresholded pseudoinverse by writing a rectangular matrix $G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top$ and setting $G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top$. Set $\widehat D(s):=M_1^\dagger{}_{\ge s_0/2}N_1-M_0^\dagger{}_{\ge s_0/2}N_0$. For $\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n$, with $V\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}$, $R\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}$ invertible on $\mathcal R_n$, $p\in\Delta^{k-1}$, and $\tau\in[-L_\tau,L_\tau]^k$, define $D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top$, $m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p$, $b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1$, and $\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^kp_u\delta_{\tau_u}$. The structured-lattice criterion at summary $s$ is 
\[
J_n(\vartheta;s):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D(s)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}+\lVert m_\vartheta-m_X\rVert_2+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2.
\]
For the empirical summary $\widehat S_n$, write $J_n(\vartheta):=J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)$.
